# All4one ### 403 working tools. One portable binary. No plugins, no packs, no filler. Every tool gets its own page with its own options — search it, open it, set what you need, run it. ![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-4.0.0-6d8cff?style=flat-square) ![Tools](https://img.shields.io/badge/tools-403-3fb950?style=flat-square) ![Plugins](https://img.shields.io/badge/plugins-0-f85149?style=flat-square) ![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%2010%2F11-0078D4?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-f7c948?style=flat-square) ![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial-blue?style=flat-square) **🌐 [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/All4ONE/)** · **🖼️ [Screenshots](#-what-it-looks-like)** · **📚 [All 403 tools](TOOL_CATALOG.md)** · **⬇️ [Download](https://github.com/drsamonline/All4ONE/releases/latest)**
--- ## What this is A rebuilt utility suite for Windows: file and folder work, text and data, encoding and hashing, images, PDFs, media, documents, network diagnostics, system and disk maintenance, developer helpers, security checks, calculators and generators — in a single executable that needs no installer, writes nothing to the registry, and runs off a USB stick. It is a rewrite, not a reskin. The previous version registered 551 tools across 45 plugin packs behind one dense table; a large share of those were thin adapters with near-duplicate behaviour ("Image Cropper — Crop image.", "Sparse File Inspector — report internals"). That architecture is gone: | | Before (3.x) | Now (4.0) | |---|---|---| | Structure | 45 plugin packs, a Packs tab, enable/disable toggles | One flat catalogue — nothing to enable, nothing to install | | Tools | 551 registered, many trivial or duplicated | 403, each with a real implementation and its own options | | UI | Tkinter, one table + details pane for everything | Qt (PySide6), sidebar navigation, one page per tool | | Options | Free-text argument box | Typed controls generated from each tool's own schema | | Verification | Registry smoke test only | Every runnable tool executed against fixtures on every build | Nothing was kept just to keep the count up. Every tool listed in [TOOL_CATALOG.md](TOOL_CATALOG.md) runs, and the sweep that proves it ships with the repository. ## What it looks like | Home | A tool page | |---|---| | ![Home](docs/screenshots/home-dark.png) | ![Tool page](docs/screenshots/tool-page.png) | | Category listing | Light theme | |---|---| | ![Category](docs/screenshots/category.png) | ![Light](docs/screenshots/home-light.png) | ## How it works **Sidebar.** Home, Favourites, Recently used, then every category with a live count. Dependencies and Settings sit at the bottom; the sun/moon button switches theme. **Search.** `Ctrl+K` from anywhere. Results are ranked on name, category, summary and keywords — typing "split" finds PDF splitting, file splitting and text splitting. **A tool page.** The header carries the tool's name, category, readiness and a star for favourites. On the left, the options: text boxes, dropdowns, numbers, colour pickers, toggles, and file/folder pickers that accept drag-and-drop. On the right, the output console: streaming lines as the tool works, a progress bar when the tool reports progress, and buttons to copy, save or open whatever the tool produced. **Running.** `Ctrl+Enter` runs. Long jobs stream and can be stopped. Tools that change or delete data ask first, and show a red badge on their page. **Readiness, not gatekeeping.** A tool that needs FFmpeg, Tesseract or a Python package is still listed; it says what is missing and how to get it. Nothing is hidden and nothing silently fails. ## Quick start ### The portable build Download `All4one-4.0.0-windows.zip` from [Releases](https://github.com/drsamonline/All4ONE/releases/latest), unzip, run `All4one.exe`. That is the whole installation. ### From source ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/All4ONE.git cd All4ONE pip install PySide6 # only needed for the desktop UI python main.py # desktop app python main.py list # every tool, by category ``` The engine and every standard-library tool run on bare Python — PySide6 is only for the window. ## Command line The same binary is a proper CLI, and every GUI option has an identical flag: ```powershell all4one list # all 403 tools, grouped all4one list --category PDF # one category all4one search hash # ranked search all4one show pdf-merge # options, defaults, readiness all4one run hash-file --file report.pdf --algorithm sha256 all4one run gst-calc --amount 10000 --rate 18 all4one run pdf-extract-pages --file book.pdf --pages "1-3,7" --output ch1.pdf all4one deps # what optional extras are installed ``` Options come from the tool's own field definitions, so the CLI can never drift from the UI. Boolean options are `--flag` / `--no-flag`. ## Optional dependencies The app and 380 of the tools run on the Python standard library alone. The rest declare what they need and light up when it is present: | Needs | Unlocks | |---|---| | Pillow | 26 image tools | | pypdf | 24 PDF tools | | FFmpeg / ffprobe | 20 media tools | | openpyxl · python-docx | 15 document tools | | Tesseract · Poppler | OCR and PDF-to-image | | 7-Zip · LibreOffice · git | archive, office conversion, git tools | | cryptography | file encryption | | pywin32 | the Windows API tools | Run `all4one deps` — or open **Dependencies** in the app — for the exact install line for each one. ## Architecture ```text main.py entry point: no arguments opens the UI, else the CLI core/ tool.py the contract — a tool is a function + a field schema registry.py discovery, validation, ranking, readiness runner.py one execution path for UI and CLI, streaming + cancel deps.py optional dependency probes and install hints cli.py argparse front-end built from the same schemas settings.py one small JSON file: theme, favourites, recents ui/ theme.py design tokens + the whole stylesheet (dark and light) icons.py line icons as inline SVG — no image files to ship widgets.py cards, chips, option editors, the output console pages.py home, category, search, tool page, settings, dependencies window.py sidebar shell, navigation history, search tools/ 16 modules; a tool is ~15 lines plus its options scripts/ catalogue + landing-page generators, release audit tests/sweep.py runs every runnable tool against fixtures docs/index.html the landing page, generated from the registry ``` A tool looks like this, and that is all it takes to appear in the app with a page: ```python @tool(id="gst-calc", name="GST Calculator", category="Numbers", summary="Add or remove GST at any rate, and split CGST/SGST or IGST correctly.", fields=[F.number("amount", "Amount (₹)", 10000.0, minimum=0.0), F.choice("rate", "GST rate", ["5", "12", "18", "28"], "18")]) def gst_calc(v, ctx): ... ``` The UI renders the fields, the CLI turns them into flags, and the catalogue is generated from the same metadata. There is no registration step and no plugin manifest. ## Building the binary ```powershell pip install -r requirements-build.txt python build.py # audit → tests → PyInstaller onefile → zip ``` Output in `dist/`: `All4one.exe` and `All4one--windows.zip`. PyInstaller cannot cross-compile a Windows binary, so the real `.exe` is produced by GitHub Actions on a `windows-latest` runner — every push to `main` builds one, and a `v*` tag publishes it as a release. The Linux job runs the audit and the full tool sweep on every push. ## Verification ```bash python scripts/audit.py # catalogue integrity, versions, hygiene, imports python tests/sweep.py # executes every runnable tool against real fixtures ``` Both are wired into CI and must pass before a build is published. The audit rejects duplicate ids, duplicate summaries, unknown dependency keys, undocumented tools and version drift; the sweep is what stops a tool from quietly becoming decoration. ## Documentation | Document | For | |---|---| | [USER_GUIDE.md](USER_GUIDE.md) | Using the app: search, tool pages, options, output, shortcuts | | [INSTALLATION.md](INSTALLATION.md) | Portable build, from source, optional dependencies, troubleshooting | | [TOOL_CATALOG.md](TOOL_CATALOG.md) | Every tool, its options and what it needs — generated from the registry | | [DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md](DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md) | The tool contract, adding a tool or a category, testing | | [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md) | The build pipeline, CI workflows, releasing | | [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) | What changed in 4.0 and why | | [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) | Reporting, and the safety design | | [docs/index.html](docs/index.html) | The landing page served at drsamonline.github.io/All4ONE | The catalogue and the landing page are generated from the live registry (`scripts/catalogue.py`, `scripts/landing.py`), and the audit fails if either drifts from the code — so the numbers in these pages are the numbers in the app. ## Licence Released under the **PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0** — free for personal and other noncommercial use; commercial use needs a separate licence. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). **Author:** Dr. Sohil Momin, BHMS. Security issues: see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

# BlinkTransfer ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Send a file with light. No internet, no Bluetooth, no cables.** Animated QR codes, **rateless-coded** so a missed frame never breaks the transfer — the receiver only needs *enough* frames, not every one. [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-7c3aed)](LICENSE) [![Commercial licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/commercial-licence%20available-22c55e)](COMMERCIAL.md) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/commits) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/stargazers) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/total)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/releases) [![Top language](https://img.shields.io/github/languages/top/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER) [![PWA: offline-first](https://img.shields.io/badge/PWA-offline--first-6366f1)](https://drsamonline.github.io/BLINKTRANSFER/play/) **[Live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/BLINKTRANSFER/play/)**  ·  **[Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/BLINKTRANSFER/)**  ·  **[All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/)** **Download:** [Windows (.exe)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/releases/latest/download/BLINKTRANSFER-portable.exe)  ·  [Android (.apk)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/releases/latest/download/BLINKTRANSFER.apk)
--- BlinkTransfer moves files between two devices using **only a screen and a camera**. One device shows an animated QR code; the other points its camera at it. Nothing leaves the room — there is no server, no network and no pairing. It is the **universal** member of the optical-transfer family: monochrome QR only, standards-based, and deliberately dependency-light, so it works on the cheapest phones and in the worst light. ## Why it is different - **Rateless (fountain) coding.** Frames are LT-encoded symbols, not an ordered list. Miss one, or twenty, and the transfer still finishes — you just need about *k* good frames out of the loop. This is the feature the previous version promised and did not ship. - **Any-scanner compatibility mode.** A small text file can be sent as a single plain QR that *any* third-party scanner can read — no app needed on the other side. - **Truly offline.** Fully installable PWA; after first load it never touches the network. - **Light on dependencies.** Two small, well-known libraries (`qrcode-generator` to draw, `jsQR` to read) and nothing else at runtime. ## How it works ``` files ─▶ gzip ─▶ split into k blocks ─▶ LT fountain symbols ─▶ QR frames (loop) │ files ◀─ gunzip ◀─ reassemble ◀─ LT belief-propagation decode ◀─ jsQR ◀ camera ``` Each QR carries a 22-byte self-describing header plus one fountain symbol, so the receiver can lock on to **any** frame — there is no header QR to catch first. A header CRC-16 drops mis-read frames; the QR's own Reed-Solomon handles bit errors; a CRC-32 on the whole payload confirms the finished file. ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER.git cd BLINKTRANSFER npm install npm run dev # http://localhost:3000 npm test # run the test suite npm run build # production bundle into docs/play/ ``` Open the dev URL on both devices (or install the PWA). On one, **Send** and pick files; on the other, **Receive** and point the camera. ## Performance Throughput is roughly `frame bytes × frame rate`. Defaults: ~1.4 KB per frame at 12 fps ≈ 17 KB/s, and larger files loop. | What | Note | |------|------| | Per frame | ~1.4 KB (balanced), ~0.8 KB (robust), ~1.8 KB (dense) | | Frame rate | 2–24 fps, your choice | | Limits | 20 MB total per transfer | | Overhead | ~5–15% extra frames for the fountain decoder | Bigger files work, but for anything over a few MB a network would be faster — this is for when there is no network, or when you would rather there were not. ## Compatibility mode Tick **Compatibility mode** to send one small text file (≤ 1.2 KB) as a single plain QR. Any phone camera app will read it — useful for links, addresses, Wi-Fi passwords and quick notes, with no second device running BlinkTransfer. ## Browser support Chrome 80+, Edge 80+, Firefox 114+, Safari 16+. Requires `getUserMedia` (camera), `CompressionStream` (gzip) and — for the sender — the Wake Lock API (optional). `jsQR` and `qrcode-generator` are bundled, so nothing is fetched at runtime. ## Project layout ``` src/ index.html styles.css main.js sw.js lib/ fountain.js LT fountain codes (encoder + belief-propagation decoder) frame.js frame header, presets, CRC codec.js multi-file container + gzip qr.js QR encode (qrcode-generator) / decode (jsQR) utils.js CRC-16/32, PRNG, helpers public/ manifest + icons tests/ node --test suite (fountain, frame, codec, optical loopback) tools/ build.mjs, dev.mjs, serve.js docs/ landing page + built demo (GitHub Pages) ``` ## Testing ```bash npm test ``` The suite includes a full **optical loopback**: files → gzip → fountain frames → rendered QR pixels → jsQR → fountain decode → files, with binary data. No browser required. ## Licence BlinkTransfer is **free for personal, academic, hobby and non-profit use** under the [PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0](LICENSE). **Commercial use needs a paid licence** — see [COMMERCIAL.md](COMMERCIAL.md) for what counts as commercial and how to get one (by email invoice). Third-party components and their licences are listed in [NOTICE](NOTICE). > Note: earlier versions were published under the PolyForm Noncommercial licence. That grant stands > for copies already distributed; this and future versions use the dual model > above. ## Credits Built by **Dr Sohil Momin** ([@drsamonline](https://github.com/drsamonline)). QR rendering by [qrcode-generator](https://github.com/kazuhikoarase/qrcode-generator) (MIT); QR decoding by [jsQR](https://github.com/cozmo/jsQR) (Apache-2.0).

# CLDR — Command Line Dispatch & Route **A single tiny Rust binary that sits in your tray, pops up on a keystroke, and runs whatever you type — a sum, a path, an app, a search.** [![Build & Release](https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR/actions/workflows/build-release.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR/actions/workflows/build-release.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/CLDR?include_prereleases&style=flat-square)](https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR/releases) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20Linux-blue?style=flat-square)](#-download) [![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-Rust-orange?logo=rust&logoColor=white&style=flat-square)](https://www.rust-lang.org/) [![License: MIT + attribution](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT%20%2B%20attribution-yellow?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) ### [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/CLDR/) · [Download the latest release](https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR/releases) · [User guide](docs/USER_GUIDE.md) · [Setup guide](docs/SETUP_GUIDE.md) · [All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/)
--- --- ![CLDR command window](docs/screenshots/01-main.png)
Type anything. CLDR routes it — math, unit conversion, a path, an app, or a web search.
--- ## 📌 What is CLDR? CLDR is a **single-binary command launcher** for Windows and Linux. Bind it to a desktop shortcut or global hotkey; it stays resident in the background and **summons its command window** when you press the key. Type anything — CLDR *routes* it to the right action instantly and shows the result inline. ```text > 2*(3+4)/7 → [CALC] 2*(3+4)/7 = 2 > 10 km in mi → [CALC] 10 km in mi = 6.213712 mi > notes.md → [OK] opened /home/you/notes.md > code → [RUN] spawned `code` (detached) > rust lifetimes → [WEB] browser → https://duckduckgo.com/?q=rust+lifetimes ``` ## ✨ Features | | | |---|---| | 🪟 **Tray-resident, one keystroke** | Lives in the background; the shortcut **summons** the existing window instead of opening a duplicate | | 🧠 **Smart routing cascade** | math → unit conversion → existing path → PATH binary → web search | | 🧮 **Zero-dep calculator** | `+ - * / % ^ ( )` with unary minus, right-associative power, div/mod-by-zero guards | | 📐 **Unit conversion** | `10 km in mi`, `100 f to c`, `5kg to lb` — length, mass, temperature | | 🗂️ **Slash commands** | `/run` `/open` `/ls` `/find` `/web` `/calc` `/sys` `/help` `/clear` | | ⏱️ **Command history** | `↑`/`↓` (or `Ctrl+P`/`Ctrl+N`), persisted between runs | | 📋 **Copy without a clipboard crate** | `Ctrl+Y` copies the last result via OSC 52 — works over SSH | | ⚙️ **Config + aliases** | `~/.config/cldr/config.toml` — search engine, caps, and `alias.g = /web` | | 🩺 **Hardware diagnostics** | `/sys` — cores, OS, hostname, user, no external tools | | 🪶 **Near-idle** | Redraws only on change; idle cost is one `poll()` every 250 ms | | 🔒 **No clipboard, no telemetry, no network daemon** | The only socket is loopback-only, for summon | ## 📥 Download Grab the latest from the [**Releases**](https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR/releases) page. | Platform | Portable | Installer | |---|---|---| | **Windows 10/11 x64** | `cldr-windows-x86_64.zip` — extract & run `cldr.exe` | `cldr--setup.exe` | | **Linux x86_64** | `cldr-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` — extract & run `./cldr` | `./install.sh` | | **Linux ARM64** (Pi 4/5) | `cldr-linux-aarch64.tar.gz` | `./install.sh` | Every release ships a `SHA256SUMS.txt` and SLSA build provenance. ### Portable (no install) ```powershell # Windows Expand-Archive cldr-windows-x86_64.zip -DestinationPath $env:LOCALAPPDATA\cldr & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\cldr\cldr.exe" --summon ``` ```bash # Linux tar -xzf cldr-linux-x86_64.tar.gz ./cldr-linux-x86_64/cldr --summon ``` ### Installer ```powershell # Windows — run the setup, or from a portable folder: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install-shortcut.ps1 ``` ```bash # Linux — installs to ~/.local/bin + menu entry + tray autostart + Super+Alt+C ./install.sh ``` ## 🏁 Build from source ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR && cd CLDR cargo build --release # → target/release/cldr(.exe) cargo test # engine + IPC + extras unit tests cargo run -- --self-test # 14 headless checks (exit 0 = pass) ``` No system libraries, no C toolchain beyond what Rust already needs. ## 🗂️ In-window commands | Command | Description | |---|---| | `/run ` | spawn detached via the OS shell | | `/open ` | open a file/folder in the default viewer | | `/ls [path]` | list a directory (row-capped) | | `/find ` | recursive search (depth-capped) | | `/web ` | search in your default browser | | `/calc ` | arithmetic `+ - * / % ^ ( ) unary-` | | `/sys` | hardware diagnostics | | `/help` · `/clear` | cheat sheet · clear pane | | *(no prefix)* | auto: math → units → path → PATH app → web | ### Keyboard | Key | Action | |---|---| | `Enter` | submit | | `↑` `↓` | history (empty input) / scroll results | | `Ctrl+P` `Ctrl+N` | history prev / next | | `PgUp` `PgDn` `Home` `End` | scroll results | | `Ctrl+Y` | copy last result (OSC 52) | | `Ctrl+L` | clear pane | | `Del` | clear input | | `Esc` / `Ctrl+C` | quit | ![Routing examples](docs/screenshots/02-routing.png) ## ⚙️ Configuration `cldr --config` writes a commented starter file to `~/.config/cldr/config.toml` (Linux) or `%APPDATA%\cldr\config.toml` (Windows). Everything is optional. ```toml # search engine — {q} is replaced by the URL-encoded query search_url = "https://duckduckgo.com/?q={q}" # search_url = "https://www.google.com/search?q={q}" max_results = 50 # /ls and /find row cap find_depth = 4 # /find recursion depth # aliases: "name = replacement"; "name arg" appends arg alias.g = /web alias.gh = /web github.com alias.n = /run nvim ``` ## 🧲 How the tray + summon works ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as User (shortcut / hotkey) participant S as cldr --summon participant I as Loopback IPC (127.0.0.1, ~/.cldr/port) participant W as Running window U->>S: press shortcut S->>I: connect, send "SUMMON" I->>W: accept, reply "OK-WINDOW" W->>W: raise_window() (Win32 / xdotool) S-->>U: exits (no duplicate window) ``` Loopback-only control channel — no clipboard, no privileged APIs, no firewall prompt. A detached daemon (`--daemon-start`) services queued `open`/`run`/`sys` requests from atomically-published per-request files in a private, per-user state directory. ![Help cheat sheet](docs/screenshots/03-help.png) ## 🎯 Design goals | Goal | How | |---|---| | **Small** | 4 crates total (`crossterm`, `ratatui`, `open`, `walkdir`); full LTO, one codegen unit, symbols stripped, `panic=abort` | | **Fast** | Redraw only on change; a single 250 ms `poll()` when idle; no async runtime | | **Dependency-free at runtime** | One binary; nothing to install, no DLLs, no Python | | **Private** | Never reads or writes the clipboard; no telemetry; the only socket is loopback | > **Why a terminal window, not a native GUI?** A native toolkit (winit/egui/Qt) > would add tens of MB of dependencies and binary size. The terminal *is* the > smallest possible GUI here — on Windows the console is auto-shrunk to a > compact ~92×26 box; on Linux your terminal emulator sizes it. ## 🏗️ Project layout ```text src/ ├─ main.rs CLI router (foreground / --summon / --tray / daemon / --self-test) ├─ engine.rs dispatcher, calc parser, smart cascade (+ unit tests) ├─ extras.rs config, aliases, history, unit conversion, base64, self-test ├─ ipc.rs loopback-TCP summon control channel ├─ tui.rs ratatui command window (dirty redraw, history, compact window) ├─ summon.rs window raising, autostart, tray loop └─ daemon.rs detached background worker packaging/ Windows installer (Inno Setup), Linux install/uninstall, portable notes scripts/ shortcut installers (PowerShell + sh) docs/ user guide, setup guide, shortcut recipes, screenshots ``` ## 📚 Documentation | Document | Contents | |---|---| | [docs/USER_GUIDE.md](docs/USER_GUIDE.md) | walkthrough, keys, examples, troubleshooting | | [docs/SETUP_GUIDE.md](docs/SETUP_GUIDE.md) | build, install, shortcuts, autostart, releases | | [docs/SHORTCUTS.md](docs/SHORTCUTS.md) | per-DE / per-tool hotkey recipes | | [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) | version history | | [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) | dev workflow, code style, PR rules | ## 🚀 Releases Releases are **tag-driven** and fully automated: ```bash # bump version in Cargo.toml + CHANGELOG.md, then: git tag v1.3.0 && git push origin v1.3.0 ``` CI builds Windows + Linux (x86_64 and aarch64), packages portable archives and the Windows installer, generates `SHA256SUMS.txt`, attests build provenance, and publishes the GitHub Release. ## ⚖️ License & attribution © **2026 Dr. Sohil Momin ([drsamonline](https://github.com/drsamonline))** — [PolyForm Noncommercial licensed with a mandatory attribution clause](LICENSE). Every source, doc, script, and asset carries an embedded watermark; **any copy must retain the author's name**. Removing watermarks terminates the license grant.

# Holistic Compression Sources (HCS)

Canonical, offline, vendored source vault for the **CHCE** engine
(Chimera Hybrid Compression Engine) and all CHIMERA-family projects
(`heavenzip`, `ziptastic`, `compfactory`).

Every third-party compressor, preprocessor, recompressor, and
entropy-coder reference used by CHCE lives in [`/old`](./old), pinned at a
known-good revision. Consumers pull this repo with `git subtree` and build
from the pinned tree.

**Design constraints (non-negotiable):**

1. **Offline-only.** No neural networks, no model files, no GPU runtimes.
   Context-mixing (CM) compressors like `zpaq`, `paq8px`, `lpaq` are pure
   algorithms — they are **not AI** and are fully offline.
2. **Single source of truth.** No submodules, no nested `.git` directories.
   All sources are vendored flat.
3. **License-audited.** Every source is listed with its license in
   `SOURCES.md` and full text in `LICENSES/`.

---

## Integration Model

| Consumer | How it uses HCS |
|---|---|
| `ziptastic` (native engine) | `git subtree` of `HCS` into `vendor/` |
| `heavenzip` (orchestrator) | Consumes **prebuilt binaries** released by `ziptastic` — does not build from `/old` |
| `compfactory` (workshop) | Full checkout; edits propagate back to HCS via PR |

> **Rule:** `heavenzip` must never contain algorithm code; `ziptastic` must
> never shell out to external executables. HCS exists to feed `ziptastic`.

---

## Repository Layout
HCS/
├── README.md # this file
├── SOURCES.md # machine-readable manifest (id, url, pin, license)
├── LICENSES/ # one .txt per source (full license text)
├── old/ # vendored sources (the vault)
│ ├── xz/
│ ├── zpaq/
│ ├── srep/
│ └── ...
└── (future)
└── chimera/ # optional: CHCE glue code that consumes /old

---

## Source Catalog

Grouped by role in a CHCE pipeline.

### 🧮 Entropy / Final-Stage Coders

| Source | Role | License | Pin |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xz` | LZMA2 reference implementation | 0BSD / LGPL-2.1 | `TBD` |
| `lzma` | LZMA SDK (raw codec) | Public Domain | `TBD` |
| `7z` | 7-Zip SDK — PPMd + LZMA | Public Domain | `TBD` |
| `brotli` | Static dictionary + context-modeled coder | MIT | `TBD` |
| `fse` | FiniteStateEntropy + Huff0 (rANS/Huffman reference) | BSD-3 | `TBD` |
| `ryg_rans` | Minimal rANS reference (Charles Bloom) | Public Domain | `TBD` |

### 🔗 LZ / Match-Finder Backends

## 🏆 The Offline Ratio Ladder

CHCE selects a tier per block based on the joint parser's cost model.
This is the target performance envelope across the sources in `/old`:

| Tier | Backend(s) | Ratio vs xz | Speed vs xz |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Max ratio** | `paq8px` / `LPAQ9` | 0.70–0.80× | 0.001× |
| **High ratio** | `zpaqfranz -m5` / `zpaq` | 0.80–0.85× | 0.01× |
| **Strong** | `bzip3` / `libbsc` / PPMd (`7z`) | 0.90–0.98× | 0.5–2× |
| **Baseline** | `xz` (LZMA2) | 1.00× | 1.00× |
| **Balanced** | `zxc` / `zstd -19` / `brotli -q11` | 1.05–1.15× | 3–10× |
| **Fast** | `density` / `lz4` / `csc` / `lizard` | 1.3–1.5× | 20–50× |
| **Ultra-fast** | `heatshrink` / `brieflz` / `snappy` | 2× | 100×+ |

Plus these orthogonal transforms that operate **before** the entropy tier:

- **Semantic recompression** — `preflate`, `preflate-rs`, `precomp-cpp`,
  `aqueous`, `rhefo` (DEFLATE, JPEG, PNG, PDF, PE, SQLite, ~20 formats)
- **Text tokenization** — `parmar` (+7–9.6 % on LZMA2 over raw text)
- **Numeric bit-transpose** — `bitshuffle`, `pcodec` (2–10× on typed arrays)
- **Short-string coding** — `shoco`, `smaz`
- **Long-range dedup** — `srep` (matches beyond LZMA's 64 MB window)
- **Executable packing** — `upx`, `zelf`

To check that `/old` contains no nested `.git` folders (the most common

```bash

# should print nothing

## Vendored sources and submodules

Most of `old/` is plain vendored source. 23 entries are **git submodules** — they
pin one commit of an upstream repository rather than copying its history, so the
mirror stays a mirror and HCS never claims authorship of code it did not write.

```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/drsamonline/HCS
# or, in an existing clone:
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

**Verify at any time:**

```bash
./scripts/check-vendor.sh          # exit 0 = every source present and mapped
```

### Why the guard exists

Until this was fixed, `old/` carried those 23 gitlinks with **no `.gitmodules`
file at all**. That state is unrecoverable: git records a commit SHA for each
submodule but has nowhere to fetch it from, so `git submodule update --init`
could not work, and every clone — HCS, and every repo that vendors a copy of it —
silently got 23 empty directories. Nothing failed until a build or a benchmark
reached for one of them, and then it looked like a missing source rather than a
broken mirror.

The repair was to add the URL mapping that was always missing (the recorded pins
were all valid — 20 resolve by ref, and the remaining 3 fetch fine by SHA). The
guard is the part that makes it not happen again: `scripts/check-vendor.sh` fails
if any directory under `old/` is empty, if a gitlink has no `.gitmodules` entry,
or if a `.gitmodules` entry points at a directory that does not exist. CI runs it
on every push with `submodules: recursive`, so a mirror that cannot materialise
goes red instead of going quiet.

Write notes in plain natural language — SmartNote uses an LLM to automatically classify them, detect priority, generate a title, and extract dates/times ("tomorrow at 3pm") so nothing slips through the cracks. **🌐 [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/SmartNotes/)**  ·  **▶ [Demo & screens](https://drsamonline.github.io/SmartNotes/#demo)**  ·  **[Source](https://github.com/drsamonline/SmartNotes)**
--- - **License:** PolyForm Noncommercial — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE) - **Version:** 1.0.0 - **Portable apps (planned):** Windows `.exe` + Linux portable builds — design in [docs/PORTABLE_APPS.md](./docs/PORTABLE_APPS.md) ## Features - 🤖 **AI note analysis** — automatic categorization into *Tasks, Deadlines, Schedule, Thoughts, Learning*, priority detection (Low/Medium/High), title generation, and natural-language date/time extraction. - ⏰ **Reminder scheduling** — reminders fire 1 hour before a deadline or scheduled time via a durable heartbeat endpoint (`POST /api/scheduled/process-reminders`). - 🔔 **Multi-channel notifications** — push notifications (Manus owner notification API) and optional email delivery through a provider-neutral webhook. Every delivery attempt is logged as `sent`, `failed`, or `skipped`. - 🔍 **Search & filtering** — full-text search over titles/content, category tabs, "hide completed" toggle, and sorting by date, priority, or category. - 📊 **Dashboard stats** — totals, completed, pending, and overdue counts with per-category summaries and overdue highlighting. - 💾 **Backup & export** — JSON backup export/import, CSV and Markdown exports, and reusable filter presets. - 🎨 **Brutalist design system** — black background, oversized condensed white typography, red divider accents; fully responsive with mobile navigation. ## Tech Stack | Layer | Technology | |-----------|--------------------------------------------------------| | Frontend | React 19, Vite 7, Wouter, TanStack Query, tRPC client | | UI | Tailwind CSS 4, Radix UI (shadcn/ui), Framer Motion, Lucide icons | | Backend | Node.js, Express, tRPC 11 | | Database | MySQL via Drizzle ORM + drizzle-kit migrations | | Auth | Manus OAuth (session cookie `app_session_id`, JWT via `jose`) | | AI | LLM invoked through the platform forge API | | Testing | Vitest | | Packages | pnpm (workspace uses patched `wouter` via `patches/`) | ## Project Structure ``` ├── client/ # React SPA (pages, components, hooks, contexts) │ └── src/ │ ├── pages/ # Home, CategoryView, SearchPage, NotificationHistory, Settings │ ├── components/ # DashboardLayout, NoteFilters, ui/ (shadcn primitives) │ └── contexts/ # ThemeContext ├── server/ # Express + tRPC backend │ ├── _core/ # Framework: trpc, oauth, llm, notification, heartbeat, env │ ├── notes.router.ts # Notes CRUD, search, stats, backup, notification history │ ├── ai.ts # LLM categorization / priority / date-time extraction │ ├── notifications.ts # Reminder processing and delivery logging │ ├── db.ts # Drizzle data access layer │ └── *.test.ts # Vitest suites ├── shared/ # Code shared between client and server ├── drizzle/ # Schema and SQL migrations ├── patches/ # pnpm dependency patches ├── vite.config.ts # Client build config └── vitest.config.ts # Test runner config ``` ## Getting Started ### Prerequisites - Node.js ≥ 20 - pnpm (`packageManager: pnpm@10.4.1`) - A MySQL-compatible database (e.g. TiDB/MySQL 8) ### Installation ```bash pnpm install ``` ### Environment Variables Copy your values into a `.env` file in the project root: | Variable | Required | Description | |-------------------------|----------|----------------------------------------------------| | `DATABASE_URL` | ✅ | MySQL connection string | | `JWT_SECRET` | ✅ | Secret used to sign session cookies | | `OAUTH_SERVER_URL` | ✅ | Manus OAuth server base URL | | `VITE_APP_ID` | ✅ | Application identifier | | `OWNER_OPEN_ID` | | Open ID of the app owner (target of push notices) | | `BUILT_IN_FORGE_API_URL`| | Platform LLM/forge API endpoint | | `BUILT_IN_FORGE_API_KEY`| | Forge API key | | `EMAIL_WEBHOOK_URL` | | Webhook endpoint for outbound email delivery | | `EMAIL_WEBHOOK_API_KEY` | | Optional bearer key for the email webhook | Email delivery is optional: if `EMAIL_WEBHOOK_URL` is not configured, email deliveries are recorded as **skipped** in the notification history rather than failing silently. ### Run ```bash # Development (tsx watch on server + Vite HMR on client) pnpm dev # Type check pnpm check # Tests pnpm test # Production build & start pnpm build pnpm start ``` ### Database Migrations ```bash pnpm db:push # drizzle-kit generate && drizzle-kit migrate ``` ## API Overview All APIs are served under `/api/trpc` (tRPC) plus a few REST endpoints. ### tRPC routers - **`system`** — health/system info. - **`auth.me`**, **`auth.logout`** — session user and cookie logout. - **`notes.*`** (protected unless noted): - `create` — create a note (AI analysis runs automatically) - `list`, `get`, `listByCategory`, `search` - `update`, `updateNote`, `toggleComplete`, `delete` - `stats` — dashboard metrics - `notificationHistory` — recent delivery log - `importBackup` — bulk restore from exported JSON ### REST endpoints - `POST /api/oauth/callback` — OAuth code exchange, sets session cookie. - `POST /api/scheduled/process-reminders` — processes due reminders. Wire this to a durable scheduler (see below). ## Data Model - **users** — Manus OAuth identity (`openId` unique), role, profile. - **notes** — `userId`, `title`, `content`, `category` (enum of the 5 categories), `priority` (Low/Medium/High), `dueDate`, `scheduledDate`, `isCompleted`. Indexed on `(userId, category)`, `(userId, dueDate)`, `(userId, scheduledDate)`. - **reminders** — `noteId` (cascade delete), `reminderTime`, `notificationType` (push/email/both), `isSent`. - **notificationLogs** — per-channel delivery record: `channel` (push/email), `status` (sent/failed/skipped), title, content, error. See `drizzle/schema.ts` for the authoritative definition. ## Production Reminder Setup Reminders are processed by an external durable scheduler calling: ``` POST /api/scheduled/process-reminders ``` After deployment, create a **one-minute Heartbeat job** targeting that endpoint. Failed/skipped-only reminders stay pending and will be retried once the email provider is configured. ## Testing ```bash pnpm test ``` Vitest suites cover AI parsing fallbacks, auth/logout cookie handling, note export/import round-trips, templates, preferences, and reminder delivery (sent/failed/skipped states). ## Known QA Notes - Chromium smoke checks passed at 1280px and 375px (dashboard, category, search, alert history views). - Firefox/Safari checks are recommended post-deployment (not available in the development sandbox). ## 📚 Documentation Set | Document | Purpose | |---|---| | [README.md](./README.md) | This file — overview, setup, usage | | [LICENSE](./LICENSE) | PolyForm Noncommercial license | | [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md) | Release history | | [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) | Development workflow & guidelines | | [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](./docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | System design deep dive | | [docs/API.md](./docs/API.md) | tRPC + REST API reference | | [docs/DATABASE.md](./docs/DATABASE.md) | Schema & migrations | | ⭐ [docs/ENHANCEMENTS.md](./docs/ENHANCEMENTS.md) | **50 non-bloat enhancements backlog** | | ⭐ [docs/PORTABLE_APPS.md](./docs/PORTABLE_APPS.md) | **Windows `.exe` + Linux portable app design (RFC)** | | ⭐ [docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md](./docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md) | **Staged delivery plan (Stages 0–5) with go/no-go gates** | | [todo.md](./todo.md) | Project task tracker | ## 📄 License Distributed under the **PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0** — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE) for details. ---

No framework, no telemetry, no remote code.** TTB (Tiny Toolbox) is a Manifest V3 browser extension that gathers a large collection of small utilities — text, calculations, developer helpers, page tools, data, design, finance, media, security, accessibility and more — into one fast, offline-first interface, instead of a separate tab or extension for every small task. ## Screenshots All images below were captured from the real extension UI in headless Chrome. **Browse the catalog, or filter by category** ![TTB catalog with the category browser](docs/screenshots/01-catalog.png) **Every tool renders the inputs it needs** ![Loan/EMI with its own input fields and a JSON result](docs/screenshots/03-tool-inputs.png) | Rich output | Images render inline | |---|---| | ![Typography scale rendered in the HTML preview](docs/screenshots/04-html-output.png) | ![QR code generated and shown inline with a download link](docs/screenshots/05-image-output.png) | | Real crypto, offline | Destructive tools ask first | |---|---| | ![TOTP code generated from a Base32 secret](docs/screenshots/06-totp.png) | ![History cleaner showing the confirmation tick](docs/screenshots/07-confirm.png) | ## Runs in your browser One source tree, assembled per browser by `npm run build`. Every build carries the full 591-tool catalog; a tool that needs an API a browser does not provide is disabled and **says so plainly** instead of failing silently. | | Chrome / Edge / Brave / Opera / Vivaldi | Firefox | Safari | |---|---|---|---| | Catalog, popup UI, per-tool inputs | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | Page tools, tab tools, crypto, all pure-computation tools | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | Side panel | ✅ `side_panel` | ✅ `sidebar_action` | — | | History · bookmarks · downloads · extension manager · cache clearing · font list | ✅ | ✅ | — not exposed by Safari | | QR / barcode scanning · screen colour picker | ✅ | — | — | | Packaging | Load unpacked | Load temporary add-on, or sign on AMO | Convert with Xcode | Full matrix, including what each browser changes and the exact gaps: **[BROWSER_SUPPORT.md](BROWSER_SUPPORT.md)**. ## What's in it - **591 cataloged tools across 18 categories**, all reachable from the popup or the side panel. - **A real category browser** — pick a category, see its count, then search within it. You don't need to know a tool's name to find it. - **Per-tool inputs.** Multi-field tools (EMI, tax, tip, regex, colour, matrix, image jobs…) render the fields they actually need — encode/decode switches, extra values, and file pickers for media tools. - **Text, HTML and image output.** Rich results (markdown previews, colour palettes, CSS generators, charts, even small games) render in a sandboxed preview; images render inline with a download link. - **Destructive actions are gated.** History/cookie/cache cleaners, duplicate-tab closing and auto-close are dry-run by default and only act after you tick an explicit confirmation. ## How it is built ``` popup.html / sidebar.html ├─ data/tools.js → globalThis.TTB_CATALOG (591 entries) └─ ui/app.js → renders the catalog, builds inputs, runs tools └─ (on first Run) tools/core.js → dispatcher ├─ text · calc · dev · page · system · security (core handlers) ├─ phase4–7 + t-*.js (bundled modules) ├─ tools/compat.js (namespace + capability layer) └─ ui/registry.js (name → handler, inputs) background.js → context menu + keyboard commands only build.mjs + browsers/*.json → per-browser packages (dist/chrome, edge, firefox, safari) lazy/loader.js → optional third-party loader (nothing is downloaded) ``` The catalog is separated from execution, so the tool list renders even if a handler or a privileged API fails. Tool execution is imported on demand. There is **no network layer** in the extension: nothing is fetched, phoned home, or loaded remotely. `tools/compat.js` is the only place that knows about browser differences: it points `chrome` at Firefox's promise-based `browser` namespace and records which APIs actually exist, so handlers can report an honest message on Safari instead of throwing. ## Honest limitations - **Optional third-party libraries are not bundled.** 24 tools (PDF merge/split/rotate, PDF→text, OCR, Excel viewer, Prettier, OpenPGP, QR scanning helpers, axe-core, zxcvbn…) report their required local dependency instead of pretending to run. No remote code is fetched. - **Safari is the most limited target.** It exposes no history, bookmarks, downloads, management, browsingData or fontSettings APIs, so those tools are disabled there. Safari also needs an Xcode conversion step and a signed build. - **Firefox has no side panel** (it uses `sidebar_action`) and no `BarcodeDetector` or `EyeDropper`. - **Some tools are intentionally lightweight.** A few provide guidance, generators or browser-native behaviour rather than the depth of a specialist app. - **Browser tools need the right context.** Tab, history, cookie, bookmark, download and page tools can fail on restricted pages (e.g. `chrome://`, the Web Store, other extensions' pages). - **Recording tools are interactive.** Screen/audio/webcam capture need a permission prompt and keep the popup open for the duration. These limitations are documented deliberately rather than hidden. ## Install **Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi** — download or clone the repository, open `chrome://extensions` (or `edge://extensions`), enable **Developer mode**, choose **Load unpacked**, and select the folder containing `manifest.json`. **Firefox** — build the Firefox package (`npm run build:firefox`), then open `about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox` and **Load Temporary Add-on…** → pick `dist/firefox/manifest.json`. **Safari** — build the Safari package (`npm run build:safari`) and convert it with `xcrun safari-web-extension-converter`, then run the Xcode project. Prebuilt ZIPs for every browser are attached to each successful CI run (Actions → *Validate* → Artifacts). See `INSTALL.md` for details. ## Development No build step beyond picking a manifest, and no framework. Vanilla JavaScript and browser APIs. - `npm test` — smoke test: catalog integrity, dispatcher coverage, registry metadata. - `npm run build` — assembles `dist/chrome`, `dist/edge`, `dist/firefox`, `dist/safari`. - `npm run shots` — regenerates the screenshots above from the real UI in headless Chrome. - CI syntax-checks every module, runs the smoke test, builds all four targets, smoke-tests each package, and uploads the ZIPs. See `INSTALL.md`, `USAGE.md`, `BROWSER_SUPPORT.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `WARNINGS.md` and `AUDIT.md`. ## Privacy and security Local-first: no analytics, no telemetry, no remote code. Privileged tools use the permissions declared in `manifest.json`, and each browser build requests only what that browser can grant. Read `PRIVACY.md` and `SECURITY.md` before deployment, and `WARNINGS.md` for the caveats that matter. ## License PolyForm Noncommercial — see `LICENSE`. ## Author **Dr. Sohil Momin**

Features · build steps · interactive rendering-pipeline walkthrough · get-started · FAQ

---

An experimental C++ browser project built on a Ladybird/SerenityOS-derived codebase.
Minimal by intent · measurable by discipline · honest about provenance.

Quick Start • User Guide • Architecture • Contributing • Security • Changelog

> **Status:** Experimental. Aetheris is not currently a production-ready, standards-complete replacement for established browsers. --- ## 📖 About Aetheris Browser is an experimental C++ browser project built on a codebase derived from the Ladybird and SerenityOS browser ecosystem. The repository contains upstream-derived infrastructure, including components and libraries from that ecosystem, alongside Aetheris-specific experiments and modifications. Aetheris is **not** presented as a browser built entirely from scratch. Its work focuses on adapting, extending, simplifying, and experimentally developing browser subsystems on an existing technical foundation. The Aetheris-specific core today is the dependency-free `AetherisRendering` foundation in [`src/rendering/`](src/rendering) with its regression suite in [`Tests/AetherisRendering/`](Tests/AetherisRendering). See [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full layout of the tree. ## 🎯 Goals - Explore a smaller and more understandable browser architecture where practical. - Improve memory efficiency and startup characteristics through measurable engineering work. - Develop HTML, CSS, DOM, layout, rendering, resource, and document integration incrementally. - Preserve upstream licensing and attribution requirements. - Prefer coherent, testable changes over speculative architectural rewrites. The project aims to be more resource-conscious than typical Chromium- or Electron-based applications where practical and measurable. These are engineering goals, not guaranteed universal metrics. ## 🧬 Upstream foundation and provenance Aetheris contains code and infrastructure derived from the Ladybird/SerenityOS ecosystem. This includes foundational components visible in the repository such as `AK`, `LibCore`, and other imported browser infrastructure. Aetheris-specific code should be distinguished from upstream-derived code during maintenance and review. Existing upstream copyright notices and licenses must not be removed or replaced by project rebranding. See [`docs/UPSTREAM_ATTRIBUTION.md`](docs/UPSTREAM_ATTRIBUTION.md) for the repository-level provenance policy. ## 🏗️ Current architecture ```text HTML input ──► HTML tokenization ──► DOM │ CSS input ───► CSS parsing ──────────┤ ▼ Style resolution │ ▼ Layout ┌────────────┼────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Block Flex Grid │ ▼ Render tree │ ▼ Paint commands │ ▼ Paint execution │ ▼ Software surface ``` The rendering pipeline currently includes work in block and inline layout, Flex and Grid foundations, positioning, sizing constraints, text layout, clipping, paint ordering, backgrounds, images, fonts, and software rasterization. Feature presence does not imply complete HTML or CSS standards compliance. ## ⚙️ Architectural optimization goals ### 🧠 Resource and memory management Aetheris may evaluate standard techniques such as controlled caches, allocation reduction, compressed resource storage, and secure clearing of sensitive memory where justified. LZ4 or similar mechanisms are implementation options rather than proprietary technology claims. ### 🚀 Selective subsystem initialization The project may explore delayed initialization of expensive subsystems, including scripting, when document requirements permit. Dynamic documents and compatibility requirements make this a design problem that must be validated rather than assumed to provide a universal benefit. ### 🎨 Rendering efficiency Current and future work may reduce redundant paint operations, improve clipping and invalidation, and evaluate accelerated backends where the complexity and dependencies are justified. ## 📊 Performance and benchmarking Aetheris does not currently claim fixed limits for binary size, idle memory usage, or startup time. Performance measurements should record the operating system, hardware, compiler, build configuration, enabled features, workload, and measurement method. Future public performance claims should be reproducible. ## 🛠️ Quick start: build and test A typical development workflow is: ```bash cmake -S . -B build cmake --build build --config Debug ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure ``` Reconfiguration is required when CMake configuration or build-registered files change. Otherwise, an existing build directory can be reused. For a dependency-light workflow that skips the upstream tree entirely, use the `Standalone` preset; for a size-first release build, use `StandaloneSize`: ```bash cmake --preset Standalone cmake --build --preset Standalone ctest --preset Standalone cmake --preset StandaloneSize # -Os, gc-sections, LTO, stripped cmake --build --preset StandaloneSize ``` The size profile applies only to the Aetheris targets (`AetherisRendering`, `AetherisRuntime`, `aetheris`); a stripped `aetheris` executable is on the order of 1 MB with the current feature set (HTML/CSS layout, bitmap-font text, PNG/JPEG/GIF/SVG/WebP images, HTTPS/TLS and the HTTP client all linked in). The `aetheris` executable exposes a small headless command surface: ```bash ./aetheris --smoke-test # init all subsystems, bounded frame loop, exit 0 ./aetheris --fetch # fetch a URL over HTTP, print status and size ./aetheris --render [out] # fetch a URL and render it to a PPM image ./aetheris --eval

--- ## Requirements - Windows 10 (build 17763+) or Windows 11 - PowerShell 5.1+ (built in to Windows) - Administrator rights - Run `Compatibility-Check.ps1` first (menu option `9`) to confirm your machine meets these --- ## Quick start 1. Extract the ZIP anywhere. 2. Right-click `scripts\00_Ultimate_Master.bat` → **Run as administrator**. 3. Choose option `9` (Compatibility Check) first. 4. Choose option `S` to create a System Restore point (recommended before your first run). 5. Choose option `M` (Performance Snapshot) and label it `Baseline`. 6. Pick a profile (1-8). 7. Optionally take another snapshot (`M`, label it e.g. `AfterGaming`) and run `R` (Compare Two Snapshots) to see real before/after numbers. 8. If you ever want to revert everything this toolkit changed, choose `U` (Undo All Tracked Changes). --- ## Profiles — what each one actually does differently | Profile | Key tweaks | Notably does NOT do | |---|---|---| | **Daily Home** | Disable telemetry, disable Start Menu ads, disable background apps, balanced visual effects, Balanced power plan | No GPU/priority/memory tweaks | | **Gaming** | GPU hardware scheduling, foreground priority boost, network throttling removed, Game DVR off, High Performance power plan | Not recommended for battery-powered laptops | | **Office** | Background-app + Xbox-service removal, explicit balanced priority separation | No GPU scheduling or priority boost | | **Laptop** | USB selective suspend, **disables** HAGS (saves power on hybrid-GPU laptops), Balanced power plan | Never disables hibernation or memory paging | | **Extreme** | Everything in Gaming + hibernation removed; `DisablePagingExecutive` only if RAM ≥ 16GB; Superfetch disabled only if system drive is confirmed SSD | Desktop only | | **Godlike** | Everything in Extreme + Windows Search indexing disabled + Xbox services disabled. **Requires typing `CONFIRM`** because it trades away Start-menu/file search speed | Desktop enthusiast machines only | | **Server** | Disables Search indexing and Xbox services, removes hibernation, favors background-service CPU priority over foreground apps (opposite of Gaming) | No GPU/gaming tweaks | | **Streaming** | Gaming-profile tweaks + `SystemResponsiveness` lowered so capture/encoding software isn't CPU-starved by the foreground game | - | Full tweak definitions live in `scripts/UWO.psm1` under `Invoke-Tweak` and the profile catalog, which is the **single source of truth** for what each profile does: the profile scripts read their tweak list from it via `Get-ProfileTweak` instead of keeping their own copy, so the table above, `Verify-System.ps1`, and what actually runs can no longer drift apart. Read them before running anything you don't understand. For the `Extreme` and `Godlike` profiles, `DisablePagingExecutive` and `DisableSysMain` are listed in the catalog so that `Verify-System.ps1` can verify them, but the profile scripts strip them from the list they run and re-append them at runtime, gated on RAM >= 16GB and SSD detection respectively — so if your hardware doesn't meet the gate, those tweaks are skipped during the run (and `Verify-System.ps1` will then correctly report them as "Not Applied"). --- ## Utilities - **Compatibility-Check.ps1** — real PASS/FAIL checks (admin rights, OS build, PowerShell version, RAM, disk space, System Restore availability) - **Hardware-Detection.ps1** — real CPU/GPU/RAM/disk/motherboard info via CIM - **Performance-Monitor.ps1** — saves a labeled, real snapshot (CPU load, RAM, disk free, top processes) - **Compare-Results.ps1** — diffs two real snapshots you choose; refuses to run with fewer than 2 snapshots - **Cleanup-System.ps1** — clears temp/cache/Recycle Bin and reports the actual GB freed (measured, not estimated) - **Advanced-Modules.ps1** — runs 8 independent tweaks and reports a real success/fail count - **Verify-System.ps1** — checks current registry/service state against what a chosen profile should have applied - **System-Rollback.ps1** — creates a real Windows System Restore point, or opens System Restore - **Undo-All-Changes.ps1** — reads every backup file this toolkit has written and restores every tracked registry value, service, and hibernation setting to its original state - **Cleanup-Backups.ps1** (menu `P`) — prunes old backup JSON files that would otherwise accumulate forever. Conservative by design: a file is deleted only if it is **both** outside the newest 20 files **and** older than 30 days, and backups that have not been undone yet are never touched unless you pass `-IncludePending`. Use `-WhatIf` to preview, `-KeepCount`/`-MaxAgeDays` to change the thresholds; everything pruned is logged --- ## What's new in v6.2.0 A correctness-and-polish release driven by an independent code audit. The undo guarantee now holds for **services, power plans and hibernation**, not just registry values. - **Undo now restores services and power plans after a re-run.** Previously, re-running a profile recorded the already-tweaked service start mode / power plan as the "original", and those record types were not de-duplicated — so "Undo All" could leave the machine on the tweaked state. `Set-ServiceStateSafe` and the `PowerPlan*` tweaks are now idempotent, and `Select-BackupRecordsToRestore` de-duplicates services (per service), power plans and hibernation as well as registry values, keeping the earliest recorded original. - **`Verify-System.ps1` now reports `DisableNetworkThrottling` correctly.** The value `0xffffffff` reads back as `-1`; the verifier now uses the same normalising comparison as the write path (`Test-RegistryValueMatch`). - **Service backups are written only after the change succeeds**, matching the registry path. - **Hibernation is state-aware.** If hibernation is already off, nothing is changed and nothing is recorded; undo restores the state that was actually captured. - **`EnableUSBSelectiveSuspend` now does what its name says.** The old version wrote `CsEnabled` (the Connected/Modern Standby flag). It now sets the real per-scheme USB selective-suspend setting for the active power plan, and is verified against the active scheme. - **Importing the module no longer creates folders.** Log/backup/snapshot directories are created lazily on first write, so a read-only utility or a `-WhatIf` preview leaves no trace. - **`VisualEffectsBalanced`** now writes `0` ("Let Windows choose" — the actual balanced default) instead of `3` ("Custom"). - **`Compare-Results.ps1`** validates your snapshot selection instead of silently comparing blanks. - **Launcher renamed** to `00_Ultimate_Master.bat` (no version in the filename). See [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md) for the full history. --- ## Safety notes - The previous state of every registry value, Windows service, hibernation setting, and power plan is captured **before** the change and written to a per-run JSON backup file **as soon as the change actually succeeds**. A failed change writes no backup record, so `Undo-All-Changes.ps1` can never try to "restore" something that was never applied. (Services originally in `Boot`/`System` start modes — kernel drivers — cannot be restored via `Set-Service` and are logged with a clear warning instead.) - **Re-running a profile is a no-op for anything that already matches.** Nothing is written and no backup record is added, so a second run cannot record an already-tweaked value as your "original" one. As a second line of defence, undo de-duplicates records across all backup files by their logical target and always restores the *earliest* recorded original. - **Registry keys created by the toolkit are removed again on undo** — but only when the value did not exist beforehand, the key was created by this toolkit, and the key is still empty. A key that something else has since written to is left in place. - `Undo-All-Changes.ps1` supports `-WhatIf` to preview what it would restore without changing anything, and tolerates corrupted/empty backup files without aborting the whole undo run. - Power plans are restored locale-independently: the plan GUID is extracted and stored when it is captured, rather than re-parsed from localized `powercfg` output at undo time. - Backup files are never deleted automatically. Pruning only happens when you run `Cleanup-Backups.ps1` (menu `P`), and by default it leaves every backup that has not been undone yet alone. - The `Godlike` profile requires typed confirmation because it disables Windows Search indexing, which has a real usability cost. - The optional dependency downloader (menu `D`) only opens official vendor download pages — it does not silently run anything, and does not claim to verify file signatures for you. - **No network, no telemetry, no credential access, no persistence.** The toolkit contains no downloader, no `Invoke-Expression`, no scheduled tasks and no security-product changes. --- ## Development The shared engine is the `UWO` module (`scripts/UWO.psm1` + `scripts/UWO.psd1`). Scripts consume it with `Import-Module (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'UWO.psd1')`; `scripts/Common-Functions.ps1` remains only as a shim that imports the module and re-publishes the old `$Global:*` catalog variables, so anything that still dot-sources it keeps working. Tests live in `tests/` and run with Pester 5: ```powershell Install-Module Pester -RequiredVersion 5.7.1 -Scope CurrentUser Invoke-Pester -Path ./tests ``` The registry tests only ever touch `HKCU:\Software\UWO-Test` and are skipped on non-Windows hosts; logs/backups are redirected to a temporary directory via the `UWO_LOG_ROOT` environment variable, so running the suite never touches `%USERPROFILE%\OptimizationLogs`. Lint with `Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -Path . -Recurse -Settings ./PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1`; both run automatically on `windows-latest` under Windows PowerShell 5.1 in CI (see [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml)). --- ## License MIT. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). It ships as **engine only**: a small, generic sample world (four chapters, eight locations, a handful of classes, races, enemies and gear) so you can see it run and then build your own RPG on top. > **The engine is MIT.** The *Aethelgard* games' story, characters and artwork are > a separate work, © Dr. Sohil Momin, all rights reserved — free to play, not > open source, and **not contained in this repository**. See [Licence](#licence). ## ▶️ See it in action This engine powers **Aethelgard: Chronicles of Fate**, a deep single-player RPG. Play it here: **[drsamonline.github.io/aethelgard-games/play/chronicles/](https://drsamonline.github.io/aethelgard-games/play/chronicles/)** Both Aethelgard games live in **[drsamonline/aethelgard-games](https://github.com/drsamonline/aethelgard-games)**. Serve the folder over http (opening `index.html` by double-click will not work in most browsers): ```bash python3 -m http.server 8000 # open http://localhost:8000 ``` No install, no dependencies. # AI Bridge [![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-3f7a52?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) **Your browser's AI, inside VS Code. No API key, no second subscription.**
--- You are already signed in to ChatGPT in Chrome. You already pay for it. AI Bridge attaches to that tab over the Chrome DevTools Protocol and drives it from inside VS Code — reading answers, writing edits into your workspace, and keeping a project state that survives a new chat. It never launches a browser. It never asks for an API key. It uses the tab you opened.

Chat panel — streamed answers, and edits you accept hunk by hunk

## Why it exists - **No API keys.** Nothing to paste, nothing to leak, nothing to bill. - **Your subscription, your session.** It drives the page you already use, with the model you already chose. - **Edits you can refuse.** Every change arrives as a proposal with a diff; untick what you don't want, accept the rest in one undo step. - **It survives the limit.** When ChatGPT says *"you've reached your limit"*, the context moves to Claude or Gemini and the conversation continues.

Providers — health dots, the model list, and any provider you configure yourself
Router — priority, cooldowns, failover, and a preview of the chain it would try

## Install **From a build:** ```bash code --install-extension ai-bridge-0.20.4.vsix ``` **From source:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/ai-bridge.git cd ai-bridge npm install && npm run build && npm run package code --install-extension ai-bridge-0.20.4.vsix ```
## Five steps to first use 1. **Open your browser with the debug port on** — close it first, then: `chrome --remote-debugging-port=9222` 2. **Sign in to ChatGPT** in that window, normally. 3. **Attach:** `Ctrl+Shift+P` → *AI Bridge: Attach Browser*. 4. **Check the dot:** `Ctrl+Shift+P` → *AI Bridge: Adapter Health*. Green means the selectors matched. 5. **Ask something:** `Ctrl+Alt+A` opens the chat panel. Try *"rename oldName to normalise in src/format.ts"*. If a dot is red, the site changed its page — press **AI Bridge: Export Breakage Report** and send that file. It contains no conversation text.
## How it works ``` ┌──────────────┐ loopback WS ┌──────────────┐ CDP ┌────────────────────┐ │ VS Code │◄────────────────►│ Bridge │◄────────►│ your browser tab │ │ extension │ 127.0.0.1 only │ (Node) │ 9222 │ ChatGPT / Claude │ └──────┬───────┘ └──────┬───────┘ └────────────────────┘ │ │ edits, state, adapters, router, settings, panel RAM watchdog ``` - The **bridge** is a separate Node process on loopback. It holds the CDP connection and the adapters. - The **extension** owns everything that touches your workspace: files, diffs, state, settings. - **Adapters** are selector maps — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or one you add in settings. - A **router** picks the provider, honours cooldowns, and fails over carrying only what changed.
## What it does about tokens Measured, not claimed (`docs/compression-bench.md`): | input | tokens | saved | |---|---|---| | polite one-liner | 34 → 21 | ⇣38% | | terse one-liner | 8 → 8 | ⇣0% | | verbose spec paragraph | 113 → 80 | ⇣29% | | pasted stack trace | 83 → 71 | ⇣14% | | code request | 68 → 59 | ⇣13% | | boot prompt | 975 → 974 | ⇣0% | | repo bundle | 588 → 370 | ⇣37% | Compression helps on verbose prose and repo context, and does nothing for terse prompts. The bigger saving is **not sending context that isn't needed**: repo context is attached only when the question names a file, a symbol or a code term, which avoids a 500–900 token bundle on chatty prompts.
## Features | | | |---|---| | **Three providers, plus your own** | ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini out of the box; any other web chat via a selector map in settings | | **Streaming panel** | Virtual-scrolled, first token measured (~471 ms in testing) | | **Reviewable edits** | Diff card with **per-hunk** accept/reject, one `WorkspaceEdit`, sha-verified, drift-refusing | | **Project state** | Gzipped, encrypted, snapshotted; a ≤4k boot prompt restores DOING/TODO in a fresh chat | | **Locked decisions** | "Never do X" is held even in auto mode, with an explicit override flow | | **Compression** | T0 always (protected spans, glossary), T1 opt-in local model, T2 opt-in provider-side | | **Session rotation** | On a usage limit: boot → new page → inject, with an editable preview first | | **Router** | Priority, per-provider cooldowns, exponential backoff + jitter, pre-warm at 80%, free-model preference | | **RAM watchdog** | 3 s poll, 80% evict + GC, 100% block; low-end mode for 8 GB machines | | **Settings** | Six tabs, every field, inline validation, a live preview on each tab | | **Keyboard first** | `Ctrl+Alt+A` chat · `Ctrl+Alt+,` settings · `Ctrl+Alt+R` rotate · `Ctrl+Alt+S` state · `Ctrl+Alt+C` compression |
## What is actually proven This is an experimental project and it would be dishonest to imply otherwise. **Proven** — 600 checks across 20 suites, run on every push: - The bridge, the CDP controller, the watchdog, the router and the state layer. - All three adapters and a fourth custom one, driven end to end **against fixtures**. - Per-hunk edits, the locked-decision guard, drift refusal, one-undo applies. - The boot prompt staying under 4k with every delta present across five failovers. - A deliberately broken fixture failing the contract suite — the suite detects breakage. - The breakage report containing no chat content, checked against known fragments. **Not proven** — and you should know before relying on it: - **Live selectors.** No adapter has run against the real ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Fixtures only. - **The one-hour memory soak.** Three minutes passes flat; an hour needs real hardware. - **T1 and T2 quality.** Built, guarded, tested for safety — never run against a real model. - **Windows.** The code paths exist; only Linux has been exercised.
## Privacy - The bridge listens on `127.0.0.1` only, with a token in `~/.ai-bridge/lock.json` (`0600`). - No telemetry, no analytics, no phone-home. Nothing leaves your machine except the prompts you send to the site you are signed in to. - State is encrypted at rest by default and redacted before it is written. - The breakage report is built from an allow-list: host only (no paths, no conversation ids), selectors tried, and tag/attribute **names**. A guard refuses to write it if any chat text appears.
## Development ```bash npm install npm run build # tsc across shared, bridge, extension npm run test:all # 626 checks, 21 suites npm run test:bench # token-savings report npm run soak # idle memory soak npm run package # bundles and builds the .vsix ``` ## Releasing Releases are automatic and version-gated — pushing code alone publishes nothing. ```bash npm run version:bump patch # or minor / major, or an explicit 1.2.3 git commit -am "release" && git push ``` Every push to `main` publishes **two** things: | release | when | what | |---|---|---| | **Latest build** (pre-release) | every push | a fresh `.vsix` from that commit, replaced each time | | **vX.Y.Z** (latest) | only when the version changes | the tagged, tested release | So there is always a downloadable `.vsix`, and version numbers stay meaningful. `docs/` deploys to GitHub Pages on any change to the landing page. Layout: `shared/` contracts and wire types · `bridge/` the CDP process, adapters, router · `extension/` the VS Code side · `test/` fixtures and suites · `docs/` evidence and the landing page.
## Licence [PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](LICENSE) — free for personal, research, educational, charitable and government use; commercial use requires a separate licence from the author. PolyForm ships several variants (Noncommercial, Small Business, Perimeter, Internal Use Only). This project uses **Noncommercial**; if you intended another, it is a one-file change.
Built by Dr Sohil Momin · Not affiliated with OpenAI, Anthropic or Google

You can also serve the folder with any static host (GitHub Pages, Netlify, `python3 -m http.server`) — that is exactly how the [hosted copy](https://drsamonline.github.io/ambient-sound-studio/play/) above is deployed. > **First click starts audio.** Browsers require a user gesture before playing sound, so press the ▶ button (or a preset) to begin. --- ## 🎛 Using it | Step | What to do | |---|---| | 1 | Tap a **preset** for an instant mood, or **Surprise me** for a random one | | 2 | Raise individual **layer faders** to build your own mix | | 3 | Use **mute** / **solo** to isolate layers, and watch the **meters** | | 4 | Press **▶** to play; the **Sleep** timer and **Pomodoro** are in the dock | | 5 | Open **⋯ (More)** for reverb, binaural beat, breathing, mixer view, sounds, extras and settings | | 6 | **Export** from the download icon | Double-tap any fader to reset it to zero. The bar under the title always shows the current mix and its layers. ### ⌨️ Keyboard shortcuts | Key | Action | |---|---| | Space / K | Play or pause | | M | Mute everything | | R | Surprise me (random mix) | | S | Silence all layers | | B | Breathing guide | | V | Toggle mixer view | | 1–9 | Apply preset 1–9 | | Ctrl/⌘+Z | Undo | | ? | Help | | Esc | Close panels | | ← → ↑ ↓ | Move a layer, when its drag handle has focus | --- ## 🎚 Exporting | Format | Speed | Notes | |---|---|---| | **WAV** 16-bit / 24-bit | Instant | Lossless. A 10-minute stereo file is ~115 MB (16-bit) or ~173 MB (24-bit). | | **Opus** (Ogg) | Fast, not instant | Small and high quality. Needs a **one-time ~230 KB encoder download** (see below), then it is cached and reused offline forever. | Exports are capped at **10 minutes**, peak-normalised, and assembled from several distinct crossfaded tiles so nothing audibly repeats. Playback pauses during the export (optional) and resumes afterwards. > **About the Opus encoder.** The app asks before downloading it, tells you why, and stores it on your device. After that one download it works offline for good. If you decline, or you are offline, the app falls back to the browser's own recorder, or to WAV. --- ## 🎵 Your own sounds **More ⋯ → Add sound files…** turns any audio file into a first-class layer: it gets a card, fader, mute, solo, meter and reverb send, and it is stored on your device and restored on every later visit. Remove one with the small × on its card. This is also the honest answer to "can it ship with recorded samples": every **built-in** layer is synthesised in the browser (no audio files, no network), while recorded audio is whatever **you** add. --- ## 📴 Offline & PWA - **Every built-in sound is generated in the browser** — there are no audio files and no network requests. Open the file with the network switched off and it works completely. - The app ships a full **web app manifest**, maskable icons and an **Install app** button, so it installs to your home screen and opens without browser chrome. - **iOS installs it as-is.** For Chrome/Edge/Android to offer a full install prompt, host the folder and make sure `sw.js` (included in this repo) sits next to `index.html` — the app registers it automatically when served over http(s). --- ## 🔒 Privacy - **No analytics, no telemetry, no accounts, no cloud.** Nothing is ever uploaded. - Everything you create — mixes, custom sounds, the cached encoder — is stored **on your own device**. - The only network request the app can ever make is the **optional, user-confirmed** Opus encoder download. - Microphone access is only requested if you explicitly turn on the microphone layer, and that audio never leaves the page. --- ## 🧩 Zero dependencies - **One HTML file.** HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single document. - **No framework, no build step required, no CDN** for the app itself. - The minified build is **137 KB**; the readable source is 164 KB (the Hindi and Gujarati strings are multi-byte, so the byte count is higher than the character count). - Third-party code is limited to the optional Opus encoder, downloaded at your request and cached locally — see [docs/THIRD-PARTY.md](docs/THIRD-PARTY.md). --- ## 🌐 Browser support | Browser | Playback | WAV export | Opus export | |---|---|---|---| | Chrome / Edge / Brave | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (Ogg) | | Firefox | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (Ogg) | | Safari (macOS / iOS) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (Ogg) — requires the encoder download | | Any browser without Web Audio | ❌ | — | — | Requires the **Web Audio API** (every current browser). The app detects its absence and shows a clear message instead of failing silently. --- ## 📁 Project layout ``` ambient-sound-studio/ ├── index.html ← the app (minified, ready to serve) │ live at drsamonline.github.io/ambient-sound-studio ├── sw.js ← optional service worker for a full PWA install ├── src/ │ └── ambient-sound-studio.src.html ← readable source (edit this one) ├── assets/ ← banner + screenshots used by this README ├── docs/ │ ├── ARCHITECTURE.md ← how the audio engine and app fit together │ ├── BUILD.md ← regenerating the minified build │ ├── FAQ.md ← common questions │ └── THIRD-PARTY.md ← third-party components and licences ├── tools/ │ └── build.js ← the minifier ├── .github/ ← issue templates, PR template, Pages workflow ├── CHANGELOG.md ├── CONTRIBUTING.md ├── CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md ├── SECURITY.md └── LICENSE ``` --- ## 🛠 Development You can edit the app with nothing but a text editor — **`src/ambient-sound-studio.src.html` is the source of truth**, and it runs directly in a browser.
