# Clinical Health Calculator ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **BMI · BMR · TDEE · Macros · Fluids · Body Composition** A single-file, offline-capable clinical calculator for adult outpatients — no build step, no dependencies, no server, no tracking. [![Landing page](https://img.shields.io/badge/Landing_page-open-14b8a6?logo=githubpages&logoColor=white)](https://drsamonline.github.io/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator/) [![All projects](https://img.shields.io/badge/All%20projects-hub-14b8a6?logo=githubpages&logoColor=white)](https://drsamonline.github.io/) [![Live demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Live_demo-open-a3e635?logo=html5&logoColor=white)](https://drsamonline.github.io/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator/play/) [![Source](https://img.shields.io/badge/Source-GitHub-0b1220?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/drsamonline/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-PolyForm_Noncommercial_1.0.0-blue)](LICENSE) [![Dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dependencies-none-success)](https://github.com/drsamonline/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator) [![Offline ready](https://img.shields.io/badge/Offline-ready-success)](https://github.com/drsamonline/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator) [![i18n](https://img.shields.io/badge/i18n-EN_%7C_HI_%7C_GU-orange)](https://github.com/drsamonline/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/drsamonline/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator)](https://github.com/drsamonline/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator/commits/main)
> **Landing page:** https://drsamonline.github.io/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator/  ·  **Live demo:** https://drsamonline.github.io/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator/play/ **Download:** [Windows (.exe)](https://github.com/drsamonline/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator/releases/latest/download/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator-portable.exe)  ·  [Android (.apk)](https://github.com/drsamonline/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator/releases/latest/download/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator.apk) --- ## Author Developed by **Dr. Sohil Momin, BHMS** — Vadodara, Gujarat, India. The original calculator, its clinical design and the choice of formulas are his work. This repository is the maintained, enhanced and minified release of that original code. --- ## What it computes | Area | Outputs | |------|---------| | **Body composition** | BMI with category and gauge, body-fat % (Deurenberg), lean body mass, body surface area (Mosteller), ideal body weight (Devine), adjusted body weight, waist-to-height ratio, waist-to-hip ratio, ideal weight range and target weight | | **Energy** | BMR (Mifflin–St Jeor), TDEE (activity multipliers), calorie targets (maintain / lose / gain) and projected weekly weight change | | **Macros** | Protein, fat, carbohydrate and fiber; protein per meal; macro split (% of calories) | | **Fluids** | Daily fluid requirement (30 mL/kg baseline, adjusted for climate, exercise, fever and breastfeeding), shown in mL / L / glasses | | **Renal** | Creatinine clearance (Cockcroft–Gault) from a serum creatinine, with its formula and limits | | **Dosing** | Weight-based (rate × weight) and surface-area-based (rate × BSA) dose, with the unit shown at every step | | **Risk scores** | CHA₂DS₂-VASc — stroke risk in non-valvular atrial fibrillation, with its source and intended population | | **Risk & flags** | Indian/Asia-Pacific **and** WHO BMI cut-offs; cautions for renal/hepatic disease, heart failure, athletes and paediatric patients | ## Features - **Responsive layout** — a single mobile column on phones, and a two-column desktop view (inputs and saved entries on the left, a sticky results panel on the right) from 960 px up. Larger type and a three-across result grid on big screens. - **Real-time** recalculation as you type. - **Unit conversion that preserves values** — cm / m / ft+in and kg / lbs switch without losing what you entered. - **Saved entries** in `localStorage`, each with an optional patient name/ID and a timestamp; delete with undo, filter, load back into the form, and a **BMI trend chart** across saved entries. - **CSV export and import** (with formula-injection protection) and **print / PDF** output. - **Copy / Share** a formatted text summary of the current result. - **Trilingual UI** — English, हिन्दी and ગુજરાતી. - **Light / dark theme**, respecting the system preference. - **Accessible** — ARIA radiogroups, live result region, keyboard navigation, focus-visible states, hover definitions on every metric, a "What these mean" panel, and a print stylesheet. - **Show the working** — every result lists its formula with your values substituted, in a "Show the working" panel, so it can be checked rather than trusted. - **Fully offline** — self-contained, no external requests; add to home screen on mobile. ## Usage - **Online:** open the [live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator/play/). - **Offline:** download [`index.html`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/drsamonline/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator/main/index.html) and open it in any modern browser. - **On mobile:** open the file/link, then "Add to Home Screen". ## Repository contents | File | Purpose | |------|---------| | `index.html` | Production build — the minified single-file app (this is what GitHub Pages serves). | | `src/clinical-health-calculator.html` | The same app, un-minified and commented, for editing. | | `LICENSE` | PolyForm Noncommercial licence. | To rebuild after editing the source, minify `src/clinical-health-calculator.html` into `index.html` with any HTML minifier. ## Changelog **v2.4.0** - New: **CHA₂DS₂-VASc** — a stroke-risk score for non-valvular atrial fibrillation, shown with its components in the "Show the working" panel and its intended population stated. - Self-tests extended: CHA₂DS₂-VASc age-band checks. **v2.3.0** - New: **dosing** — weight-based (mg/kg × weight) and surface-area-based (mg/m² × BSA) dose, each shown with its formula in the "Show the working" panel. - Self-tests extended: dosing known-value checks. **v2.2.0** - **Show the working** — a panel that lists every result with its formula and the values substituted, so a number can be checked rather than trusted. - New: **creatinine clearance** (Cockcroft–Gault) from an optional serum creatinine, with its formula, units and limits. - Self-tests extended: known-value checks for creatinine clearance plus a units-consistency check (BMI from cm equals BMI from m). **v2.1.0** - Responsive desktop/tablet layout (two-column, sticky results, three-across tiles). - New tools: hip circumference and **waist-to-hip ratio**; **ideal weight range** and **target weight** with the change needed; **protein per meal**; **macro split %**. - New info: hover definitions on every result, a "What these mean" panel. - New: **BMI trend chart** across saved entries; **Copy** and **Share** summary buttons. - Extended CSV export/import with the new fields. **v2.0.0** - Clinical additions: BMI category with Indian/WHO cut-offs, carbohydrates, IBW/adjusted BW/BSA/body-fat/lean mass, waist-to-height ratio, calorie targets with projected change, fluid adjustments, clinical caution flags, disclaimer, adult-only guard. - Data: `localStorage`, patient ID and timestamps, delete/undo, filter, CSV import, print. - Accessibility, trilingual UI, light/dark theme, minified single-file build. ## Formulas & references - **BMR** — Mifflin MD, St Jeor ST, et al. *Am J Clin Nutr* 1990;51:241–7. - **TDEE** — standard activity multipliers (1.2 / 1.375 / 1.55 / 1.725 / 1.9). - **BMI cut-offs** — WHO international and WHO Asia-Pacific / ICMR Indian cut-offs. - **Protein & fiber** — IOM Dietary Reference Intakes; ACSM/NSCA protein range 0.8–2.0 g/kg. - **Fluid** — 30 mL/kg/day adult baseline (EFSA / IOM general guidance). - **Ideal body weight** — Devine BJ. *Drug Intell Clin Pharm* 1974. Adjusted BW = IBW + 0.25 × (actual − IBW). - **BSA** — Mosteller RD. *N Engl J Med* 1987;317:1098. - **Body fat** — Deurenberg P, et al. *Br J Nutr* 1991;65:105–14. - **Waist** — IDF / WHO Asia-Pacific cut-offs (men >90 cm, women >80 cm); waist-to-hip >0.90 (men) / >0.85 (women). - **Creatinine clearance** — Cockcroft DW, Gault MH. *Nephron* 1976;16:31–41. Adults 18+; needs steady-state renal function and a steady-state serum creatinine; not valid in pregnancy or at extremes of body size. - **Show the working** — each result is rendered with its formula and the substituted values; the arithmetic is the app's own, not a lookup. - **Dosing** — weight-based (rate × actual weight) and surface-area-based (rate × BSA, Mosteller). Arithmetic only; not a prescribing decision — check the product's own dosing and the patient. - **CHA₂DS₂-VASc** — Lip GYH, et al. *Chest* 2010;137:263–72. Congestive heart failure (1), hypertension (1), age ≥75 (2), diabetes (1), prior stroke/TIA/thromboembolism (2), vascular disease (1), age 65–74 (1), female sex (1). **Intended population: non-valvular atrial fibrillation.** Not a general risk score; it does not decide treatment. ## Tests The app carries its own known-value self-tests — one per calculator, plus a units-consistency check. Open `index.html?selftest=1` and read the console, or run them headlessly: ``` npm install npm test ``` `test/selftest.js` loads the built `index.html` in a headless DOM, runs the self-tests, and drives the calculator (creatinine clearance, the "Show the working" panel). `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs it on every push. ## Disclaimer This is a **decision-support aid only**. Results are population estimates, not a diagnosis, and do not replace clinical judgement. Use adjusted weights and clinical context for individual patients, and apply appropriate caution for renal, cardiac and paediatric cases. ## License Released under the **PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0** — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). © 2026 Dr. Sohil Momin. --- Made with care by [Dr. Sohil Momin](https://github.com/drsamonline).

# Canteen

<!-- shot:start -->

![Screenshot](docs/shot.png)

<!-- shot:end -->

[![live](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-online-22c55e)](https://drsamonline.github.io/canteen-lan/)
[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)
[![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-78%20passed-22c55e)](test-node.js)
[![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/canteen-lan)](https://github.com/drsamonline/canteen-lan/releases)

**Order from your table over the room's own Wi-Fi.** Guests tap a menu and send an
order from their seat; the kitchen sees every table's orders live and moves each one
along. No accounts, no internet, no telemetry — the orders travel across your own
network and nowhere else.

Built with **Forge**, thin on two shared kits: **web-kit** (storage, i18n
EN/HI/GU, CSV, theme, a11y, ui) and **lan-kit** (the LAN room transport).

## What it does

One person starts a room on a laptop in the canteen; everyone else opens the board
and joins it. A guest picks a table and a name, adds items from the menu to a cart,
and places the order. The kitchen view lists every open order grouped by table,
shows the running bill for each table, and can mark an order *preparing*, *served*
or *cancelled* — or wipe the served pile at the end of a shift. A guest can also
**call the waiter** or **ask for the bill**, and the kitchen acknowledges it. A late
joiner is caught up from the host's history automatically.

## Run it

**Start the room** (on one machine — a laptop, a Pi, anything with Node):

```
node host/room.js                 # room "canteen", port 8080
```

It prints the address to use on the LAN, for example `http://192.168.1.20:8080`. It
also seeds the room with the menu, so every device sees the same prices. Override
the menu with `--menu my-menu.json` (a JSON array of `{ "sku", "name", "price" }`,
price in paise).

**Join the board** — open the published page on any device on the same Wi-Fi:

- **https://drsamonline.github.io/canteen-lan/** → *Open the board*, then paste the
  host address and tap **Join room**;

or run it locally: open `docs/play/index.html` in a browser (the engine
`docs/play/canteen.js`, the transport `docs/play/lan-kit.js` sit next to it, so it works from `file://` too).

```
node test-node.js      # 78 passed, 0 failed
```

## How it is built

The app is **thin**: storage, languages, theming, accessibility and the CSV export
come from **web-kit**; the room — SSE for server→client, plain POST for
client→server, a room code and a LAN URL — comes from **lan-kit**. The only
app-specific code is

- `docs/play/canteen.js` — a small, pure, zero-dependency engine holding the order

# case-kit

[![live](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-online-22c55e)](https://drsamonline.github.io/case-kit/)
[![test](https://github.com/drsamonline/case-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/case-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)

**Clinical case tracking.** Zero dependencies. One file. Sections, dated symptoms, follow-ups, a timeline and a summary — the shared logic
extracted from the drsamonline apps that repeat it.

## Use it

See `case-kit.js` for the full API and `test-node.js` for worked examples.

## What it does

- sections (history / habits / mapping)
- dated symptoms with severity
- follow-ups (remedy / potency / response)
- timeline + summary + JSON
- a plain-JSON interchange record (patient + version + cases)

## Interchange record

A case (or a set of cases) can be handed to another app in the family as **one
plain-JSON file** — no server, no network:

```json
{
  "format": "case-kit/record",
  "version": 1,
  "exported": "2026-01-07T10:00:00.000Z",
  "patient": { "id": "p-001", "label": "S.M." },
  "cases": [ { "id": "c…", "title": "Skin case 12", "sections": { … }, "symptoms": [ … ], "followUps": [ … ] } ]
}
```

```js
var text = Case.exportRecord(caseOrCases, { id: "p-001", label: "S.M." });
var rec  = Case.importRecord(text);   // { version, patient, cases: [...] }
```

- **`patient`** is an opaque `id` and a short `label` (initials or a code) —
  **never a name**. Nothing identifying is carried by default.
- **`version`** lets the shape evolve: older records still import (migrated at
  `importRecord`), and a *newer* version is refused rather than guessed.
- The family mapping: a case's `followUps` are the **encounters**, and its
  `symptoms` / `sections` are the **notes** — a case-kit record expresses both.
- Where a record is encrypted (the **Encrypted Case Log**), encrypt the whole
  envelope — the interchange file must be the encrypted archive, not plaintext.

## Verified

```
node test-node.js
26 passed, 0 failed
```

## Consumers

skin-case-tracker, HMS, whispering-body-first-aid, gentle-pediatrics-companion

**A shared whiteboard for the room.** Everyone on the same Wi-Fi draws on the
same board, live. No accounts, no internet, no telemetry — the strokes travel
across your own network and nowhere else.

Built with **Forge**, thin on two shared kits: **web-kit** (storage, i18n
EN/HI/GU, theme, a11y, ui) and **lan-kit** (the LAN room transport).

## What it does

One person starts a room on a laptop in the room; everyone else opens the board
and joins it. Draw with a finger or a mouse, pick a colour and a brush, rub
things out, undo your last stroke, clear the board for everyone, and save a PNG
of the result. A late joiner is caught up from the host's history automatically.

## Run it

**Start the room** (on one machine — a laptop, a Pi, anything with Node):

```
node host/room.js                 # room "chalk", port 8080
```

It prints the address to use on the LAN, for example `http://192.168.1.20:8080`.

**Join the board** — open the published page on any device on the same Wi-Fi:

- **https://drsamonline.github.io/chalk-lan/** → *Open the board*, then paste the
  host address and tap **Join room**;

or run it locally: open `docs/play/index.html` in a browser (the engine
`docs/play/chalk.js`, the transport `docs/play/lan-kit.js` and the shared runtime
`docs/play/web-kit.js` sit next to it, so it works from `file://` too).

```
node test-node.js      # 38 passed, 0 failed
```

The app is **thin**: storage, languages, theming and accessibility come from
**web-kit**; the room — SSE for server→client, plain POST for client→server, a
room code and a LAN URL — comes from **lan-kit**. The only app-specific code is

- `docs/play/chalk.js` — a small, pure, zero-dependency engine holding the board
  document and the four-message protocol that keeps every device in step
  (`point`, `stroke`, `undo`, `clear`). It runs unchanged in the browser and under
  Node, so the whole mechanic is unit-tested headlessly;
- `docs/play/index.html` — the canvas, the toolbar and the join panel, wired to
  web-kit and lan-kit;
- `host/room.js` + `host/lan-host.js` — the tiny zero-dependency room host.

Every message is sanitised on arrival (colour, size and points are validated and
clamped), so a buggy or hostile peer on the LAN cannot break the board.

## Build the EXE and APK

This repo calls the shared build workflow. On every push, GitHub Actions builds a
portable Windows EXE and a signed Android APK from `docs/play` and attaches them
to the `app-latest` release.

# compress-kit

[![live](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-online-22c55e)](https://drsamonline.github.io/compress-kit/)
[![test](https://github.com/drsamonline/compress-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/compress-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)

**The shared compression core for drsamonline apps.** One file, no dependencies,
built on the platform's **Compression Streams**.

The browser counterpart to `lexora` (which compresses on the CLI/server). Apps
never bundle a compression library:

```js
const gz  = await Compress.gzip(bytes);      // -> Uint8Array
const raw = await Compress.gunzip(gz);       // -> Uint8Array

const b64 = await Compress.compressString("lots of text…");
const txt = await Compress.decompressString(b64);
```

## API

| Call | Does |
|---|---|
| `Compress.gzip` / `gunzip` | gzip (with header). |
| `Compress.deflate` / `inflate` | zlib deflate. |
| `Compress.deflateRaw` / `inflateRaw` | raw deflate (no header) — smallest. |
| `Compress.compressString` / `decompressString` | Text ⇄ base64, any format. |
| `Compress.ratio(original, compressed)` | Compressed/original, for a UI. |
| `Compress.human(n)` | "12.4 KB" style formatting. |
| `Compress.bytes` | text/base64 helpers. |

## Why not a library

Compression Streams are built into modern browsers and Node 18+, so a
compression library is dead weight. This wrapper is the one place the plumbing
lives — and it reads the stream directly, so it needs no `Response`/`Blob` and
runs everywhere the streams exist.

## Verified

```
node test-node.js
PASS  gzip round-trip
PASS  deflate round-trip
PASS  deflate-raw round-trip
PASS  repetitive data compresses well
PASS  string round-trip
PASS  unicode survives
6 passed, 0 failed
```

## Environment

Needs **Compression Streams** — Chrome 80+, Firefox 113+, Safari 16.4+, Node 18+.
`Compress.available()` reports it.

Landing page  ·  Live demo  ·  Download for Windows (.exe)  ·  Download for Android (.apk)  ·  Source  ·  Features  ·  Changelog  ·  All projects

--- Conqueror OS is a self-contained personal application for building mental resilience. click any highlight to edit or delete. - **Selection quick-actions** — highlight, copy, or send the selection straight to a new journal entry. - **Notes** per chapter with Markdown and `[[wiki links]]` to other chapters. - **Bookmarks with labels**, a dedicated Bookmarks page, and a Favourite-quotes page. - **Inline SVG diagrams** — a themed, hand-built diagram for every chapter, drawn to adapt to the current theme. - **Focus mode**, line-spacing / width / font / weight controls, and **read-aloud** (Web Speech API). - **Themes:** light, dark, sepia, high-contrast, OLED black, and Auto (follows the OS). - **Resume banner** and dwell-time tracking (minutes per day and per chapter). ### Journal & reflection - Six entry types, **tags**, and filters by **type, tag, date range and free text**. - **Edit** entries, **draft autosave**, **voice dictation**, and a rotating daily prompt. - **"On this day"** resurfacing of past entries. - **Attachments** (images) stored in IndexedDB. ### Trackers & analytics - Built-in trackers (mood, sleep, exercise, meditation, habits) plus **custom trackers**. - **Trend line + 7-day moving average**, **calendar heatmap**, and **correlation** (Pearson r) between any two trackers. - Local-only **insights** and printable / exportable reports. ### Challenges & review - Structured 7/21/30/45/90-day programs plus **custom challenges**. - **Pause/resume**, **reminders**, a **shareable progress card** (canvas → PNG). - **Spaced repetition** (SM-2 lite) over each chapter's key idea and reflection. ### Worksheets & knowledge - Reusable fillable sheets with saved history (Daily Check, Weekly Review, Setback Ledger). - **Knowledge graph** of chapters, worksheets and challenges by shared concepts. - **Glossary** auto-built from chapter tags. ### Data, safety & privacy - **Undo** on every delete; # control-panel

[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32)](LICENSE)

**Every workflow in every repository — what runs, when, what calls what, and what is connected to nothing.**

Nothing in this system knew its own shape. There were ~112 workflows across ~64 repositories: reusable
ones, callers, schedules, dispatches — and no single place that answered *"what runs, and what calls
what?"*. This is that place.

It is also the control surface: **every workflow has a Run button**, and they are grouped into the four
stages they actually form — from an idea to a shipped app to the system repairing itself.

## What it holds

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `docs/inventory.json` | every workflow, parsed: its triggers, cron, jobs, `needs`, steps, permissions, and every reusable call it makes |
| `docs/plan.json` | the four stages, the routes through them, and the workflows that fit in no stage |
| `docs/index.html` | the panel — the pipeline, the routes, the Run buttons, and what is broken |
| `tools/fetch.py` | pull every repo's workflows into a tree (no secret needed for public repos) |
| `tools/scan.py` | parse the tree into the inventory, and work out who calls whom |
| `tools/plan.py` | turn the inventory into the stages and the routes |

## The four stages

1. **Scratch** — an idea becomes a repo. `intake`, `new-app`, `adopt`.
2. **Build** — a repo becomes an artefact. Every `test`, `ci`, `lint`, and the app pipeline.
3. **Deliver** — an artefact becomes public. `release`, `pages`, `shot`, `app-deliver`, the refreshers.
4. **Repair** — the system keeps itself honest. `self-diagnose`, `self-heal`, `health`, `audit`, `backup`,
   `repo-learning`, `backlog-status`.

## The routes — how little you have to do

| route | you do | then, on its own |
|---|---|---|
| **A new app** | describe it in one line | spec → repo → guards → landing page → three-platform build → release → demo → screenshot |
| **Change an app** | push, or merge a PR | test → build → release → demo → screenshot |
| **Repair** | nothing | diagnose → heal → audit → learn → back up |
| **Ship on demand** | press Run | three builds → release → demo → screenshot |

**The everyday routes ask for at most one thing, and usually nothing.**

## How Forge embeds

Three layers, three jobs:

- **Forge** (private) is the **brain** — the memory (backlog, run log, registry, rules), the tools, and the agent's workspace.
- **This panel** (public) is the **map** — what runs, what calls what, what is missing, and the routes.
- **The dashboard** (public) is the **vitals** — what the system *is*: the products, their health, the conformance scores.

One-way and checkable: **Forge writes the memory → the tools derive the facts → the panel and the dashboard publish them.**
Anyone can run the tools and get the same numbers.

## Why this is the commercial product

You are not selling an app. You are selling **a system that governs itself and can prove it** — one that audits its own
drift, catches its own silent failures, backs up before every merge, and shows its work in public, with the numbers
generated from the repositories rather than typed into a slide. The licence sells **Forge**; the apps stay free, which is
what makes the map worth reading.

## What is missing (tools/gaps.py)

Every check is a rule with a reason — `permissions`, `timeout-minutes`, `concurrency`, drift, orphans, un-runnable
workflows. **DRIFT is the one that already cost a release.**

## The chosen routes (tools/simulate.py)

Candidates are **scored**, not asserted: inputs, hand-actions, how many things must go right, **the chance the output is
wrong**, stage coverage, resumability, and whether the route leans on a hand-copied workflow. The winner per scenario is
the one the numbers choose.

## The Run buttons

Each opens that workflow's page on GitHub — the real dispatch. Nothing here needs a token in a browser,
which is why the panel can be public.

## How it stays true

`scan.yml` runs daily: it re-fetches every workflow, rebuilds the inventory and the plan, runs both
tools' own tests first, and commits the fresh data. The page reads that data, so it cannot drift from
what the workflows actually are.

## Licence

PolyForm Noncommercial — see `LICENSE`. © 2026 Dr Sohil Momin.

# crypto-kit

[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32)](LICENSE)

[![test](https://github.com/drsamonline/crypto-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/crypto-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml)


**The shared crypto core for drsamonline apps.** One file, no dependencies,
built on the Web Crypto API.

Apps should never hand-roll cryptography. This is the one place it lives — the
browser-side counterpart to what `lockhtml` does on the command line:

- **AES-256-GCM** — authenticated encryption, so tampering is detected;
- **passphrase keys** via **PBKDF2-SHA256**;
- a portable **sealed envelope** (`salt + iv + ciphertext`) as bytes or base64;
- a **one-time-view** helper (seal with a random key, delete it after first open);
- byte / text / base64 helpers.

## Use it

```js
// passphrase-sealed note
const b64 = await CryptoKit.sealString("meet me at 7", "correct horse");
const text = await CryptoKit.openString(b64, "correct horse");   // -> "meet me at 7"

// or a key you manage yourself
const key = await CryptoKit.newKey();
const box = await CryptoKit.encrypt(key, CryptoKit.bytes.fromText("hi"));
const back = await CryptoKit.decrypt(key, box);
```

## API

| Call | Does |
|---|---|
| `CryptoKit.seal(bytes, passphrase, opts)` | Returns the sealed envelope (Uint8Array). |
| `CryptoKit.open(envelope, passphrase, opts)` | Decrypts; **throws** on wrong passphrase or tampering. |
| `CryptoKit.sealString` / `openString` | The same, as base64 strings. |
| `CryptoKit.deriveKey(pass, salt, iters)` | A PBKDF2 AES-256 key. |
| `CryptoKit.encrypt` / `decrypt` | AES-GCM with a key you hold. |
| `CryptoKit.newKey` / `exportKey` / `importKey` | Random keys, for one-time view. |
| `CryptoKit.randomBytes(n)` | Cryptographically random bytes. |

`opts.aad` adds associated data (bound to the ciphertext, not encrypted).
`opts.iterations` sets the PBKDF2 cost (default 250,000).

## One-time view

Seal with a random key, give the key out-of-band, and delete it after the first
`open`. `crypto-kit` gives you the primitives; the app owns the "used once" state.

## Secure context

Web Crypto needs **https or localhost**. GitHub Pages is https, so deployed apps
are fine; opening a page from `file://` may not be.

## Verified

```
node test-node.js
7 passed, 0 failed
```

# Dance Fight ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Every fight move is a dance move.** A single-file browser rhythm game — load your own track, the beat is analysed up front, and every attack you throw is a dance move. Land it in time with the music and it becomes a **PERFECT** hit worth 60% extra damage. **🔗 [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/dance-fight/)**  ·  **🎮 [Play the live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/dance-fight/play/)**  ·  **[Source](https://github.com/drsamonline/dance-fight)** **Download:** [Windows (.exe)](https://github.com/drsamonline/dance-fight/releases/latest/download/dance-fight-portable.exe)  ·  [Android (.apk)](https://github.com/drsamonline/dance-fight/releases/latest/download/dance-fight.apk)
---

Every fight move is a dance move.

Load a track from your device and the character dances to it. The beat is analysed up front, the whole arena pulses on the pulse, and every attack you throw is a dance move — land it in time with the music and it becomes a PERFECT hit worth 60% extra damage.

▶ Play it in your browser

--- ## What it is A single-file browser game. No build step, no dependencies, no install, no server. ``` index.html # the entire game — HTML, CSS, JS, ~78 KB ``` Open it, pick a song, fight. It works offline and from `file://` too. ### Highlights - **The music drives everything.** Your track is analysed for its real beat grid, and the character's dance is locked to the audio playhead — so it can't drift, and it doesn't depend on frame rate. - **Every move is a dance move.** Arm Wave, Spinning Kick, Body-Roll Uppercut and a 720° Body-Roll Finisher. Spins are real rotations, not pose swaps. - **The character never stops dancing.** Attack poses are layered *over* the ongoing groove rather than replacing it. - **Rhythm is the combat system.** Moves landed on the beat hit 60% harder and build a bigger combo. Shuffle-stepping in time charges your finisher meter. - **Keyboard and touch.** On-screen controls appear automatically on phones. - **One file, zero dependencies.** No framework, no bundler, no CDN. --- ## How to play Pick an audio file (or just press Start and it plays a default 128 BPM groove). | Key | Move | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `A` `D` | Shuffle step | Dance-walk. Stepping in time charges your finisher meter | | `W` | Leap | Arabesque | | `S` | Dip | Guards and dodges — hold to block | | `J` | **Arm Wave** | Fast, low damage | | `K` | **Spinning Kick** | Medium — a full 360° turn | | `L` | **Body-Roll Uppercut** | Heavy — rolls through a full turn | | `SPACE` | **Body-Roll Finisher** | Needs a full meter — a 720° spin | | `P` | Pause / resume music | | **Land moves on the beat.** A move thrown within ~80 ms of a beat lands as a PERFECT: 1.6× damage and a bigger combo multiplier. The gold `· ON BEAT` tag on the move name tells you when you nailed it. **On a phone:** on-screen controls appear automatically. Hold a direction with one thumb and tap attacks with the other. Rotate to landscape — the arena is wider than it is tall. --- ## How the beat sync works The interesting part. The usual approach — polling an `AnalyserNode` every frame — ties beat detection to the render frame rate, which falls apart on a slow device. This game does it **offline instead**, on the decoded audio buffer, before the fight starts: 1. **Low-pass** the signal to ~180 Hz with a one-pole filter (kick-drum territory). 2. Build a **per-10 ms RMS envelope**, then take its **positive flux**. 3. **Peak-pick** onsets against an adaptive threshold. 4. **Autocorrelate** the flux over lags of 0.30–0.75 s to find the tempo, refined to sub-sample accuracy. 5. Search every phase offset for the **grid that lines up with the most onset energy**. The result is a beat grid. During play the dance phase is read *straight off the audio playhead* — `(playhead − phase) / period` — so the groove cannot drift, and it is completely independent of frame rate. On test tracks at 100, 128 and 150 BPM the detected tempo was exact, and **97% of kicks landed within 30 ms of a grid beat** (median offset 5–9 ms, which is just the 10 ms hop resolution). Everything else is drawn on a forward-kinematic skeleton. Moves are keyframed joint angles blended *over* the ongoing dance groove rather than replacing it, so the character keeps dancing while it fights. Spins are faked as a horizontal squash that mirrors past 90°, with the near and far limbs swapping — and every attack leaves additive ghost trails of the last few poses, which is what makes a rotation read as motion. --- ## Run it locally ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/dance-fight.git cd dance-fight open index.html # macOS (xdg-open on Linux, start on Windows) ``` No toolchain needed. To serve it instead: ```bash python3 -m http.server 8000 # then visit http://localhost:8000 ``` --- ## Known limitations Being straight about what this is and isn't: - **Autoplay.** Browsers block audio until you interact with the page, so the first tap or click unlocks sound. If you ever hear nothing, a **live level meter** under the BPM readout shows whether audio is actually flowing — and a banner appears if it isn't. That meter reads real signal, not a flag. - **Tempo lock is at load.** A track with a long ambient intro, or one that drifts tempo, gets a grid based on the overall character of the song. If no clear pulse is found it falls back to a steady 128 BPM. - **Mobile is landscape.** It's playable in portrait, but the arena is 16:9 and it will be cramped. - **Feel is unverified at 60fps.** The geometry, timing and beat grid were verified programmatically, but I could only test in a headless browser rendering a few frames per second. How the spins and trails feel in motion is the part you're the judge of. ---

License

MIT © Dr Sohil Momin

# dashboard — the live status of the drsamonline system

[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32)](LICENSE)

A **public** status page for the whole fleet, served from **GitHub Pages** (public
repo = free Pages, no paid plan). It shows every repo, its build health, its
download links, and the store.

## How it stays current (free, no PAT)

A static page cannot read private repos from a browser. So the data is
**pre-rendered**: the Forge agent (which has admin access) generates `data.json`
from the `registry`, the `knowledge` index and the GitHub API, and commits it here
on a schedule. `index.html` is a plain static app that just renders `data.json`.

```
registry + knowledge + GitHub API
        │  (Forge agent, scheduled)
        ▼
   data.json  ──▶  index.html  ──▶  GitHub Pages (public, free)
```

No PAT, no secrets, no server. Sensitive internals (quota detail, the commercial
plan) stay in the private repos and are reported to the owner directly, not here.

## Files

- `index.html` — the static dashboard (no CDN, no build step).
- `data.json` — the rendered data (regenerated by the agent).
- `generate.py` — the reference generator the agent runs.

# drsamonline.github.io

The personal project index for **Dr Sohil Momin**, served by GitHub Pages at
**https://drsamonline.github.io/**.

[![Live site](https://img.shields.io/badge/live%20site-drsamonline.github.io-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/)
[![Projects: 41](https://img.shields.io/badge/projects-41-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/)
[![Offline-first](https://img.shields.io/badge/offline--first-yes-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/)
[![No trackers, no cookies](https://img.shields.io/badge/no%20trackers-no%20cookies-586069?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/)
[![Type: project hub](https://img.shields.io/badge/type-project%20hub-586069?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/)
[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](LICENSE)

**Live site:** <https://drsamonline.github.io/>  ·  **Source:** <https://github.com/drsamonline/drsamonline.github.io>

A single static page that lists every project. The data is **built ahead of
time and committed**, so the page never depends on a rate-limited third-party
call to render — it fetches one same-origin JSON file and falls back to an
embedded snapshot if that is unavailable.

## How it works

1. A scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/refresh-hub.yml`)
   runs daily at 03:17 UTC and on `workflow_dispatch`, with
   `permissions: contents: write`.
2. It calls the GitHub API **with the runner's authenticated token** (never the
   60-requests/hour unauthenticated limit), drops forks and the
   `drsamonline` / `drsamonline.github.io` repos, and merges the rest with the
   `CURATED` map inside `index.html`. A repo that is **not** in the map still
   appears, under the automatic **Other / New** category, using its GitHub
   description.
3. `tools/build_hub.py` writes the merged data to **`repos.json`** and
   regenerates the embedded snapshot in `index.html` (so the offline fallback
   always matches) plus the JSON-LD `ItemList` and `sitemap.xml`.
4. `tools/capture_shots.py` loads every project landing page at 1200×750,
   downscales to 600×375 and encodes **WebP** into `assets/shots/<repo>.webp`.
   Images that already exist, are recent and were a successful capture are
   skipped; failures fall back to a branded placeholder and are retried.
5. Everything is committed back to the repository.

At runtime the page:

* renders instantly from the embedded snapshot, then
* fetches **`repos.json`** (same origin, no rate limit, fast) and re-renders.

No third-party screenshot host, no runtime GitHub API call, no analytics.

## Design

* Calm, professional palette built on CSS custom properties in `:root`, with a
  full override under `[data-theme="dark"]`. Body text meets WCAG AA (4.5:1)
  and UI borders meet 3:1 in both themes.
* A **theme toggle** in the navigation that respects `prefers-color-scheme` on a
  first visit, persists the choice in `localStorage`, applies the stored theme
  **before first paint** via a tiny inline `<head>` script, updates its
  `aria-label` / `aria-pressed` and icon, and works with the keyboard.
* `prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured throughout.
* Self-contained: inline CSS/JS, no external JS libraries, inline SVG icons.

## Layout

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | The hub. Contains the `CURATED` map (source of curated fields) and the embedded snapshot. |
| `repos.json` | Build-time data the page fetches at runtime. |
| `tools/build_hub.py` | Fetches the API, merges with `CURATED`, writes `repos.json` + snapshot + JSON-LD + sitemap. |
| `tools/capture_shots.py` | Captures and encodes the local thumbnails. |
| `tools/placeholders.py` | Branded fallback thumbnail. |
| `assets/shots/` | Locally served thumbnails (`<repo>.webp`) + `_manifest.json`. |
| `.github/workflows/refresh-hub.yml` | The scheduled build. |

## Customising

Everything configurable lives in the small block at the top of the inline
`<script>` in `index.html`:

| Setting | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `CURATED` | Per-repo `cat`, `desc`, `demo`, `feat`, `rel`, `kicker`, `tag`. |
| `CAT_LABEL` / `CAT_ORDER` | Category names and display order. |
| `FEATURED` | Repo keys pinned to the top of the Featured section. |

## Local preview

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8080
# then open http://localhost:8080/
```

To regenerate the data locally without the API:

```bash
HUB_REPOS_FILE=repos_raw.json python3 tools/build_hub.py
```

## Privacy

The page has no backend, no analytics and no cookies. It fetches only its own
`repos.json` and its own images; the Content-Security-Policy restricts network
access to `'self'`.

original prose) belongs to its author and is **© 2026 Dr Sohil Momin, all rights
reserved**. Repository descriptions are pulled from the GitHub API and remain
the property of their respective authors.

# export-kit

[![live](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-online-22c55e)](https://drsamonline.github.io/export-kit/)
[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)


**Get bytes and files off the device, in the browser.** One file, no build step,
no dependencies. Works from `file://` and from GitHub Pages.

Every single-file app was re-implementing the same thing: `Blob` →
`URL.createObjectURL` → a hidden `<a download>`; and one app hand-wrote a ZIP to
bundle several files. This is that code, once.

It is the layer *above* the codecs: `web-kit` writes CSV text, `compress-kit`
does gzip/deflate — `export-kit` turns data into a file the user actually
receives, and can bundle several into one archive.

## Use it

Drop `export-kit.js` next to your code and load it, then use the global `Export`:

```html
<script src="export-kit.js"></script>
<script>
  Export.text("notes.txt", "hello");
  Export.json("data.json", { hello: "world" });
  Export.csv("rows.csv", Loom.csv.toCSV(rows));   // build the CSV with web-kit
  Export.blob("photo.png", someUint8Array, "image/png");

  // bundle several files into one archive (store-only, no compression)
  Export.saveZip("bundle.zip", [
    { name: "notes.txt", data: "hello" },
    { name: "data.json", data: JSON.stringify(obj) },
    { name: "raw.bin", data: bytes }
  ]);
</script>
```

For a truly single-file app, inline the contents of `export-kit.js` in a
`<script>` block. Nothing else is required.

## API

| | |
|---|---|
| `Export.save(name, data, mime)` | Generic: string → text, `Uint8Array`/`ArrayBuffer`/`Blob` → binary. |
| `Export.text(name, str, mime?)` | Save a text file. |
| `Export.json(name, obj, pretty?)` | Save pretty JSON (pass `false` to minify). |
| `Export.csv(name, csvText)` | Save CSV text (build it with `Loom.csv.toCSV`). |
| `Export.blob(name, data, mime?)` | Save binary data. |
| `Export.zip(files)` | Build a **store-only ZIP** → `Uint8Array`. `files = [{ name, data, date? }]`. |
| `Export.saveZip(name, files)` | Build and download a ZIP. |
| `Export.crc32(data)` | CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3), as the ZIP format requires. |
| `Export.toBytes(data)` | Normalise string / `Uint8Array` / `ArrayBuffer` to bytes. |
| `Export.blobUrl(blob)` / `Export.revoke(url)` | Object-URL helpers. |

## Notes

- **Store-only ZIP** (method 0): fast, dependency-free, and readable by every
  unzip tool. If you need compression, gzip each entry with `compress-kit`
  first.
- **Zero dependencies.** No `TextEncoder` needed (a UTF-8 fallback is built in);
  no CDN; no telemetry.
- `Export.zip` is pure and runs in Node too — which is how it is tested.

## Verified

`test-node.js` proves byte normalisation, the CRC-32 vectors, and a full ZIP
round-trip (build → read back → check names, bytes and CRCs):

```
node test-node.js
...
22 passed, 0 failed
```

The generated archive is also verified with the system `unzip -t` in CI-style
checks.

# frame-kit

[![live](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-online-22c55e)](https://drsamonline.github.io/frame-kit/)
[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)


**The shared transfer-frame core for drsamonline apps.** One file, no build step,
no dependencies.

`optical-kit` moves bytes; `frame-kit` *wraps* them. It is the layer the
optical-transfer apps (`helioprism`, `blinkcode-ai`, `BLINKTRANSFER`) were each
re-implementing: a self-describing frame, the rateless collector that locks onto a
stream, and the byte/checksum helpers underneath.

## What it gives you

- **A 22-byte self-describing header** — magic, version, transferId, k,
  blockSize, totalLength, a payload CRC-32, the symbol id, and a header CRC-16.
  A receiver can lock onto *any* frame, mid-stream, with no separate header code.
- **Strict validation of untrusted input** — a decoded frame is bytes from a
  camera; a corrupt or crafted header is dropped, not allowed to allocate.
- **A rateless `FountainCollector`** — absorbs symbols in any order, tolerates
  duplicates, restarts when the transfer id changes, and verifies the payload
  checksum when it assembles.
- **Byte/checksum utilities** — CRC-16/CCITT, CRC-32, a seeded PRNG, XOR/concat
  helpers and size formatting.

## Use it

Drop `frame-kit.js` next to your code and load it, then use the global `Frame`:

```html
<script src="frame-kit.js"></script>
<script>
  const frame = Frame.pack({
    magic: 0xb7, transferId: 42, k, blockSize,
    totalLength: payload.length, payloadCRC: Frame.crc32(payload),
    symbolId, data: symbol,
  });
  const parsed = Frame.parse(frame, { magics: [0xb7], label: 'MyApp' });
</script>
```

The collector sits over a fountain decoder (the codec lives in `optical-kit`).
Pass the decoder factory, or omit it to use `optical-kit`'s decoder if it is
loaded:

```js
const rx = new Frame.FountainCollector(LTDecoder);   // your decoder
rx.add(Frame.parse(bytes, { magics: [0xb7] }));
rx.progress;                 // 0..1
rx.assemble();               // Uint8Array, checksum verified — or throws
```

## API

| | |
|---|---|
| `Frame.pack(opts)` | Build a frame from `{ magic?, transferId, k, blockSize, totalLength, payloadCRC\|checksum, symbolId, data }`. |
| `Frame.parse(bytes, opts?)` | Parse and validate; `opts` = `{ magics?, label? }`. Throws on anything malformed. |
| `Frame.FountainCollector(Decoder)` | The rateless collector. `.add(frame)`, `.assemble()`, `.complete`, `.progress`, `.received`, `.count`, `.symbols`, `.transferId`, `.magic`, `.reset()`. |
| `Frame.crc16`, `Frame.crc32` | CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE and CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3). |
| `Frame.createPRNG(seed)` | Mulberry32 seeded PRNG. |
| `Frame.xorInto`, `Frame.concatBytes`, `Frame.formatSize`, `Frame.generateUUID`, `Frame.guessType` | The small helpers the apps share. |
| `Frame.HEADER_SIZE`, `Frame.VERSION`, `Frame.MAX_CONTAINER`, `Frame.DEFAULT_MAGIC`, `Frame.frameBytes`, `Frame.blockCount` | Frame geometry. |

## Verified

`test-node.js` proves the frame, its validation and the collector:

```
node test-node.js
...
19 passed, 0 failed
```

--- ## The two transports | | **QR** | **SpectraCode** | |---|---|---| | Physical layer | monochrome QR modules | 36-colour cells, 5 bits each | | Per frame | ~1.4 KB | ~5.1 KB | | Strength | any camera reads it; any scanner reads a tiny file | far more capacity per frame | | Best for | small files, cheap optics, maximum compatibility | larger files | Both carry the **same** frame format and the **same** rateless fountain stream, so a missed frame costs one more symbol rather than a whole loop. The magic byte in each frame says which layer carried it, so the receiver **auto-detects** — point one receiver at either code and it works. ## How it works ``` files ─▶ container ─▶ fountain symbols ─▶ frames ─▶ QR or colour matrix │ files ◀─ container ◀─ collector ◀─ frame ◀─ camera ─┘ ``` - **Selection engine** — auto-picks QR for small payloads and the colour transport for large ones, or you choose. - **Compatibility mode** — a small text file can go out as one plain QR that any third-party scanner reads. - **Offline-first PWA** — installable; after first load it never touches the network. ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/helioprism.git cd helioprism npm install npm run dev # http://localhost:3000 npm test # both transports, end to end npm run build # production bundle into docs/play/ ``` Open the dev URL on both devices (or install the PWA). # Repertorium Publicum Explorer

[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32)](LICENSE)

<!-- shot:start -->

![Screenshot](docs/shot.png)

<!-- shot:end -->

An **offline, single-file** repertory explorer for **Repertorium Publicum** (2008) — an open,
**Kent-derived** repertory — with the printed three-grade system intact, a case builder, and
grade-weighted repertorisation.

**[Open the repertory →](https://drsamonline.github.io/kent-repertory-explorer/)** · no server,
no backend, no account, no API calls. Everything runs in the browser; nothing you type leaves the device.

---

## What it is, precisely

The data is **Repertorium Publicum** by **Vladimir Polony (2008)**, published as part of the
[OpenRep](https://github.com/nondeterministic/oorep) source code and licensed **GPL v3**.

It is **not** Kent's *Repertory of the Homoeopathic Materia Medica*, 1897 first edition. It has its
own chapter structure — separate *Clinical*, *Appetite*, *Blood* and *Heart & Circulation* chapters,
which Kent does not have — and its own additions. Earlier releases of this app described it as Kent
1897; that was wrong, and it has been corrected throughout.

## What's inside

| | |
|---|---|
| Rubrics | **74,480** |
| Graded remedy links | **735,460** |
| Remedies | **669** |
| Chapters | **41** |

Every link carries a grade, taken from the typography of the printed repertory:

| grade | meaning | links |
|---|---|---|
| **3** | strongest association | 71,582 |
| *2* | moderate | 198,591 |
| 1 | least | 465,287 |

## Features

- **Search in repertory language** — `anxiety night`, `thirstless`, `weeping consolation`. Results
  are ranked **narrowest first**, because the rubrics with three remedies are the ones that narrow a case.
- **Chapter browse** across all 41 chapters, with rubric counts.
- **Filters** — narrow-only with an adjustable threshold, sort by narrowest / broadest / A–Z / chapter.
- **Case builder** — add rubrics, attach a note to each, remove or clear.
- **Analysis** — remedies ranked by the sum of grades and rubrics covered; minimum-grade filter;
  "cover all rubrics"; exclude a remedy (it stays visible, struck through, and can be brought back).
- **Matrix** — remedy × rubric grid showing each grade.
- **Export** — plain text, CSV, JSON, copy to clipboard, and a clean print/PDF sheet.
- **Themes** — dark, light, high-contrast. **Keyboard-first** with `/`, `↑ ↓`, `Enter`, `c`, `a`, `m`, `t`, `Esc`.
- **Offline-first** — one self-contained HTML file, PWA manifest and a network-first service worker.
- **Case persists** in local storage; notes included.

## Using it

1. Search in **repertory language** — not the patient's words.
2. Prefer **narrow** rubrics; a rubric with 250 remedies tells you little, one with three is gold.
3. **Add** the rubrics that survive to your case.
4. Open **Analysis** to rank remedies across them.
5. Treat the ranking as a **shortlist to study in the materia medica** — the repertory narrows, the materia medica decides.

## Files

```
app.html                     the whole application (one self-contained file)
index.html                   landing page
docs/                        the same site, for a Pages source pointed at /docs
pipeline/extract.py          rebuilds kent.json from the OOReP database dump
pipeline/build_app.py        embeds the data (gzip + base64) into app.html
pipeline/app_template.html   the application source
```

`app.html` is built by `build_app.py`, which injects the repertory — gzipped and base64-encoded —
into the template. The browser decompresses it with `DecompressionStream`. The payload is ~1.9 MB.

## Data

Extracted from the OOReP PostgreSQL dump (repertory token `publicum`). The structured, graded JSON is
also published in
[`homoeopathic-materia-medica-repertory-json`](https://github.com/drsamonline/homoeopathic-materia-medica-repertory-json)
under `repertory/repertorium-publicum-2008/`.

## Licence

**GNU GPL v3** for the whole work. The app embeds the *Repertorium Publicum* dataset, which is
third-party material published under GPL v3, so the combined work is distributed under GPL v3.
GPL v3 permits commercial use; it requires that derivative works stay under GPL v3 and that the
source is made available.

- [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) · [`LICENSE-GPL-3.0.txt`](LICENSE-GPL-3.0.txt)
- Embedded data: Repertorium Publicum (2008), Vladimir Polony — GPL v3, part of the OpenRep source code.

Requests, not conditions: please credit Dr Sohil Momin and the source of the data.

## Disclaimer

A study and reference tool for practitioners and students. Not medical advice, and not a substitute
for the judgement of a qualified practitioner.

---

## Built with Forge

This repo is a **Forge** app and adopts the shared kits.

- **Shared build workflow** — `.github/workflows/build-apps.yml` calls the reusable
  build in [`drsamonline/app-builder`](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-builder).
  On every push to `main` it builds a portable Windows **EXE** and a signed
  Android **APK** and attaches them to the `app-latest` release, so these URLs
  always track the newest build:

  - `https://github.com/drsamonline/kent-repertory-explorer/releases/latest/download/kent-repertory-explorer-portable.exe`
  - `https://github.com/drsamonline/kent-repertory-explorer/releases/latest/download/kent-repertory-explorer.apk`

- **web-kit** — the shared offline-first runtime (`web-kit.js`, from
  [`drsamonline/web-kit`](https://github.com/drsamonline/web-kit)) is vendored in
  this repo, ready for the app to adopt on its next release.

Built with [Forge](https://github.com/drsamonline/forge) by Dr Sohil Momin.

# lan-kit

[![live](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-online-22c55e)](https://drsamonline.github.io/lan-kit/)
[![test](https://github.com/drsamonline/lan-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lan-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)

**The shared LAN core for drsamonline apps.** Zero dependencies. A local room with
a real-time channel, for apps that run on a Wi-Fi network with **no internet**.

The transport behind the LAN apps (`Chalk`, `Canteen`, `Blackboard`, `Rally`) —
extracted from `HMS` so it isn't re-implemented per app.

## Why SSE + POST (not WebSocket)

A WebSocket needs a framing library. Server-Sent Events and plain POST are built
into every browser and Node, so a room needs **no dependencies at all**:

- **server → clients:** `GET /events` (SSE)
- **clients → server:** `POST /send`
- **health:** `GET /health`

## Use it

**Host (Node, zero deps):**

```js
const { createHost } = require("./lan-host.js");
const host = createHost({ room: "canteen", history: 50 });
const port = await host.listen(0);          // 0 = any free port
host.onMessage(m => console.log("got", m));
host.broadcast({ hello: "room" });
```

**Client (browser):**

```js
const c = Lan.client({ url: Lan.hostUrl(8080),
                       onOpen:    h => console.log("joined", h.room),
                       onMessage: m => console.log("got", m) });
c.send({ from: "me", text: "hello room" });
```

`Lan.roomCode()` makes a short code (no 0/O/1/I/L); `Lan.hostUrl(port)` builds the
URL for the current LAN.

## Verified

```
node test-node.js
8 passed, 0 failed
```

Covers: listen, SSE connect, client count, POST broadcast, the hello event, the
observer callback, the health endpoint, and a clean close.

## What it is not

Not a security boundary. A LAN room is open to anyone on the network — add a room
code check in your app if you need one, and never send secrets over it.

## Licence

MIT. (c) 2026 Dr Sohil Momin. Part of the Forge system — kits open, orchestrator licensed.

LEXORA

Layered EXact-text Repository & Adaptive compression architecture
Canonicalize text conservatively, then compress it with guaranteed byte-exact recovery — decode(encode(C)) == C for every input.

Landing page  ·  Install from source  ·  Benchmarks  ·  FAQ  ·  Status  ·  Repository  ·  All projects

Phase 1 prototype — no releases and no stable API yet; install from a source checkout. PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 © 2026 Dr. Sohil Momin.

--- > **Project status: Phase 1 prototype in development.** Documentation (Batches A–E) complete/drafted; > early implementation code exists (canonicalization, Zstd core baseline, `.lxz` v0 container, benchmark harness, > CLI app, experimental PySide6 GUI milestones M1–M3). > Nothing here is a shipped or released feature. See [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) for the verified state. > **Badge honesty note:** the CI badge reflects the real workflow in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, but > **GitHub Actions runs are paused by owner decision 2026-10-17** (free-tier minutes exhausted; OQ-15) — > the badge shows the last historical run, not current state; verification gate is local (`pytest -q` + linkcheck > before every commit). The *Tests* badge is a > static snapshot of the locally verified suite (101 passed, re-verified 2026-10-17), not a live measurement. > **Last verified:** 2026-10-17 against the current working branch (see git history). --- ## What is LEXORA? LEXORA is a text-cleaning and **exact-compression** system for document collections (TXT, PDF, optionally OCR'd scans). It: 1. **Ingests** TXT and PDF files (OCR optional for scanned pages). 2. **Canonicalizes** the extracted text conservatively into deterministic UTF-8 bytes (this step *may* be lossy relative to the source, by design). 3. **Compresses** those canonical bytes with **guaranteed byte-exact recovery**: `decode(encode(C)) == C` for every input. The core invariant: **canonicalization may lose information relative to the original source; compression after canonicalization must never lose a single byte.** ## Why? Generic compressors (Zstandard, XZ, Brotli) treat text as opaque bytes. Document collections contain structure — repeated boilerplate, templates, records, multilingual text (English, Hindi, Gujarati) — that a compressor can exploit if it is allowed to *learn* representations safely. LEXORA's goal is to beat frozen generic baselines on total stored size while preserving strict correctness and running on low-resource hardware (~4 GiB RAM). ## Goals - Byte-exact losslessness after canonicalization — always, provably, via round-trip verification. - Conservative, versioned canonicalization with golden test vectors. - Cost-driven codec/candidate selection: every candidate competes against pinned baselines, and **every serialized byte counts** in the cost model. - Operate within a ~4 GiB RAM budget with bounded, streaming/block-based processing. - Multilingual support: English, Hindi (Devanagari), Gujarati. ## Non-goals (current scope) - Reconstructing original OCR output or source PDF layout bit-for-bit. - Claiming any performance advantage over Zstd/Brotli/XZ/PPMd before reproducible benchmark evidence exists (**no LEXORA-vs-baseline evidence exists**; the only published numbers, Revision R1, are baseline-vs-baseline on a Tier-1 smoke corpus — see [docs/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md](docs/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md)). - Being a general-purpose archive format. ## Features by maturity | Status | Capability | |---|---| | **Implemented** | Conservative canonicalizer (`src/lexora/canonicalize.py`), Zstd core baseline (`src/lexora/zstd_core.py`), `.lxz` v0 container (`src/lexora/container.py`, ADR-0007), **nine CLI verbs** (`canon`/`zround`/`pipe`/`pack`/`unpack`/`verify`/`inspect`/`batch`/`doctor` — see [docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md](docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md)), benchmark harness (`benchmarks/harness.py` + `corpus.py`, reproducible per [benchmarks/README.md](benchmarks/README.md)), test suite (**492 passed, 1 skipped**, verified 2026-10-29). **Every core path streams** — encode, decode and canonicalization are flat in document size (measured: 126 MiB / 35 MiB / 35 MiB peak) | | **In progress** | GUI milestones M1–M3 landed & offscreen-tested but **not released**; ADR-0011 decided the GUI becomes a *client of the CLI* (process separation) and that implementation has not started — it needs a Qt-capable machine. Corpus **meets** the ≥1 GiB benchmark requirement (2395 files / 1.054 GiB, OQ-8); what is missing is a protocol-scope run and owner sign-off. GitHub Actions paused by owner (OQ-15) — local gate is `pytest -q` + linkcheck | | **Planned** | TXT/PDF ingestion; experimental candidates (dictionaries, Re-Pair, bounded token PPM, numeric/record coding, template+residual); `.lxdb` database mode; optional encryption profile; GUI stretch items (batch queue, drag-and-drop, shortcuts) | ## Architecture overview (proposed) ``` TXT/PDF ──▶ Extraction (optional OCR) ──▶ Canonicalization (versioned, deterministic) ──▶ Compression (byte-exact, cost-selected codec) ──▶ .lxz archive (.lxdb later) ◀── decode ◀── verify: decode(encode(C)) == C enforced at build time ``` A normative specification (`docs/SPECIFICATION.md`) and detailed architecture documents exist as drafts (Batch B). To contribute, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md); the release process is documented in `docs/RELEASE_PROCESS.md` (no releases exist yet). ## Supported inputs & current limitations - **Design targets:** `.txt` (UTF-8/other encodings), `.pdf` (text-layer first; OCR for scanned pages), scripts: Latin, Devanagari, Gujarati. - **Current reality:** byte-level canonicalization of raw text streams is implemented (rules CAN-R01/R02/R05 of the v0 rule set); TXT/PDF *file ingestion* is not implemented yet. Build scope is English-only per owner directive 2026-10-16 (Hindi/Gujarati deferred, not blocking). ## Installation / Quick start Install from a source checkout (no published package exists): ```bash pip install -e . # core (Qt-free): zstandard pinned range, Python >=3.12,<4.0 pip install -e ".[dev]" # + pytest for the test suite pip install -e ".[gui]" # + PySide6 for the experimental GUI (opt-in extra, ADR-0008) ``` Then try the CLI — `lexora --help` for the nine subcommands, all documented in [docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md](docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md): ```bash lexora doctor # install health, incl. a live round-trip self-test printf 'alpha\r\nbeta\r\n' > in.txt lexora canon --in in.txt --out canon.txt lexora pack --in canon.txt --out a.lxz # default zstd level 9 (ADR-0012) lexora verify --in a.lxz # audit: structure + every block's SHA-256 lexora inspect --in a.lxz --verify # readable summary + accounting identity lexora unpack --in a.lxz --out back.txt lexora batch --in DIR --out-dir OUT --op canon # a whole tree, per-file JSON report ``` The GUI launcher `lexora-gui` requires the `[gui]` extra and exits 2 with guidance without it. ## Build & test commands Verified in-container (2026-10-29): ```bash python3 -m pytest -q # 492 passed, 1 skipped (~30 s; includes fuzz + interruption suites) QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen python3 -m pytest -q # same, incl. offscreen GUI widget tests (needs pyside6 + libegl1) python3 scripts/linkcheck.py # docs integrity gate — ALL INTERNAL LINKS OK ``` ## Benchmarks **LEXORA has now been measured against both frozen baselines — at smoke scope, not verdict scope.** The acceptance gates are defined in the blueprint (Pass ≥ 10%, Partial ≥ 3% smaller total stored size vs. the best frozen baseline) and formalized in `docs/BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md`. R4, three splits, 172 files / 78.6 MiB, 3 reps (draft, awaiting owner review): | system | ratio | |---|---| | `lexora` (shipped default, level 9) | 0.3352 | | `lexora19` | **0.3090** | | `zstd19` (baseline) | 0.3109 | | `xz9` (baseline) | **0.3068** | So the pipeline sits **between** the two baselines: a small, consistent advantage over zstd-19 (167 of 172 files smaller) and a small, consistent deficit against xz-9 (xz wins every file). **Neither is a gate verdict**: the corpus now meets the ≥1 GiB requirement but no protocol-scope run has been done, and the honest reading is in [docs/R4_SMOKE_DRAFT.md](docs/R4_SMOKE_DRAFT.md). Reproduce it from [benchmarks/README.md](benchmarks/README.md). ## Security & privacy notes - No security guarantees are claimed and no formal review has been performed. - **What is tested:** deterministic fuzz suites throw truncations, byte flips, end-drops and random blobs at seven reader entry points and assert that every mutant either decodes to the original bytes or raises `ContainerError` — never another exception and never a wrong answer; the reader enforces absolute limits (LIM-01/LIM-02) rather than trusting a header's declared caps; the atomic-write guarantee is verified against real SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGKILL. - Design intent: decoders enforce resource limits (bounded blocks, memory caps) to survive hostile archives; sensitive/clinical corpora must not train shared dictionaries by default. - Vulnerability reporting instructions live in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Documentation index - [docs/RELEASE_NOTES.md](docs/RELEASE_NOTES.md) — what this unreleased tree contains, its limits, and what a release would need - [benchmarks/README.md](benchmarks/README.md) — reproduce every measurement from a clean checkout - [docs/R4_SMOKE_DRAFT.md](docs/R4_SMOKE_DRAFT.md) — LEXORA vs both baselines, and what the numbers do not say - [docs/DEPENDENCY_LICENCE_REVIEW.md](docs/DEPENDENCY_LICENCE_REVIEW.md) — third-party obligations under PolyForm Start at **[docs/index.md](docs/index.md)**.
