# 🔒 LockHTML ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Turn any file into a PIN-protected document — optionally viewable only once.** AES-256-GCM · PIN-protected · one-time view · cross-platform · offline · nothing leaves your device. [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/drsamonline/lockhtml?style=for-the-badge&logo=github&color=22d3ee&labelColor=0a1024)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml/stargazers) [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=0a1024)](LICENSE) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/lockhtml?style=for-the-badge&color=22d3ee&labelColor=0a1024)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml/releases) [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyPI-not%20published-lightgrey?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=0a1024)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20Linux%20%7C%20macOS-22d3ee?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=0a1024)](#) [![CLI + GUI](https://img.shields.io/badge/interface-CLI%20%2B%20GUI-22d3ee?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=0a1024)](#) ### 🌐 [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/lockhtml/)  •  🚀 [Live demo — open the app](https://drsamonline.github.io/lockhtml/play/)  •  🧭 [All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/) **Download:** [Windows (.exe)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml/releases/latest/download/lockhtml-portable.exe)  ·  [Android (.apk)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml/releases/latest/download/lockhtml.apk)
--- **LockHTML** takes an ordinary file — an HTML page, a PDF, a photo, anything — encrypts it with a key derived from a PIN, and gives you back a single self-contained `.html` file. Anyone who opens it is asked for the PIN; enter it and the document appears. Choose **one-time view** (or a view limit, or an expiry date) and it stops opening once the conditions are met. No server. No accounts. No uploads. The locked file is a normal web page you can email, message or put on a USB stick — and the GUI works **offline** once loaded. ## ✨ Features - 🔐 **Argon2id** (memory-hard) by default, with **PBKDF2-SHA256** as a lighter alternative. - 🔑 **Recipient mode (X25519)** — lock a file to someone's *public key* so only they can open it, with no shared secret; add a PIN on top if you want two factors. - 🕳️ **Hidden volume** — a second PIN that opens entirely different content, so the file has a plausible cover story. - 🎛️ **Auto-calibrated KDF** — `--auto-kdf` times this machine and picks the strongest Argon2id cost that still unlocks quickly. - 🐢 **Constant-memory save** — for large streaming files, decrypt straight to disk chunk-by-chunk (Chromium), instead of building the whole file in memory. - 🔄 **age interop** — read and write ordinary [age](https://age-encryption.org/v1) files (X25519 recipients), so you can open a file the `age` tool encrypted and vice versa. - 🧩 **Shamir secret sharing** — split the key into *n* shares so any *k* holders (and no fewer) can open it. Give five people a share; any three can open it. - 🧂 **Keyfile support** — optionally require a second file in addition to the PIN. - ✍️ **Ed25519 signing** — sign a locked file so recipients can verify it came from you and wasn't altered. - 🎭 **Duress PIN** — a second PIN that opens a harmless decoy document instead. - 👁️ **View limits** — one-time, *N* views, a "do not open before" time, and an expiry time. - 💧 **Watermarking** — overlay recipient-specific text to trace a leaked copy. - 📦 **Any file type** — HTML renders inline; everything else is offered as a download. - 🗂️ **Two containers** — a single self-contained file for documents, or a chunked **streaming bundle** for very large files (video, disk images) at constant memory. See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md). - 🌐 **Browser GUI** — a single self-contained HTML file, installable as a PWA, fully offline. - 🖥️ **Cross-platform CLI** — one command on Windows, Linux and macOS. - 🔁 **Reversible** — `lockhtml unlock` recovers the original with the PIN. - 🌍 **Localised viewer** — English, हिन्दी and ગુજરાતી unlock screens. - 🧩 **Zero runtime for the recipient** — any modern browser opens a locked file. ## 🚀 Quick start ### GUI (no install) Open the live app → **** — or run it locally with the CLI. Drag in your file, set a PIN, download the locked copy. It works offline after the first load. ### CLI ```bash pip install lockhtml ``` ```bash # Lock one file with a PIN lockhtml lock report.html --pin 4821 # One-time view, Argon2id, with a watermark lockhtml lock report.html --pin 4821 --one-time --watermark "For A. Sharma" # Expire it and cap the views lockhtml lock plan.pdf --pin 4821 --max-views 3 --expires 2026-12-31T00:00:00Z # Require a keyfile as a second factor lockhtml lock report.html --pin 4821 --keyfile team.key # Sign it so the recipient can verify authenticity lockhtml keygen -o sign.pem lockhtml lock report.html --pin 4821 --sign sign.pem # Lock to a person's public key (no shared secret) lockhtml keygen --type x25519 -o alice.pem # writes alice.pem + alice.pub lockhtml lock report.html --to alice.pub -o report.locked.html lockhtml unlock report.locked.html --key alice.pem # Add a duress PIN that opens a decoy page lockhtml lock report.html --pin 4821 --decoy-pin 0000 # Split the key: 5 shares, any 3 open it lockhtml lock report.html --shares 5:3 lockhtml unlock report.locked.html --shares report.locked.shares.txt # Hide the real file behind a cover, and tune the KDF to this machine lockhtml lock cover.html --pin 4821 --hidden-pin 0000 --hidden-file real.html --auto-kdf lockhtml unlock cover.locked.html --pin 0000 # opens the hidden content # Lock a whole folder lockhtml lock ./contracts --recursive --pin 4821 --outdir ./locked # Read and write standard age files (interoperates with the `age` tool) lockhtml keygen --type age -o key.txt lockhtml age-encrypt report.pdf -r age1abc… lockhtml age-decrypt report.pdf.age -i key.txt -o report.pdf # Large file: streaming container (viewer + sidecar .bin, constant memory) lockhtml lock holiday.mp4 --pin 4821 --stream # Recover the original lockhtml unlock report.locked.html --pin 4821 -o report.html # Open the browser GUI lockhtml gui ``` > **Tip:** share the PIN (and keyfile) over a *different* channel than the file. ## 🖥️ The GUI One self-contained HTML file (`lockhtml/gui/index.html`) — no server, no build step, works offline: - **Lock tab** — drop in any files, set a PIN (or generate a passphrase), and use the advanced panel for the KDF, view limits, expiry, watermark, keyfile and duress PIN. - **Unlock / Verify tab** — open a locked file with its PIN to preview and recover it. Because it's plain HTML + Web Crypto (+ a bundled Argon2 WASM), it runs identically in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari and on Windows, Linux, macOS, Android and iOS. The hosted copy is a **PWA** — installable, and cached for offline use. ## 📸 Screenshots
**The GUI — every option, straight from your browser**

**A locked file asks for the PIN before revealing anything**
## 🔬 How it works 1. Your file is encrypted with **AES-256-GCM**. 2. The key is derived from your PIN with **Argon2id** (or PBKDF2-SHA256) and a random 16-byte salt. 3. If a **keyfile** is used, it is mixed in as a pepper (a post-KDF HMAC), so the PIN alone is not enough. 4. If you **sign**, an Ed25519 signature over the ciphertext is embedded with your public key. 5. The salt, IV and ciphertext are embedded as JSON inside a small *viewer* page. 6. Opening the file runs the viewer, which asks for the PIN and decrypts **in the browser**. The plaintext never leaves the device. ``` locked.html = viewer shell + { kdf, params, salt, iv, AES-256-GCM(ciphertext), limits, watermark, sig } ``` The full format is documented in [`docs/FORMAT.md`](docs/FORMAT.md). The CLI (Python) and the GUI (JavaScript) implement the same format, so files lock and unlock interchangeably across both — enforced by CI on every push. ### 🔑 Recipient mode Instead of a shared PIN you can lock a file to someone's **X25519 public key**, so only the holder of the matching private key can open it. A fresh ephemeral keypair is generated per file, the ECDH secret goes through HKDF-SHA256, and the result encrypts the file with AES-256-GCM. Because the shared secret is already 256 bits of entropy, no slow KDF is applied on top — and you can still layer a PIN (and a keyfile) on top for two factors. It works in the streaming container too. ```bash lockhtml keygen --type x25519 -o alice.pem # private (keep) + alice.pub (hand out) lockhtml lock big.mp4 --to alice.pub --stream ``` ### 🔄 age interop LockHTML reads and writes standard [age](https://age-encryption.org/v1) files, so it interoperates with the `age` tool. Supported: the v1 header and its MAC, `X25519` recipients and identities, the 64 KiB STREAM payload, and multiple recipients per file. Not supported: `scrypt` passphrases, the ML-KEM hybrid and P-256 tagged recipients, and ASCII armor. ```bash lockhtml keygen --type age -o key.txt # an age identity; prints the recipient lockhtml age-encrypt report.pdf -r age1abc… # -> report.pdf.age lockhtml age-decrypt report.pdf.age -i key.txt -o report.pdf ``` age uses ChaCha20-Poly1305, which Web Crypto does not expose, so this is **CLI-only** — the HTML viewer and GUI cannot open age files. Interoperability is verified against the reference implementation in both directions; see [docs/AGE.md](docs/AGE.md). ### 🧩 Shamir secret sharing Split a file's key so that any *k* of *n* holders can open it and no fewer can. A random 32-byte seed is split with Shamir's scheme over **GF(256)**; the seed feeds HKDF-SHA256 to produce the AES key. The shares are written to a `.shares.txt` file that you distribute **separately** — the locked file alone cannot be opened. It works in the streaming container and can be combined with a PIN and a keyfile. ```bash lockhtml lock report.html --shares 5:3 # writes report.locked.html + report.locked.shares.txt lockhtml unlock report.locked.html --shares some-three.txt lockhtml unlock report.locked.html --share --share --share ``` ### 🚀 Launchers (no install needed) The repo ships small launcher scripts that run the CLI straight from the checkout — handy on a machine where you have not `pip install`ed anything: | Platform | CLI | GUI | | --- | --- | --- | | Linux / macOS | `./lockhtml.sh …` (or `sh lockhtml.sh …`) | `./gui.sh` | | Windows | `lockhtml.bat …` | `gui.bat` | They find Python 3.9+, prefer a local `.venv`, check the two dependencies, and give a clear message if something is missing. On Windows the `.bat` files are directly runnable; on Unix, mark them executable once with `chmod +x lockhtml.sh gui.sh` (or just run them through `sh`). ### 🕳️ Hidden volume A locked file can carry more than one payload. The **cover** content opens with the main PIN, and a second PIN opens **hidden** content — different bytes entirely, with no indication in the file that it exists. This is the same idea as the duress PIN, generalised: you can add several hidden slots. ```bash lockhtml lock cover.html --pin 4821 --hidden-pin 0000 --hidden-file real.html ``` A hidden volume is **plausible deniability, not proof of absence**: someone who knows the format can see that extra encrypted slots exist, they just cannot read them. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ### 📦 Containers and size limits The default **embedded** container puts the ciphertext inside the HTML as base64. That is the most convenient form — one file the recipient can just open — but memory use is roughly **3–4× the file size**, so it is comfortable to about 50 MB and breaks somewhere around 250–300 MB (the browser's single-string limit is ~512 MB, and base64 inflates by 33%). For bigger files use `--stream`, which writes the ciphertext to a sidecar `.bin` in fixed-size chunks. Reading and decryption then cost **~O(chunk size)** instead of O(file size), so multi-gigabyte files work. The trade-off is that the recipient receives **two files**. | | Embedded (default) | Streaming (`--stream`) | | --- | --- | --- | | Files the recipient gets | 1 | 2 (`.html` + `.bin`) | | Practical size ceiling | ~250–300 MB | Limited by disk | | Memory to encrypt/decrypt | ~3.7× file size | ~O(chunk size) | | Size overhead | ≈33% (base64) | ≈16 bytes per chunk | Neither mode touches the network — "streaming" here means *memory*, not the internet. Full reasoning, the memory arithmetic and the chunk format are in **[docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md)**. ## 🛡️ Security model — read this **The PIN (and keyfile) gives you real encryption.** Without them the file is unreadable even if someone opens it in a text editor. Wrong PINs are rejected cryptographically (AES-GCM authentication), not by a string comparison. Signatures are verified before the content is shown. **The view limits, watermark and one-time view are browser-enforced deterrents, not server guarantees.** Since there is no server, the view counter lives in the browser's IndexedDB. A determined recipient can copy the file first, use another browser or profile, clear their storage, or screenshot the decrypted page. These features stop casual re-sharing and help you trace a leak; they are not a hard guarantee. **This is not a substitute for end-to-end tools** when the stakes are high (medical records, credentials, legal documents). Once a recipient decrypts, the content is on their screen and in their memory. For genuinely enforced single-view delivery, use a server that deletes the document after the first fetch. | Property | Guarantee | | --- | --- | | Content unreadable without PIN | ✅ Strong (AES-256-GCM + Argon2id) | | Content unreadable without the private key | ✅ Strong (X25519 + HKDF) | | Content unreadable with fewer than k shares | ✅ Strong (Shamir over GF(256)) | | Wrong PIN rejected | ✅ Strong (authenticated encryption) | | Keyfile required as a second factor | ✅ Strong (pepper) | | Authenticity (sender identity) | ✅ Strong when signed (Ed25519) | | Works offline / no upload | ✅ Yes | | Truly view-once / expiry | ⚠️ Best-effort (client-side) | | Survives a determined recipient | ❌ No | See [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) and the self-audit in [`docs/AUDIT.md`](docs/AUDIT.md). ## 📂 Project layout ``` lockhtml/ ├── lockhtml/ │ ├── core.py # crypto + payload format v2 │ ├── cli.py # command-line interface │ ├── templates/ │ │ ├── viewer.src.html # viewer source (generated files below) │ │ ├── viewer.html # PBKDF2-only viewer (small) │ │ └── viewer-argon2.html # viewer with Argon2id WASM inlined │ └── gui/ │ ├── app.html # GUI source │ ├── index.html # generated, self-contained GUI │ ├── manifest.webmanifest, sw.js, icon.svg # PWA ├── tools/ │ ├── build.py # builds the viewer variants + GUI │ ├── minify.mjs # minifies the generated assets │ ├── check_gui_compat.mjs # cross-implementation check (run in CI) │ ├── e2e_fixtures.py # builds fixtures for the browser test │ ├── e2e_browser.mjs # end-to-end browser test (embedded + streaming) │ ├── e2e_gui.mjs # locks files with the GUI code path │ └── e2e_gui_verify.py # verifies those with the Python core ├── docs/ # design notes, format spec, audit ├── tests/ # crypto + CLI tests ├── examples/ # sample.html and its locked twin └── .github/workflows/ # CI + GitHub Pages deploy ``` ## 🤝 Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Planned work lives in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml cd lockhtml pip install -e ".[dev]" npm install # build tooling: minifier + Argon2 WASM make test # run the test suite make build # regenerate + minify the GUI and viewers ``` ## 📜 License [PolyForm Noncommercial](LICENSE) © Dr Sohil Momin

# ml-kit [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32)](LICENSE) **The classic algorithms, from scratch — for offline features.** tf-idf · Naive Bayes · k-NN · k-means · PCA · ID3 · linear regression · Markov chains · grammar A single file, zero dependencies, no model, no API key, no network. MIT.
--- ## THE BOUNDARY — read this first This kit is for **ranking, similarity, clustering and simple trend**. It is **NOT a diagnostic or predictive engine**, and **nothing in it may be used to claim a clinical or medical capability.** Several apps that use this kit are clinical; the algorithms here are generic maths and make no clinical claim. A model that ranks notes, groups similar cases or draws a trend line is not a diagnosis, and must never be presented as one. ## Why from scratch Forge's rule is offline, single-file, zero-dependency — so the usual ML frameworks (TensorFlow, Spark, scikit-learn) are unusable: they are hundreds of megabytes and need a runtime. But the algorithms that actually earn their place offline are the *classic* ones, and each fits in tens of lines. This is the light half of Forge's AI story: **heavy AI uses the user's own key; light AI runs on the device, from scratch.** ## What's in it | Algorithm | For | |---|---| | `tfidf` + `search` | ranked text search (tf-idf weighting, cosine similarity) | | `NaiveBayes` | a tiny bag-of-words classifier (tag a note, categorise an entry) | | `knn` | "items like this one" | | `kmeans` | clustering | | `pca2` | reduce many dimensions to two, for plotting | | `id3` + `predict` | a small, readable rules classifier | | `linearRegression` | a trend line | | `markov` + `generate` | statistical generation from a corpus (char- or word-level) | | `grammar` | rule-based generation: rules, slots, weighted alternatives | Plus `rng(seed)` — a seedable RNG, so a sampled start or a generated sentence is reproducible. ## Usage ```js var ML = require("./ml-kit.js"); // Node; in a browser it is window.MLKit // Ranked search var index = ML.tfidf(["the cat sat on the mat", "dogs bark and cats meow"]); ML.search(index, "cat"); // -> [{ i: 0, score: ... }] // Classify var nb = ML.NaiveBayes().train([ { text: "good product", label: "pos" }, { text: "terrible waste", label: "neg" } ]); nb.classify("excellent product"); // -> "pos" // A trend line ML.linearRegression([0, 1, 2, 3], [1, 3, 5, 7]).slope; // -> 2 // Reproducible generation var m = ML.markov(corpus, { order: 2, word: true }); ML.generate(m, { seed: 42, length: 12 }); // same seed -> same text ``` ## Tests ``` node test-node.js ``` A known tf-idf ranking case, a Naive Bayes classification case, a k-means convergence case, a regression line against a known slope, PCA, k-NN, ID3, and seeded-reproducibility checks for the Markov chain and the grammar. CI runs it on every push. ## Design notes - **Every algorithm is reimplemented from the idea**, not copied. Where a survey suggested a reference, only the shape was taken — the code is ours. - **Deterministic where it matters.** k-means seeds from the first *k* points; Markov and the grammar take a seed, so the same seed gives the same output. - **Small and readable.** Tens of lines each, so the maths can be read and checked. - **UMD.** `module.exports` in Node, `MLKit` in a browser — the same shape as the other kits. ## License PolyForm Noncommercial — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). © 2026 Dr Sohil Momin.

--- ## What it is **Mnemosyne Companion** is the companion application to the book **_Mnemosyne Materia Medica: A Memory-Optimised Clinical Guide to 100 Polycrest Homoeopathic Remedies_** by **Dr. Sohil Momin**. The book teaches the method; this app is the practice bench. It carries the study material of all one hundred remedies — their poetic pearls, keynotes, modalities, differentials and miasmatic groupings — and turns them into an active-recall drill with a spaced-repetition schedule. It is deliberately **not** the full book: the clinical descriptions and case histories stay in the text. This is the helper you keep open while you study. > The remedy that surfaces in three seconds is worth ten times the remedy that emerges after twenty minutes. ## Screenshots | Home | Quick reference | |:---:|:---:| | ![Home](assets/screenshot-home.png) | ![Quick reference](assets/screenshot-remedies.png) | | Remedy card | Diagrams | |:---:|:---:| | ![Remedy card](assets/screenshot-card.png) | ![Diagrams](assets/screenshot-diagrams.png) | | Study drill | On a phone | |:---:|:---:| | ![Study](assets/screenshot-study.png) | ![Mobile](assets/screenshot-mobile.png) | ## What it contains - **All 100 remedies** — number, name, family, kingdom (plant / mineral / animal / nosode), and miasmatic group where the book classifies one. - **Eight keynotes per remedy** — the strange, rare and peculiar symptoms that name the picture. - **The Poetic Pearl** for every remedy — the four-line verse that fixes its emotional essence. - **A retrieval trigger** — the few words meant to summon the whole picture. - **Modalities** — the better and worse that seal the choice. - **Differentials** — how each remedy separates from its nearest competitors. ## Features | | | |---|---| | 🔎 **Quick reference** | Search all 100 pictures by symptom, keynote or pearl; filter by kingdom and by miasm. | | 🃏 **Spaced repetition** | Flashcards in three modes — Pearl → Remedy, Keynotes → Remedy, Remedy → Keynotes — graded Again / Hard / Good / Easy on a 1, 3, 7, 21, 45-day schedule. | | 📈 **Progress** | Started, due-now and mastered counts, with a progress ring. Saved locally in your browser. | | 🖼️ **Six SVG diagrams** | The four-phase study cycle, the forgetting curve, the four principles of retention, the C and LM potency scales, the miasmatic tree, and the memory palace. | | ⏱️ **Protocol timer** | A session timer that walks the encode → recall → integrate → master cycle. | | 📖 **Guide** | The method, the field guide to a remedy card, a short posology note, and the safety frame. | | 🌗 **Light and dark** | A one-tap theme toggle. | | 🔗 **Deep links** | `#remedies`, `#study`, `#diagrams`, `#guide` open straight to a view. | ## Getting started **Use it online.** Open **[drsamonline.github.io/mnemosyne-companion/play/](https://drsamonline.github.io/mnemosyne-companion/play/)** — nothing to install. **Use it offline.** Download [`dist/Mnemosyne_Companion.html`](dist/Mnemosyne_Companion.html) and open it in any browser. # MusicGen

**A pocket generative composer.** One tap makes a finished-sounding track — harmony, melody, drums, mix and master — from six presets and a 12-character seed. No accounts, no server, no samples. It runs entirely in your browser, offline.

[![tests](https://github.com/drsamonline/musicgen/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/musicgen/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-c6f24e.svg)](LICENSE)
[![dependencies: 0](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-0-9aa8ff.svg)](
[![size: 43 KB gzipped](https://img.shields.io/badge/size-43%20KB%20gzipped-9aa8ff.svg)](
[![PWA: offline-first](https://img.shields.io/badge/PWA-offline--first-c6f24e.svg)](
[![web audio api](https://img.shields.io/badge/web%20audio-api-ff9f6b.svg)](

**[▶ Live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/musicgen/)** · **[Open the studio](https://drsamonline.github.io/musicgen/app/)** · **[Releases](https://github.com/drsamonline/musicgen/releases)**

![The MusicGen landing page, with a live specimen of a generated song](docs/screenshots/landing-desktop.png)

---

## What it is

A generative composer that behaves like an instrument rather than a toy. Every song is a **pure function of `(presets, seed)`**: the same inputs produce a byte-identical song, so a link is a recording. Random is sampled through a compatibility table so it stays musical, and every note is checked against the key and the chord sounding under it.

The whole thing is vanilla ES modules and the Web Audio API — no framework, no build step, no audio files, no network requests at runtime.

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Studio, mobile](docs/screenshots/studio-mobile.png) | ![Studio, desktop](docs/screenshots/studio-desktop.png) |
| *Studio on a phone — piano roll, chord labels, section timeline* | *Desktop — spectrum view, live transport* |
| ![Waveform view](docs/screenshots/studio-spectrum.png) | ![Generated cover art](docs/screenshots/cover-art.png) |
| *Waveform visualiser* | *Cover art, generated from the song's own data* |

## Try it

```bash
git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/musicgen
cd musicgen/app
python3 -m http.server 8080
# → http://localhost:8080
```

Then use your browser's **Install** / **Add to Home Screen** (iOS: Share → Add to Home Screen). The service worker precaches the whole shell, so after that first visit it launches and plays with the network switched off.

## What's inside

**The composer** — eleven stages, each testable: key and mode → harmonic grid (2nd-order Markov over style progressions, modal interchange) → voicing with a voice-leading solver → bass → drums (groove templates, Euclidean layers, phrase fills) → motif → development transforms → pad and counter-line → arp → humanise → tension curve.

**The presets** — 11 styles, 10 moods, 10 themes, 8 song types, 7 synthesis technologies, plus a compatibility table that maps styles to allowed moods and engines.

**The synthesis** — subtractive, FM, chiptune (real `PeriodicWave` pulses), additive, wavetable, Karplus-Strong and noise instruments; a drum kit built from oscillators and filtered noise; generated convolution reverb, tempo-synced delay and chorus; glue compressor and limiter on the master. Voice cap with stealing, 25 ms lookahead scheduler.

**The exports** — WAV (16/24/32-bit, normalised to the style's LUFS target under a −1 dBTP ceiling), per-track stems as a zip, Type-1 MIDI, 1024 px cover art, and seed links that reproduce the exact song elsewhere.

**The platform bits** — installable PWA, MediaSession metadata with generated artwork, screen Wake Lock during playback, keyboard shortcuts throughout, `prefers-reduced-motion` and `prefers-color-scheme` support, and a strict CSP (`default-src 'self'`) with zero runtime fetches.

## Tests

```bash
npm test              # 24 unit tests, no browser needed
npm run test:browser  # 38 tests in real Chromium with real Web Audio
npm run shots         # regenerate docs/screenshots
```

The suite asserts, rather than claims:

- determinism — the composer run 100× on the same seed, diffed
- musicality — 330 style × mood × seed cases through the theory validator
- audio — an offline render measured for silence, clipping and LUFS against the style target
- exports — WAV byte length, MIDI header and track count, zip archive structure
- the app — service worker caching the shell, visualiser modes painting, stems quieter than the mix
- the landing page — composing, drawing and linking its specimen

## Architecture

```
index.html            landing page (its own live specimen)
landing.css landing.js
app/                  the PWA
  index.html styles.css manifest.webmanifest sw.js icons/
  src/core/           rng algorithms theory voicing motif composer validate
  src/presets/        styles moods themes types techs compatibility
  src/audio/          engine instruments drums fx mastering lufs
  src/export/         wav midi zip artwork
  src/visual/         pianoRoll (+ bars, waveform, generative art)
  src/state.js        src/main.js
  qa/matrix.html      listening matrix (dev only)
tests/unit/ tests/browser/
scripts/screenshots.mjs
```

## Design notes

Three decisions are worth knowing about, because they were made against the obvious choice:

**The validator accepts chromatic notes when the chord owns them.** An absolute "everything in the key" rule would reject the modal interchange and borrowed chords that make the harmony interesting. The rule is *in key **or** a tone of the chord sounding at that moment*.

**Loudness targets are per style.** Lo-fi sits at −16 LUFS, EDM at −11, Ambient at −18. Normalising everything to a single streaming number would flatten exactly the character the styles are for; the export normalises to each style's own target instead.

**No AudioWorklets in v1.** Granular and physical-modelling worklets are where a generative-audio project goes to die. Everything here uses native nodes, which is why it runs on a mid-range phone and why the whole app is 43 KB gzipped.

## Known gaps

Stems are summed from one shared gain rather than re-mixed per track; there is no undo across *generations* (only across preset changes); sidechain pumping exists in the style data but is not wired into the graph; the library stores presets and metadata rather than note data, so a saved song recomposes from its seed; MIDI import, microtuning and a protocol handler are not implemented.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Music you generate with it is yours.

This one asks you to **position**. The gun is fully automatic and picks its own targets, so the only decisions left are spatial ones: how close do you dare stand, when do you break line of sight, when do you spend your slide, when do you jump and when do you duck. Every mechanic below exists to make those decisions interesting rather than to add buttons. - **Three controls.** Left, right, jump, duck. That is it. There is no fire button, and there never will be. - **Range is a resource.** Your gun only fires when something is inside its circle, so damage output is a function of positioning. - **Heat punishes camping.** Firing builds heat, and heat only cools when *nothing is in range*. # Neon Velocity

**Play in the browser:** <https://drsamonline.github.io/neon-velocity/play/> — it
installs as an app (PWA) and works offline after the first load.
**Landing page:** <https://drsamonline.github.io/neon-velocity/>

![Gameplay](site/assets/shots/action.jpg)

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Boss fight](site/assets/shots/boss.jpg) | ![Swarm](site/assets/shots/swarm.jpg) |
| The Core Interceptor, first of four bosses | Drone formations converging |
| ![Title screen](site/assets/shots/menu.jpg) | ![Pause menu](site/assets/shots/pause.jpg) |
| Title screen, difficulty select | Pause menu |

A retro side-scrolling shooter for **Godot 4.3** where every sprite and every
sound is generated at runtime. The repository contains no binary assets at all:
no PNGs, no OGGs, no fonts — just GDScript, three shaders and two scene files.

```
godot --path .          # or open the folder in the Godot 4.3 editor and press F5
```

There is also a **web build that installs as an app** (PWA) — see
[Play in a browser](#play-in-a-browser-pwa).

## Controls

| Action | Keys |
|--------|------|
| Move | `WASD` / arrow keys |
| Fire | `Z` or left mouse button |
| Dash (brief invulnerability) | `Space` / `Shift` |
| Switch weapon | `Q` / `E` |
| Pause | `Esc` |

On a phone or tablet the game draws its own controls: drag anywhere on the left
half to fly, `FIRE` and `DASH` sit under the right thumb, and `WPN` / pause are
in the top-right corner. Turn the device to landscape — portrait shows a
"rotate your device" screen. On the web build the first tap also asks for
fullscreen and a landscape lock.

## Play in a browser (PWA)

The project exports to Web, and the export is patched into a real installable
PWA: manifest, icons, service worker, offline page. It is single-threaded, so it
does **not** need `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` / `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy`
headers and will run on any static host, including GitHub Pages, Netlify,
Cloudflare Pages and itch.io.

```bash
godot --headless --path . --export-release "Web" build/web/index.html
python3 tools/pwa_post_export.py build/web

# local preview (service workers need http, not file://)
python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory build/web
# then open http://localhost:8000
```

The first load pulls a ~35 MB wasm bundle; after that the service worker serves
it from cache and the game starts instantly, including offline. Install it from
the browser's address bar ("Install") to get a standalone window and an icon.

Two things to know: a **keyboard is required** (there are no touch controls),
and the page must be served over **HTTPS or localhost** — service workers are
refused on plain `http://` origins.

`tools/pwa_post_export.py` does two things the raw export does not: it registers
the service worker (Godot only does that for thread-enabled builds) and it
prunes the worker's precache list, which otherwise lists `index.worker.js` in
thread-less builds — one 404 there makes `cache.addAll()` reject and silently
kills offline support.

## What is in the game

- **Six weapons** — plasma cannon, spread shot, laser lance, seeker missiles,
  railgun, nova burst. Each has five levels and gains XP from kills.
- **18 mods** — stat modifiers and named effects (chain lightning, ricochet,
  life siphon, MIRV split, EMP slow, multi-pulse nova). Picking up a mod card
  pauses the run and offers three choices.
- **Endless procedural levels** — the world is a strip of 2400-unit chunks,
  each generated from `run_seed + chunk_index`, so a seed always replays the
  same run.
- **Four bosses** on a five-chunk cycle, each with its own attack patterns and
  a phase change every quarter of its health.
- **Full loop** — title screen, difficulty select, HUD, pause menu, settings,
  run summary with accuracy and best score, local save file.
- **Adaptive music** — four synthesised layers (bass, lead, pad, drums) that
  fade in as you get deeper into a run, plus 24 procedural sound effects.

## How the "zero assets" trick works

| Thing | Where it comes from |
|-------|---------------------|
| Sprites | `scripts/core/Art.gd` rasterises every image with the `Image` API from a fixed 16-colour palette, then wraps it in an `ImageTexture` |
| Sound effects | `scripts/core/AudioManager.gd` synthesises PCM float buffers (FM, sweeps, noise, arpeggios) and packs them into `AudioStreamWAV` |
| Music | The same file builds four 6.857 s loops at 140 BPM and crossfades them |
| Level art | Starfield, nebula and mountain silhouettes are generated once and tiled by `ParallaxBackground` |

Audio generation takes roughly half a second at startup on a modest laptop, all
of it before the title screen appears.

## Project layout

```
scripts/
  core/        EventBus, SaveSystem, Art (sprites), AudioManager, ObjectPool
  systems/     WeaponSystem, LevelManager, GameManager, ReplaySystem
  entities/    Player, Bullet, Powerup
  enemies/     DroneEnemy, CoreBoss
  effects/     Spark, Explosion
  ui/          HUD, MainMenu, SettingsMenu, PauseMenu, ModSelect, GameOverScreen
  tools/       test_runner (headless smoke test), dump_sprites (art previews)
scenes/        Main, MainMenu, SettingsMenu, TestRunner, tools/{DumpSprites,SoakTest}
shaders/       crt_palette_combined, player_glow, palette_shift
web/           PWA icons + offline page (inputs to the web export)
tools/         pwa_post_export.py, ci_install_godot.sh
docs/          SPEC.md (the original brief), REVIEW.md (audit of that brief)
```

## Testing

```bash
# headless smoke test: boots Main, plays 7 seconds of synthetic input, asserts 27 things
godot --headless --path . res://scenes/TestRunner.tscn

# 50-second soak run: chunk streaming, pooling and the first boss fight
godot --headless --path . res://scenes/tools/SoakTest.tscn

# dump every generated sprite to art_preview/ for inspection
godot --headless --path . res://scenes/tools/DumpSprites.tscn
```

The test runner exits non-zero on failure, so CI can gate on it.

## Builds and releases

`export_presets.cfg` defines four presets: Web, Linux, Windows and macOS.
Export templates must be installed first (Editor → Manage Export Templates).

```bash
godot --headless --path . --export-release "Linux/X11"      build/linux/NeonVelocity.x86_64
godot --headless --path . --export-release "Windows Desktop" build/windows/NeonVelocity.exe
godot --headless --path . --export-release "macOS"          build/macos/NeonVelocity.zip
godot --headless --path . --export-release "Web"            build/web/index.html
```

Everything is automated in `.github/workflows/build.yml`:

| Trigger | What happens |
|---------|--------------|
| any push / PR | headless smoke test + 50-second soak test |
| push to `main` | the above, then the Web build is patched into a PWA and deployed to GitHub Pages |
| `v*` tag | the above, then Linux, Windows, macOS and Web are exported and attached to a GitHub release |
| manual dispatch | same as a tag, without publishing a release |

So shipping a new version is `git tag v1.1.0 && git push --tags`.

Note on Pages: GitHub Pages needs a **public** repository on the free plan, so
the Pages job is opt-in. To turn it on, make the repository public, enable Pages
with "GitHub Actions" as the source, then set a repository variable
`ENABLE_PAGES=true` (Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> Variables).
Every push to `main` will then publish the PWA. Until then, take
`neon-velocity-web.zip` from the release and drop the unzipped folder on any
static host — Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, itch.io and GitHub Pages all work,
because the build needs no special headers.

## Saves and replays

Settings live in `user://settings.cfg`, the last run and lifetime stats in
`user://save_game.save` (JSON, XOR-obfuscated — not encrypted, and not meant to
be), and recorded inputs in `user://replays/`.

Replays are **recorded, not yet playable**: each run writes a JSON file with the
seed, difficulty and three bytes of input per frame, which is everything needed
to re-simulate it, but no playback UI is wired up yet.

## Why it exists

The files people merge and split are usually the ones they should not hand to a stranger's server —
patient reports, contracts, statements, identity documents. Every "free PDF tool" online uploads
your file. This one cannot: it is a single HTML file with the PDF engine compiled into it, and there
is no backend to send anything to. Unplug the network and it still works.

## Features

| | |
|---|---|
| **Merge** | Add several PDFs; they lay out in order. Drag any page to reorder. |
| **Split / extract** | Select pages (shift-click for a range) and pull them into a new PDF. |
| **Rotate** | 90° steps, left or right, per page or for a whole selection. |
| **Reorder / duplicate / delete** | Drag and drop, or move selections earlier/later. |
| **Watermark** | Text, centre / tiled / corner, with size, opacity, angle and colour. |
| **Page numbers** | Four formats, four positions, starting number, size. |
| **Metadata** | Title, author, subject, keywords. |
| **Compress** | Renders each page to JPEG at a chosen DPI and quality, then rebuilds. |
| **Images → PDF** | PNG and JPEG, one image per page. |
| **Password protect** | AES-256, with user/owner passwords and permissions for printing, copying, modifying. |
| **Unlock** | Remove a password you already know, in the browser. |
| **Extract text** | From a digital PDF → `.txt`. |
| **OCR** | From a scan. Engine downloaded once (~7 MB) then cached; the document is never uploaded. |
| **Credits** | All bundled libraries credited in-app and in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`. |
| **Themes** | Dark, light, high-contrast. |
| **Shortcuts** | `a` select all · `d` deselect · `[` `]` rotate · `Delete` remove · `t` theme · `?` help |

## Not included, deliberately

- **PDF/A conversion** and **Ghostscript-class compression.** These need AGPL-licensed components
  (Ghostscript, PyMuPDF, CoherentPDF). Using them would force this app to be AGPL, which is
  incompatible with the licence below. Compress here means rasterise-and-rebuild, which is
  permissive and works well on scans.
- **Editing page content.** The toolkit rearranges and annotates pages; it does not edit text inside them.

## Files

```
app.html                     the whole application (one self-contained file, ~1.9 MB)
index.html                   landing page
docs/                        the same site, for a Pages source pointed at /docs
pipeline/app_template.html   the application source (readable)
pipeline/landing.html        the landing page source (readable)
pipeline/build_pdf.py        inlines the libraries + minifies, producing app.html
                             and both landing pages from the one source
```

`build_pdf.py` embeds **pdf-lib**, **pdf.js** and the pdf.js worker directly into the HTML and
minifies the app's own CSS/JS/HTML on the way out. The readable template stays in `pipeline/`.

## Privacy

Your documents are read into the browser's memory, processed on your own CPU, and written back to
your disk. Nothing is uploaded, stored or logged, and closing the tab discards everything.

# optical-kit

[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32)](LICENSE)

[![test](https://github.com/drsamonline/optical-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/optical-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml)


**The shared optical-transfer core for drsamonline apps.** One file, no build
step, no dependencies.

This is the transport logic behind the transfer apps (`helioprism`,
`blinkcode-ai`, `BLINKTRANSFER`), extracted once so it isn't re-implemented three
times:

- a **systematic LT fountain code** — the receiver needs *any* ~k frames, so a
  dropped frame costs time, never correctness (there is no back-channel to ask
  for a resend);
- **self-describing frames** — session, sequence, block count, block size, total
  length, and a CRC, so a receiver can lock onto a stream mid-flight;
- a **sender** and a **receiver** with progress;
- a **pluggable codec** — the app supplies the QR or colour-matrix renderer.

## Why a fountain code

A screen-to-camera (or speaker-to-mic) link has no way to ask for a retransmit,
and a camera *will* drop frames. Numbered frames then need the receiver to catch
every one — a coupon-collector problem. A fountain code needs only *enough*
frames, in any order, so a loss costs a little time and nothing else.

## API

```js
// send
const sender = Optical.Sender(dataBytes, { blockSize: 1400 });
sender.session; sender.k;                 // tell the receiver these first
const frame = sender.next();              // a Uint8Array; render it as a QR / matrix

// receive
const rx = Optical.Receiver(session, k, blockSize, totalLen);
rx.add(frameBytes);                       // returns progress 0..1
rx.progress();                            // 0..1
rx.result();                              // Uint8Array, or null until complete
```

Lower-level pieces: `Optical.Fountain` (encode/symbol), `Optical.Decoder`
(peeling), `Optical.Frame` (pack/unpack), `Optical.crc32`, `Optical.bytes`
(text/base64).

## Verified

`test-node.js` proves the round-trip, including dropped frames:

```
node test-node.js
PASS  1024B block=1400 loss=0%   k=1   overhead=1.00x
PASS  51200B block=1400 loss=0%  k=37  overhead=1.00x
PASS  51200B block=1400 loss=10% k=37  overhead=1.11x
PASS  51200B block=1400 loss=30% k=37  overhead=1.46x
PASS  204800B block=2000 loss=10% k=103 overhead=1.20x
PASS  524288B block=2000 loss=20% k=263 overhead=1.47x
PASS  10240B block=800 loss=15%  k=13  overhead=1.00x
7 passed, 0 failed
```

The browser demo (`demo/index.html`) runs the same round-trip in-page.

## Pluggable codec

`optical-kit` moves bytes; it does not draw them. The app renders each frame with
its own codec:

- **QR** — e.g. `zxing-wasm` / `jsQR`, one frame per code;
- **colour matrix** — a dense grid of colour cells;
- **multi-code grid** — several codes per displayed frame.

## Licence

MIT. (c) 2026 Dr Sohil Momin.

profile-kit: # profile-kit **A small, reusable kit for a theme-aware, self-updating GitHub profile.** [![Landing page](https://img.shields.io/badge/landing%20page-open-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/profile-kit/) [![All projects](https://img.shields.io/badge/All%20projects-hub-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/) [![Offline-first](https://img.shields.io/badge/offline--first-yes-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/drsamonline/profile-kit) [![Built with Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-Python-3572A5?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/drsamonline/profile-kit) [![Type: reusable kit](https://img.shields.io/badge/type-reusable%20kit-586069?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/profile-kit/) [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) **Landing page:**  ·  **All projects:** Lift it into your own `username/username` profile repo — by hand, or by handing this repository to an AI agent — and you get a profile page that: - renders the right artwork and stats card for **light and dark** GitHub themes, - keeps its **badge counts and project list current** from the GitHub API, on a daily schedule, without you editing the README, - stays **self-contained and offline-first**: inline SVG, no external JS, no build step, no service to sign up for. Built and maintained by [Dr. Sohil Momin](https://github.com/drsamonline) — see **[All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/)**. --- ## The three ideas it combines 1. **A theme-aware hero.** A hand-drawn SVG banner served through `` with `media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"`, so GitHub shows the light artwork on a light theme and the dark artwork on a dark one — no JavaScript, just two committed files and the right markup. 2. **A metrics card, rendered twice.** [`lowlighter/metrics`](https://github.com/lowlighter/metrics) with the `classic` template, rendered once per theme into `assets/metrics-light.svg` and `assets/metrics-dark.svg`. Each render pins its own palette through the action's `extras_css` option, because metrics has no real light/dark switch (see the known limitation below). 3. **A self-updating README.** A small Python script regenerates the regions of the README that sit between HTML comment markers — a row of badge counts and a categorised project list — straight from the GitHub API, and a workflow commits the result daily. Everything outside the markers is left alone. Each idea stands on its own; you can take one, two, or all three. --- ## What's in the kit ``` README.md this file assets/hero-light.svg hero banner template (light) — edit the placeholders assets/hero-dark.svg hero banner template (dark) — edit the placeholders metrics.yml the metrics workflow — copy to .github/workflows/ profile-generator/ update_profile.py regenerates the marked README regions profile-data.json owner + markers + categories + curated repos update-profile.yml the workflow that runs it daily README.md how the generator works and how to configure it docs/ the kit's own landing page (GitHub Pages, served from /docs) ``` --- ## How to use it ### 1. Create your profile repo Create a public repo named exactly `username/username` (GitHub treats it as your profile README) and give it a `README.md`. ### 2. Add the hero Copy `assets/hero-light.svg` and `assets/hero-dark.svg` into your repo's `assets/` folder, then embed them in the README with a ``: ```html ``` **Editing the hero.** Both SVGs ship with three visible placeholders — `YOUR KICKER`, `YOUR NAME` and `YOUR TAGLINE` — plus the two-letter monogram `YN` in the corner circle. Open **both** files and replace those four strings in each, and update the `aria-label` / `` at the top of each file (they repeat the name and tagline for screen readers). Keep the two files byte-for-byte identical apart from their palette so the light and dark banners line up. ### 3. Add the metrics card Copy `metrics.yml` to `.github/workflows/metrics.yml`, replace `YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME` with your login, and run it once (Actions → *Metrics* → *Run workflow*). It commits the two SVGs to `assets/`. Embed them the same way as the hero: ```html <picture> <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="assets/metrics-dark.svg"> <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" srcset="assets/metrics-light.svg"> <img src="assets/metrics-light.svg" alt="GitHub metrics" width="480"> </picture> ``` Read the **Known limitation** below before you expect the languages panel to show anything. ### 4. Add the self-updating README regions - Copy `profile-generator/update_profile.py` to `.github/scripts/update_profile.py`. - Copy `profile-generator/profile-data.json` to `profile-data.json` at the repo root. - Copy `profile-generator/update-profile.yml` to `.github/workflows/update-profile.yml`. - Put the four markers in your README: ```markdown <!-- BADGES:START --> <!-- BADGES:END --> ... <!-- PROJECTS:START --> <!-- PROJECTS:END --> ``` - Edit `profile-data.json` — set `owner`, keep or change the `markers`, set your `categories`, and curate your repos. Run the workflow once to fill the regions. See [`profile-generator/README.md`](profile-generator/README.md) for the full configuration reference. ### 5. Turn on GitHub Pages (optional) The kit's own landing page lives in `docs/`. To publish something similar: **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Deploy from a branch → `main` / `/docs`**. The `docs/.nojekyll` file tells Pages to serve the files as-is. --- ## Known limitation: the languages panel is empty under `GITHUB_TOKEN` `lowlighter/metrics` works with the default `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`, but its **languages plugin renders empty** because the token is forbidden from reading a field the base query asks for: - metrics' base repositories query requests `stargazers { totalCount }`; - the repository-scoped `GITHUB_TOKEN` is **not permitted** to read that field, and the GraphQL call comes back `FORBIDDEN: Resource not accessible by integration`; - that leaves the repositories data unusable, so `plugin_languages` renders "0 Languages" with a bare, unstyled "Most used languages" link and no chart; - **the action still reports success.** There is no failing step and no red X, so the card simply looks broken with no error to explain why. **The fix:** a **classic personal access token with no scopes**, saved as the secret `METRICS_TOKEN`, is allowed to read `stargazers`. Create one (GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic) → Generate new token (classic); no scopes required for public data), save it as `METRICS_TOKEN`, switch the `token:` input in both render steps to `${{ secrets.METRICS_TOKEN }}`, and re-enable the `plugin_languages*` lines. The steps are spelled out at the foot of `metrics.yml`. **Also worth knowing:** `config_theme` is **not a real metrics option**. It is copied around the web often, but it silently does nothing. There is no built-in light/dark switch — light and dark have to be done with `extras_css` and **two renders**, which is exactly what `metrics.yml` does. --- ## Built with This profile is assembled from other people's work, and it deserves the credit. - **[lowlighter/metrics](https://github.com/lowlighter/metrics)** — the rendering engine behind the stats card. It uses the `classic` template with the `base` (header, activity) and `calendar` plugins, and its `extras_css` option to produce a matched light and dark pair from one configuration. Worth knowing: `config_theme` is not a real option and silently does nothing, despite how often it is copied around — light/dark has to be done with `extras_css` and two renders. - **[avgupta456/github-trends](https://github.com/avgupta456/github-trends)** — the idea of tracking lines of code by language over time, and the pattern of embedding a hosted SVG instead of generating one in the repo. Its embed is parked here until an account is created on their service. - **[rzashakeri/beautify-github-profile](https://github.com/rzashakeri/beautify-github-profile)** — the catalogue this was worked from. The badge vocabulary comes from its Badges section (the shields.io family), and metrics was chosen from its Widgets list; the busier widgets it also lists (typing SVG, profile trophy, contribution snake) were deliberately left out to keep this page quiet. --- <sub>Part of **[All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/)** · built and maintained by [Dr. Sohil Momin](https://github.com/drsamonline)</sub>

Change it, then rebuild the release: ```bash npm install # installs terser (the only dev dependency) npm run build # src/retro-strike.html -> dist/retro-strike.min.html ``` --- ## 📦 Project structure ``` retro-strike/ ├── src/retro-strike.html # 📜 readable, commented source (edit this) ├── dist/retro-strike.min.html # 🎮 minified, playable release (~90 KB) ├── tools/build.mjs # 🔧 minifier (extracts + compresses src -> dist) ├── assets/ # 🎨 banner, logo, social preview, screenshots ├── docs/ # 📚 architecture, controls, performance, audit ├── .github/ # ⚙️ Pages workflow, issue & PR templates ├── package.json # 📦 build script (dev-only) ├── CHANGELOG.md · CONTRIBUTING.md · CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md · SECURITY.md └── LICENSE ``` **Source vs release:** `src/` is the human-readable single file you edit; `dist/` is the same game compressed for shipping. The GitHub Pages workflow publishes `dist/` so the repo is instantly playable online. --- ## 🛠️ Tech Built from scratch with **zero runtime dependencies** — only web-platform APIs: - **Renderer** — a hand-written software rasteriser on **Canvas 2D**: per-face camera-space projection, near-plane clipping and a painter's-algorithm depth sort. Sprites are cached to offscreen canvases and blitted in one `drawImage`. - **Audio** — procedural **chiptune** (bass + arpeggio) and all SFX synthesised live from `OscillatorNode` / noise buffers via the **Web Audio API**. - **World** — a seeded **xorshift PRNG** for reproducible arenas, flood-fill reachability so nothing spawns in a sealed room, and biome quadrants (default / ice / lava). - **Persistence** — settings, stats, achievements, leaderboard, campaign progress, run save and ghost replay in **`localStorage`** (every access guarded). - **Input** — Pointer Lock for mouse aim, multi-touch with a virtual joystick, and the Gamepad API. --- ## ⚡ Performance The game targets a smooth **~60 FPS** on modest hardware and caps its frame rate so high-refresh displays stay cool. | Optimisation | Effect | |---|---| | Precomputed wall/lava cell lists | Minimap no longer rescans the 48×48 grid twice per frame | | Quantised fog-colour cache | Avoids ~700 string builds per frame | | Cached sprite atlases | One `drawImage` per sprite instead of per-pixel fills | | Distance-culled particles/bullets | Fewer short-lived objects and closures per frame | | Hoisted palettes & sort comparators | Removes per-frame allocations | | `dt` clamp + FPS cap | Stable physics on any refresh rate | See [`docs/PERFORMANCE.md`](docs/PERFORMANCE.md) for the measured before/after. --- ## 🚢 Publishing 1. **Create the repo** and push: ```bash git init git add . git commit -m "Initial commit — RETRO STRIKE v1.1.0" git branch -M main git remote add origin https://github.com/drsamonline/retro-strike.git git push -u origin main ``` 2. **Make the badges yours** — find-and-replace every `drsamonline/retro-strike` in `README.md` with your GitHub username and repo name (the banner, star/issue badges and the **▶️ Play** link all use it). 3. **Turn on the live demo** — go to **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: Deploy from a branch**, then pick the `main` branch and the `/docs` folder. Saga

Plain JavaScript · one stylesheet · no build step · works offline

Landing page  ·  Play the game it powers — Aethelgard: The Books  ·  Aethelgard — The Books

---

A small, dependency-free visual-novel engine for the browser.
Plain JavaScript · one stylesheet · no build step · works offline

--- **Saga** is a visual-novel engine that runs from a static file server with nothing installed. It was built to make *Aethelgard — The Books*, and it is released on its own so you can make something else with it. > **The engine is MIT.** It ships no story and no artwork — you bring your own. > The *Aethelgard* games' artwork and story are a separate work, © Dr. Sohil > Momin, all rights reserved — free to play, not open source, and not contained > in this repository. See [Licence](#licence). ## ▶️ See it in action This engine was built to make **Aethelgard — The Books**, a visual novel in three books — 36 chapters and seven endings, all authored in plain `.scene` text files that this engine reads. Play it here: **[drsamonline.github.io/aethelgard-games/play/books/](https://drsamonline.github.io/aethelgard-games/play/books/)** It is one of two games in the *Aethelgard* world; the other is an RPG on a different engine, [drsamonline/Aethelgard-Engine](https://github.com/drsamonline/Aethelgard-Engine). Both live together in **[drsamonline/aethelgard-games](https://github.com/drsamonline/aethelgard-games)**. --- ## Contents - [See it in action](#-see-it-in-action) - [Run the engine](#run-the-engine) - [How to play](#how-to-play) - [Features](#features) - [Project layout](#project-layout) - [Write a chapter](#write-a-chapter) - [Art](#art) - [Mods](#mods) - [Making it yours](#making-it-yours) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [Licence](#licence) --- ## Run the engine The engine ships **code only** — no story, no art. To see it in action, play **[Aethelgard: The Books](https://drsamonline.github.io/aethelgard-games/play/books/)**, which is built on this engine. To build your own, see [Making it yours](#making-it-yours). The engine is served like any static site — it reads its scene files over http, so use a server (opening `index.html` by double-click will not work in most browsers): ```bash python3 -m http.server 8000 # open http://localhost:8000 ``` No install, no build, no dependencies. Any static server works (`npx serve`, nginx, GitHub Pages — anything). ## How to play You read the story and make choices. That's the whole game — but there are a few things worth knowing before your first run. ### Controls | key | action | |---|---| | `Space` / `Enter` | advance dialogue (clicking the stage works too) | | `Tab` + `Enter` | move to a choice and pick it — every option is a real button | | `D` | open the **Diary** (people, places, lore, decisions, deeds) | | `B` | open the **Backlog** — scroll back through everything said | | `S` | save to localStorage (you can also export/import a JSON file) | | `Esc` | close the current panel | Mouse and touch work throughout; the layout is tested from 360×640 up. ### Choices and gates Some options show a requirement like `[Bonds 2]`. If you don't meet it, the option is shown **greyed out with the reason** — never hidden. You should always be able to see what you missed. ### The four axes and the endings Every choice secretly moves one of four counters: **Mercy**, **Truth**, **Bonds** or **Conviction**. They stay hidden while you play and are revealed in the epilogue. The ending is not a score — it is the *shape*: which axis led, and how far the four spread. Seven endings resolve from that shape, from *Dawn* to *Hollow*: | ending | the shape that earns it | |---|---| | Dawn | every axis high — nothing was sacrificed | | The Long Road | mercy carried the run | | The Weight | truth led, and its cost | | Ash | a balanced, ordinary run | | The Crown's Shadow | conviction led, without mercy | | Silence | never committed to anything | | Hollow | refused everything | The resolver lives in `js/endings.js` and is pure data — rewrite it freely. ### Tips - Read the Diary as you go — it fills itself and tells you who matters. - There is no wrong way to play; the seven endings are shapes, not grades. - Reaching the end of a chapter list without an ending still returns you to the title screen safely. ## Features | | | |---|---| | **Dialogue** | per-line speaker, ten expressions, a portrait that changes with the mood of the line | | **Choices** | branching, with stat gates shown greyed-out and their reason visible — never a hidden lock | | **Branches** | `@label` / `@goto`, so a choice can rejoin the main line | | **Four axes** | hidden counters that every choice moves; the ending is their *shape* | | **Seven endings** | resolved from which axis led and how far they spread | | **The Diary** | people, places, lore, decisions and deeds, filled as you play | | **Intro cards** | a character card the first time someone appears | | **Achievements** | declared in the script, unlocked in play | | **Save / export** | localStorage, plus export and import as a JSON file | | **Backlog** | scroll back through everything said | | **Music** | synthesised with Web Audio — no audio files at all | | **Mods** | drop a folder in `mods/`, it is found; five safety rules enforced | | **Mobile** | tested from 360×640 up | | **Accessibility** | full keyboard play, visible focus outlines, dialog semantics, `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured | ## Project layout ``` index.html the page css/style.css the look js/core.js state, save, settings, the four axes js/script.js the scene-script parser js/chars.js the cast and the regions <- YOUR DATA js/graphics.js sprite lookup js/music.js synthesised sound js/play.js the runner: dialogue, choices, diary, cards js/ui.js title, Diary, settings, endings js/mods.js the mod loader and its safety rules js/endings.js the axis shape and the ending resolver js/boot.js wiring scenes/ the story, as plain text <- YOU ADD THIS assets/sprites/ the art <- YOU ADD THIS docs/SCENE-FORMAT.md how to write a chapter ``` Everything marked **YOUR DATA** is meant to be replaced. The engine does not know anything about any particular story. ## Write a chapter A chapter is a plain text file, one instruction per line. Full reference in `docs/SCENE-FORMAT.md`. ``` @title The Demo — Chapter One @bg road @mood uneasy narrate A road at dusk. wanderer neutral "You're the Keeper of the hall, then." keeper warm "I am." choice * "Tell the truth." => truth+1, bonds+1 * [Bonds 2] "Say you knew her mother." => bonds+2, mercy+1 end @label after @mood calm keeper warm "Then come in. It's cold." ``` Then add one line to `scenes/manifest.js` and the chapter appears. ## Art The engine finds a portrait by name: ``` char.. -> _.webp, then .webp bg. -> bg_.webp ``` Ship no art and the game runs text-only — a missing portrait simply hides. The sprites in `assets/sprites/` here are **generated placeholders**, PolyForm Noncommercial-licensed like the engine. Replace them. Rebuild the index after adding art: ```bash python3 tools/make-sprite-index.py assets/sprites ``` ## Mods Drop a folder into `mods/` with a `mod.js`, add a line to `mods/mods.json`, and the engine finds it. Mods can add chapters, cast, regions, achievements, and can also *replace* existing entries. Five safety rules are enforced so a mod can never break a running game: 1. Every load is wrapped in try/catch — a broken mod cannot take the game down. 2. Structural mods apply at boot only, never mid-session. 3. `requiresMods` is honoured. 4. Two mods claiming the same `provides` conflict; the first wins, the second is refused **visibly**. 5. `loadAfter` orders mods deterministically. See `mods/README.md` for the full manifest format and the example mods. ## Making it yours The engine ships **no story**. To make a game you replace three things: | file | what to put in it | |---|---| | `js/chars.js` | your cast, your regions, `G.TITLE`, `G.SLUG`, `G.ACHIEVEMENTS` | | `scenes/` | your chapters, and a `manifest.js` listing them | | `assets/sprites/` | your art | Nothing else needs to change. The engine starts at whatever scene the manifest lists first, so it never needs to know your chapter ids. ## Documentation | document | about | |---|---| | `docs/SCENE-FORMAT.md` | the full scene-script reference | | `mods/README.md` | writing a mod, and the five safety rules | | `assets/sprites/README.md` | the art naming convention | | `CONTRIBUTING.md` | how to send changes to the engine | | `CHANGELOG.md` | release history | ## Contributing Read `CONTRIBUTING.md` first — the engine is meant to stay small, with no build step and no dependencies. Bug fixes, parser features inside the existing format, accessibility work and new mod hook points are all welcome. ## Licence **Two licences, clearly split:** | what | licence | |---|---| | The Saga engine — code, stylesheet, tools | **[PolyForm Noncommercial](LICENSE)** — use it, fork it, ship it | | The *Aethelgard — The Books* game's artwork, story and characters | © Dr. Sohil Momin, **all rights reserved** — free to play, not open source. Not contained in this repository | If you build a game on this engine, your content is yours; the engine stays MIT. ---

Made with plain JavaScript by Dr. Sohil Momin

# Seance

[![live](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-online-22c55e)](https://drsamonline.github.io/seance/)
[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)
[![download](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/seance

**Sealed notes, opened once.** Write a note, seal it with a passphrase, and share
the sealed text. It opens on the reader's device — offline, no account — and the
device remembers that it was opened.

Built with **crypto-kit** (AES-256-GCM) and **web-kit**.

## What it does

- **Seal:** a note + a passphrase → a sealed text (base64) you can paste anywhere.
- **Open:** paste the sealed text + the passphrase → the note.
- Authenticated encryption, so a wrong passphrase or altered text is rejected.
- Share the text and the passphrase **separately** — the text is useless alone.
- Everything happens on your device; nothing is sent anywhere.

## Run it

Open `docs/index.html`. That's the whole app — offline, from `file://` or Pages.
(It needs a **secure context** for Web Crypto: Pages is https, so the live site is
fine; some browsers restrict `file://`.)

## Structure

```
docs/index.html      the app
docs/web-kit.js      the shared runtime (drsamonline/web-kit)
```

## Honest limits

- A passphrase-sealed note is only as strong as the passphrase. Use a strong one.
- "Opened once" is remembered **on this device** — it is a courtesy, not
  enforcement; a determined reader can clear storage or open it elsewhere.
- Not a substitute for a vetted messaging app for anything truly sensitive.

## Licence

# skills

**A machine-consumable knowledge base of the working methods behind the drsamonline projects.**

[![Landing page](https://img.shields.io/badge/landing%20page-open-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/skills/)
[![All projects](https://img.shields.io/badge/All%20projects-hub-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/)
[![Type: knowledge base](https://img.shields.io/badge/type-knowledge%20base-586069?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/skills/)
[![Format: Markdown + JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/format-Markdown%20%2B%20JSON-586069?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/drsamonline/skills)
[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](LICENSE)

**Landing page:** <https://drsamonline.github.io/skills/>  ·  **All projects:** <https://drsamonline.github.io/>


This repository is a **machine-consumable knowledge base**. Each of the
projects under [`drsamonline`](https://github.com/drsamonline) has its working
*method* extracted into a reusable **skill**, so the same approach can be
reused, extended or branched from instead of being rediscovered.

## Conforms to the Agent Skills standard

This repository conforms to the **Agent Skills** standard — see
[agentskills.io/specification](https://agentskills.io/specification). That is a
claim we can make and did not, which is free credibility we had already earned.

Run `python3 validate.py` to check it. The validator enforces the standard's rules
for `name` and `description`, and the folder layout:

- **name** — 1-64 characters; lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens only; no
  leading, trailing or doubled hyphen; and equal to the folder name.
- **description** — 1-1024 characters, present.
- **layout** — a directory holding `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter.

**What the claim does and does not mean.** We conform on the fields the standard
defines for `name` and `description`, and on the layout. We do **not** claim support
for every optional field: where one is unused it is *absent*, not present-and-empty,
which is what the standard allows. Anything more specific than that would be
inventing a compatibility we have not tested.

Non-directory entries are **skipped** rather than failed — this repository holds a
`.gitkeep`, and a validator that calls a placeholder file a broken skill is a
validator people stop running.

There are two kinds of skill:

- **Technique skills** — the cross-cutting methods that recur across many
  projects: the offline-first single-file web app, Android WebView packaging,
  the portable EXE launcher, the shared build/release workflow, the landing-page
  + SEO conventions, the auto-updating showcase hub, the open-data pipeline, the
  LAN single-server architecture, the theme-aware GitHub profile, optical file
  transfer, embedded-bundle feature gating, and safe repository cleanup.
- **Imported first-party skills** — 501 skills from eighteen upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Google, Vercel, Hugging Face, Cloudflare, MiniMax, Addy Osmani, Matt Pocock, Matteo Collina, Jesse Vincent, Emil Kowalski, Steph Ango, Seth Hobson and others), deduplicated by topic and kept under their own licences.
- **Vendored packs** — five packs and the seventeen skills they were merged from, imported unchanged from [ChrisTitusTech/titstack](https://github.com/ChrisTitusTech/titstack) (MIT). Each carries its own `LICENSE`; the pack is the merged reading, the individual skill is the same text on its own.
- **Project skills** — one per repository: what the project is, how it is built,
  how it is released, and what makes its workflow distinctive.

**Catalogue:** `1485` skills across 28 categories. The machine-readable index is [`catalog.json`](catalog.json); the landing page is <https://drsamonline.github.io/skills/>.

## Repository layout

```
README.md                     # this file — human index + how AIs consume the repo
llms.txt                      # short plain-text pointer for AI agents
catalog.json                  # machine-readable index of every skill
skills/<skill-id>/SKILL.md    # the skill itself (YAML front-matter + body)
skills/<skill-id>/meta.json   # machine-readable metadata for that skill
docs/                         # the landing page (its own sub-website)
```

Skill ids are lowercase-hyphenated and stable. Categories are a fixed set:

`web-app-patterns`, `android-packaging`, `windows-desktop`, `game-engine`, `data-and-schema`, `health-tools`, `landing-and-seo`, `ci-and-release`, `marketing`, `docs-and-planning`, `code-quality`, `linux-desktop`, `sysadmin-ops`, `media-design`, `frontend-ui`, `backend-services`, `testing-qa`, `security-audit`, `cloud-and-deploy`, `ai-and-ml`, `office-docs`, `engineering-workflow`, `notes-knowledge`, `mobile-apps`, `browser-automation`, `google-workspace`, `game-dev`, `product-management`.

## The skill format

### `SKILL.md`

YAML front-matter, then a body with five fixed sections.

```markdown
---
name: Human-readable skill name
description: One sentence — what the skill lets you do.
---

# Human-readable skill name

A short introduction.

## When to use
- ...

## Method
1. ...

## Key files / entry points
- ...

## Gotchas
- ...

## Source projects
- [repo](https://github.com/drsamonline/<repo>) — what it demonstrates.
```

### `meta.json`

```json
{
  "id": "lowercase-hyphenated-id",
  "name": "Human-readable skill name",
  "category": "one of the nine categories",
  "description": "One sentence.",
  "tags": ["..."],
  "source_repos": ["RepoName", "..."],
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "updated": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "source_snapshot": { "RepoName": "<latest commit SHA when derived>" },
  "subskills": ["related-skill-id", "..."]
}
```

`source_snapshot` maps each source repository to its latest commit SHA at the
time the skill was derived, so a consumer can tell whether the skill still
matches the code it describes.

## The catalogue

Every skill in the repository, by category, with the one line that tells you whether to open it. The id is the directory: `skills/<id>/SKILL.md` holds the method, `meta.json` its provenance, its licence and its upstream commit. Where a category has an index pack, the pack is named first — it is the routing table for that category.

## How an AI agent should consume this repo

1. Read **`catalog.json`** first — it is the single source of truth. It carries
   `generated`, `count`, `categories[]` and a `skills[]` array whose entries
   mirror each `meta.json`.
2. Pick the skill(s) you need by `id`, `category` or `tags`.
3. Read the matching **`skills/<id>/SKILL.md`** for the actual method.
4. To reuse a project's approach, follow its `source_repos` and, if the skill
   looks stale, compare `source_snapshot` against the repo's current HEAD.

A short pointer file for agents is also provided at [`llms.txt`](llms.txt), and
the same catalogue is rendered for humans at the [landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/skills/).

## Keeping the catalogue current

The catalogue is refreshed by a weekly GitHub Actions workflow,
[`.github/workflows/refresh.yml`](.github/workflows/refresh.yml) (cron +
`workflow_dispatch`, `permissions: contents: write`). It performs the
**mechanical refresh only**: it re-reads the repository list from the GitHub
API, updates each skill's `meta.json` `updated` and `source_snapshot` fields
(and any changed source-repo metadata), regenerates `catalog.json`, and commits
only if something changed.

It does **not** rewrite the skill prose. That split is deliberate:

- **Mechanical refresh (automated)** — SHAs, dates, counts, `catalog.json`.
  Safe to run unattended every week.
- **Prose update (human/AI, separate)** — the `When to use`, `Method`, `Key
  files`, `Gotchas` and `Source projects` text. Rewriting a method from a diff
  is a judgement call, so it is never done by the scheduled workflow.

## Licence & attribution

This repository's text (the skills) is © 2026 Dr. Sohil Momin. The projects it
describes retain their own licences — see each `SKILL.md`'s source links.

The three `marketing` skills (`product-copywriting`, `directory-submissions`,
`free-tool-marketing`) are adapted from
[coreyhaines31/marketingskills](https://github.com/coreyhaines31/marketingskills)
(MIT, © its authors); the shape and the ideas are theirs, the text and the
situation are ours. Their PolyForm Noncommercial licence is retained.

### Vendored third-party skills

The five `pack-*` skills and the seventeen skills they merge are imported from
[ChrisTitusTech/titstack](https://github.com/ChrisTitusTech/titstack) at commit
`b9b7fb0`, under the **MIT** licence (© 2026 titstack contributors). Each of
those directories carries the full MIT text as its own `LICENSE`, and each
`meta.json` records the upstream repo, path and commit. MIT content is
redistributed here with its notice intact; the repository's PolyForm
Noncommercial terms continue to apply to the drsamonline skills around it.

`source_repos` is left empty for those entries on purpose: they describe a
repository that is not part of `drsamonline`, so the weekly refresh workflow
must not try to resolve their commit SHAs. The pin lives in `upstream.commit`
instead, which the refresh does not touch.

### The multi-repo import

501 skills and 10 index packs were imported from eighteen first-party skill
collections in one pass, at the commits recorded in each `meta.json`. The
import is a **deduplicated** one: where two repositories shipped the same topic
the fullest version is kept and the others are listed under *Upstream variants*
inside that skill, so nothing is silently dropped and no two entries claim the
same ground.

Licences are per skill, not per repository — `MIT` for most, `Apache-2.0` for
`google/skills` and `huggingface/skills`, each with its full text in that
directory's `LICENSE`. Two sources (`anthropics/skills`,
`vercel-labs/agent-skills`) publish **no licence file**; their skills are
included at this repository owner's explicit direction and carry a
`LICENSE-NOTICE.md` instead of a grant. Twenty-three skills were mined from the
aggregator collections to fill categories with thin first-party coverage; they
are marked `origin: third-party-aggregator` and their upstream attribution is
incomplete by nature.

`source_repos` is empty for every imported entry on purpose — the weekly refresh
workflow resolves SHAs against the `drsamonline` repo list, so a foreign repo
name there would be dropped on the next run. The pin lives in
`upstream.repo/path/commit`.

### The third import

1,013 more first-party skills from 45 repositories, deduplicated against everything
already here: 21 topics already had a fuller version in the catalogue, so the new
copy was recorded under *Upstream variants* instead of adding a second entry, and 6
existing entries were replaced because the new source was substantially fuller.
Four categories were added (`browser-automation`, `google-workspace`, `game-dev`,
`product-management`) and every index pack was regenerated, so a pack now covers
all members of its category rather than the batch it was born with.

Five listed repositories contributed nothing: `NeoLabHQ/sadd`, `NeoLabHQ/kaizen`,
`baskduf/codex-fable5`, `oliverb-io1902e8/agent-skills-collection` and
`testmu-ai/api-skill` do not exist at those URLs, and `agentskills/agentskills`
carries no `SKILL.md`. Four more are aggregators (`davila7/claude-code-templates`,
`ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills`, `alirezarezvani/claude-skills`,
`foryourhealth111-pixel/Vibe-Skills`); they were read for overlap but not bulk
imported.

New categories are listed compactly in this README: at this size the descriptions
belong in the pack tables and `catalog.json`, not in 1,000 more README rows.

### Pruning

The catalogue is not a mirror. After the imports it was cut back to what does
real work:

- **142 skills removed.** The four Anthropic office skills that reserve
  all rights (`docx`, `pdf`, `pptx`, `xlsx`); a placeholder template; two alias
  stubs that only pointed at another skill; and the product-internal CLI wrappers
  with no reusable method (`ctx-*`, `caveman-stats`, `caveman-compress`,
  `remotion-render`).
- **124 thin families merged into 12 skills.** The 81
  `nexu-io/html-anything` style specs (median body 266 bytes) became five style
  libraries grouped by what you are producing: deck, web page, dashboard, visual
  card, document. The 45 `googleworkspace/cli` `recipe-*` skills became six
  grouped recipe sets by service. The two `grilling` aliases folded into
  `grilling`. Every original id survives as a heading inside its merged skill, so
  nothing was lost, only indexed.

Everything kept is substantive: the median body across the catalogue is several
kilobytes, and each skill states a trigger, a method and the traps it hit.

A private, offline browser app for tracking a skin case over time — History, Habits, Mapping and Symptoms, logged day by day and read as a 90-day pattern.
The companion app to the book The Skin Is a Liar by Dr. Sohil Momin. It records; it does not diagnose.
