No install needed — it runs in the browser and installs as an offline app.

--- ## ✨ What it is A working implementation of the **HHMS dashboard** described in _The Skin Is a Liar_ (chapters 11 and 14). HHMS stands for the four fields it records — **History, Habits, Mapping, Symptoms**. The book's claim is that the skin is the body's readout, and that a skin case should be tracked over time and read as a *pattern*, not treated as a snapshot. This is that tracking instrument. > **It records; it does not diagnose.** Nothing here is medical advice. The reading of the pattern > is the clinician's job. All data stays on your device. ## 🚀 Quick start | | | |---|---| | 🌐 **Use it now** | Open **https://drsamonline.github.io/skin-case-tracker/play/** | | 📲 **Install it** | Open the link, then use your browser's **Install** option (⊕ in the address bar, or *Add to Home screen*). It then works fully offline. | | 🧪 **Try sample data** | Press **Load demo case** on the Cases tab, or open the link with `#demo` on the end. | | 💾 **Run it locally** | Download the repo and open `index.html` — it is one self-contained file. | ## 🩺 What it does - **Records** the four HHMS fields — one entry a day (skin severity, the day's habits, and five symptom groups), plus a flare log with the 48-hour food, cycle, stress and sleep. - **Maps** the eruption on a body map (*present · has been · migrated*) and attaches photographs. - **Connects** the skin against each symptom group, day by day, and scores the **seven organ-skin axes** from the book's signatures. - **Reads** the pattern — a skin-vs-symptoms chart, a lead/lag view, a **colour-blind-safe** correlation heat-map, baseline-vs-current, and a plain-language conclusion. - **Audits** at **30 / 60 / 90 days**, and exports the trail as JSON (the full backup, *including photos*), CSV, a pooled research CSV, the photos as a ZIP, or a printable report. ## 🧭 The four fields | Field | What it captures | |---|---| | **History** | The narrative, and the audit of the suppression — eruptions "cured" before an internal complaint, with the latency | | **Habits** | Stress, cold drinks, alcohol, sleep, heavy food, menstruation, medications, vaccination | | **Mapping** | Where the eruption is, where it has been, where it has migrated — plus photos | | **Symptoms** | Cardiac · Respiratory · Digestive · Neurological · Gynaecological, scored 0–10 | ## 🔒 Privacy Everything is stored in your own browser (`localStorage`). **Nothing is sent anywhere.** There is no account, no server, and no tracking. Export at any time and import the JSON back on the same or another device. ## 📦 Exports | Export | Contains | |---|---| | **JSON** (case / all cases) | The complete backup — history, logs, flares, reviews, body map **and photos** | | **Daily log CSV** | The numeric day-by-day table (image-free) | | **Pooled research CSV** | One summary row per case, for pooling across cases | | **Photos ZIP** | The images as files, plus a `manifest.csv` | | **Photo list CSV** | `case, date, note, filename, bytes` | | **Codebook (.md)** | The full field dictionary | | **Print / PDF** | A one-page clinician report | ## ⚠️ Not medical advice This app records information; it does not diagnose and gives no medical advice. The axis scores are a transparent, rule-based reading of your own log. If a symptom worries you, see a doctor; in an emergency, seek emergency care. ## 📜 Licence **Free to use — for personal and clinical use — but copyrighted.** Copyright © 2026 Dr. Sohil Momin. **All rights reserved.** You may use it free of charge for personal and clinical purposes. # web-kit

[![test](https://github.com/drsamonline/web-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/web-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml)


**The shared offline-first runtime for drsamonline apps.** One file, no build
step, no CDN. Works from `file://` and from GitHub Pages.

Every single-file app was re-implementing the same things — storage, languages,
CSV export, theming, SEO. This is that code, once.

## Use it

Drop `web-kit.js` next to your `index.html` and include it:

```html
<script src="web-kit.js"></script>
<script>
  Loom.theme.apply();            // light/dark from the system, remembered
  Loom.storage.set("count", 1);  // namespaced, JSON-safe
  document.body.textContent = Loom.i18n.t("app_ready");
</script>
```

For a truly single-file app, inline the contents of `web-kit.js` in a `<script>`
block. Nothing else is required.

## What's in it

| API | Does |
|---|---|
| `Loom.storage` | `get/set/remove/clear` on localStorage (namespaced), plus a small IndexedDB wrapper (`put/getItem/all`) for larger data. |
| `Loom.i18n` | `t(key)`, `setLang`, `langs`, `extend` — English, Hindi and Gujarati built in. |
| `Loom.csv` | `toCSV(rows)`, `fromCSV(text)`, `download(name, text)`. |
| `Loom.theme` | `apply`, `set`, `toggle` — light/dark tokens as CSS variables. |
| `Loom.a11y` | `trapFocus(el)`, `announce(msg)`. |
| `Loom.pwa` | `register(sw)`, `themeColor(color)`. |
| `Loom.seo` | `title`, `description`, `jsonld`. |
| `Loom.ui` | `el(tag, props, children)` — a tiny DOM helper. |

## Conventions it follows

- **Offline-first:** no network calls, no CDN, no telemetry.
- **No accounts:** all data stays on the device.
- **Small:** one dependency-free file you can read in one sitting.

## Demo and tests

- `demo/index.html` — a working mini-app (counter, theme toggle, language
  switch, CSV export).
- `test/index.html` — a tiny assertion page; open it and check the console.

# Weft-8 Classroom ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Nine exercises that teach how a computer actually works — on a real one.** [![Live exercises](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-the%20exercises-e8d48b?style=flat-square&labelColor=1c2b24)](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-classroom/) [![Test](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/weft8-classroom/test.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=tests&labelColor=1c2b24)](https://github.com/drsamonline/weft8-classroom/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![Build + deploy](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/weft8-classroom/build-apps.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=build&labelColor=1c2b24)](https://github.com/drsamonline/weft8-classroom/actions/workflows/build-apps.yml) [![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-9fe0a8?style=flat-square&labelColor=1c2b24)](LICENSE) [![Built on the Loom](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20on-the%20Loom%20(app--jacquard)-e8d48b?style=flat-square&labelColor=1c2b24)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) [![For classrooms](https://img.shields.io/badge/classrooms-free%20to%20use-9fe0a8?style=flat-square&labelColor=1c2b24)](#for-teachers) [**Open the exercises →**](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-classroom/) · [Teacher's sheet](TEACHER.md)
![The exercises](docs/shot.png) A first lesson in how computers work, built on the **Weft-8** — the 8-bit machine from [Jacquard, the Loom](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard). Sixteen registers, four flags, twenty-seven instructions, and **no `if` statement**, so the student builds one. Every exercise starts **incomplete**. The machine runs, does something, and the class can see exactly what is missing — then the check names the register and the value that was expected. ## The nine exercises | # | Exercise | What it teaches | |---|---|---| | 1 | Put a number somewhere | `LDI` fills the accumulator, `MOV` moves it | | 2 | Add two numbers | what `ADD Ra, Rb` really means | | 3 | Double a number | `SHL` is multiply-by-two | | 4 | Count to ten | a loop needs a counter, a decrement and a branch | | 5 | Remember something | `STORE` and `LOAD` reach RAM at `0x80` | | 6 | Call a subroutine | `CALL` pushes, `RET` pops — and the code after the call proves you came back | | 7 | Decide something | `CMP` sets the flags, `JZ` branches: your first `if` | | 8 | Say something out loud | `OUT` hands a byte to a port | | 9 | Swap two registers | why a swap needs a third register — and why "just copy it" loses a value | ## For teachers [`TEACHER.md`](TEACHER.md) has the lesson plan, the answers in words, three things worth saying out loud, and a table of common mistakes with what they look like on screen and what to ask the student. Two properties make it usable in a real classroom: - **Offline, one file, no accounts.** A room with no internet and a decade-old laptop can run the whole lesson. There is nothing to install. - **No partial credit.** The machine has no partial answers, so a tick means the program is right — not that it looks right. ## Built on the Loom `docs/play/weft8.js` is the **Weft-8** from [app-jacquard](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard), byte for byte the same engine. A student who finishes these eight can open Jacquard, or the puzzle set in `app-weft-puzzles`, and it is the same computer. ## Test it ``` npm install node test-node.js # 72 assertions — the machine, every exercise, and the checks node tests/page-smoke.js # 10 assertions — the page, driven in jsdom ``` The suite asserts the three things a teaching pack must be able to promise: 1. **every exercise is solvable** — the shipped answer passes its own checks, on the real machine 2. **every starter is genuinely incomplete** — it must *fail*, or there is nothing to teach 3. **the checks bite** — subtracting instead of adding, forgetting to `LOAD` back, ending a subroutine with `HLT` instead of `RET`, and writing one byte when two were asked for are all caught, each with the message a teacher would give ## The Weft-8 family One machine, seven faces. Every one of these runs `weft8.js` from the Loom, byte for byte — learn it once and you have learned all seven. | | what it is | |---|---| | [the Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/) | the machine and its editor — where it all starts | | [Weft Puzzles](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-weft-puzzles/) | five puzzles solved in assembly, a robot on a grid | | [Clip Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-clip-loom/) | clipboard programs you can read: strip, squeeze, wrap | | [Weft-8 on hardware](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-hardware/) | the same machine in C, three-way parity with the JS one | | [weft8-kit](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-kit/) | rules small enough to sign off | | **Weft-8 Classroom** (you are here) | eight exercises that teach how a computer works | | [Weft-8 beside x86 and ARM](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-compare/) | the same four jobs in three machines | ## Licence **PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0** · © 2026 Dr Sohil Momin. Free for any noncommercial purpose, including classrooms; commercial use needs a licence from the author.

# Weft-8 beside x86 and ARM ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Which part is the computer, and which part is the language?** [![Live columns](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-three%20columns-2f6f4f?style=flat-square&labelColor=1e1f1c)](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-compare/) [![Test](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/weft8-compare/test.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=tests&labelColor=1e1f1c)](https://github.com/drsamonline/weft8-compare/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![Build + deploy](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/weft8-compare/build-apps.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=build&labelColor=1e1f1c)](https://github.com/drsamonline/weft8-compare/actions/workflows/build-apps.yml) [![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-8c4a3b?style=flat-square&labelColor=1e1f1c)](LICENSE) [![Built on the Loom](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20on-the%20Loom%20(app--jacquard)-2f5a8c?style=flat-square&labelColor=1e1f1c)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) [**Open the three columns →**](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-compare/)
![Three columns](docs/shot.png) Five small jobs, written three times: for the **Weft-8** (the Loom's 8-bit machine), for **x86-64**, and for **AArch64**. Put them side by side and the answer to "what is a computer, really?" stops being abstract — load, add, compare, branch, store. Everything else is naming. ## The five jobs | Job | What it shows | |---|---| | **Add two numbers** | the Weft-8 must move a literal into a register first; the other two add one straight in | | **Sum 1 to 5** | x86 does it in two instructions, ARM in one, the Weft-8 in three — `SUB` sets flags but cannot branch | | **The greater of two** | a compare, a conditional branch, two paths that converge. Identical shape on all three | | **Remember, then recall** | the Weft-8 addresses memory with a literal byte; x86 and ARM compute an address from a frame or stack pointer | | **Multiply by four** | two shifts here, one wide instruction there — the same idea in a wider instruction | ## Honest about the columns The **Weft-8 column is executable**. The page runs it on the real machine, shows the registers afterwards, and the test suite asserts the result of every one of the four jobs. The **x86-64 and AArch64 columns are hand-written illustrations** — short, accurate in shape, and labelled as illustrations in the page and in the data. They are not compiler output, and they do not claim to be. A listing that pretends to be compiled when it was typed by hand would be exactly the sort of thing this whole estate exists to avoid. ## Built on the Loom The Weft-8 column is `docs/play/weft8.js` from [Jacquard (the Loom)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) — byte for byte the same engine, the same one its 102 assertions cover. ## Run it Open `docs/index.html`, or the [live columns](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-compare/). ## Test it ``` npm install node test-node.js # 65 assertions — the four jobs and the honesty of the columns node tests/page-smoke.js # 9 assertions — the page, driven in jsdom ``` The suite asserts that every Weft-8 listing assembles, halts, fits the 128-byte ROM and leaves the expected register or memory value; that every job says what it is, what the machines share and what actually differs; and that **both illustration columns say they are illustrations** and contain real mnemonics rather than a comment pretending to be code. ## The Weft-8 family One machine, seven faces. Every one of these runs `weft8.js` from the Loom, byte for byte — learn it once and you have learned all seven. | | what it is | |---|---| | [the Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/) | the machine and its editor — where it all starts | | [Weft Puzzles](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-weft-puzzles/) | five puzzles solved in assembly, a robot on a grid | | [Clip Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-clip-loom/) | clipboard programs you can read: strip, squeeze, wrap | | [Weft-8 on hardware](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-hardware/) | the same machine in C, three-way parity with the JS one | | [weft8-kit](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-kit/) | rules small enough to sign off | | [Weft-8 Classroom](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-classroom/) | eight exercises that teach how a computer works | | **Weft-8 beside x86 and ARM** (you are here) | the same four jobs in three machines | ## Licence **PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0** · © 2026 Dr Sohil Momin. # Weft-8 on hardware ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **The Loom's 8-bit machine, in C — and a bench that proves it is the same machine.** [![Live bench](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-the%20parity%20bench-6ee7a0?style=flat-square&labelColor=0b1f14)](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-hardware/) [![Test](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/weft8-hardware/test.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=tests&labelColor=0b1f14)](https://github.com/drsamonline/weft8-hardware/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![Build + deploy](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/weft8-hardware/build-apps.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=build&labelColor=0b1f14)](https://github.com/drsamonline/weft8-hardware/actions/workflows/build-apps.yml) [![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-c98b4b?style=flat-square&labelColor=0b1f14)](LICENSE) [![Built on the Loom](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20on-the%20Loom%20(app--jacquard)-c98b4b?style=flat-square&labelColor=0b1f14)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) [**Open the parity bench →**](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-hardware/)
![The parity bench](docs/shot.png) A machine described in one language can hide a mistake inside that language's habits. So the Weft-8 — the 8-bit computer from [Jacquard, the Loom](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) — is written here a second time, in about 180 lines of C, and the two implementations are held against an answer neither of them produced: **eleven programs whose results were worked out by hand from the instruction set**. | | | |---|---| | `c/weft8.c`, `c/weft8.h` | the machine: 16 registers, Z/C/N/V, 256 bytes, 27 two-byte opcodes | | `c/main.c` | runs the corpus, prints one JSON object per program | | `corpus.json` | eleven programs and the results they must produce — **hand-computed** | | `tools/gen-corpus.mjs` | assembles the corpus with the Loom's own assembler into `c/corpus.h` | | `tools/sync-demo.mjs` | writes `docs/play/corpus.js` for the page, from the same `corpus.json` | | `tools/parity.mjs` | three-way comparison: hand-computed vs C vs JavaScript | | `docs/play/` | the bench: the same corpus, run live in your browser | ## The three that must agree 1. **the hand-computed expectation** — worked out from the ISA, not recorded from either machine 2. **the C machine** — `gcc -O2`, run over the corpus in CI on every push 3. **the Loom's JavaScript machine** — `docs/play/weft8.js`, byte for byte the engine every Weft app runs If any of the three drifts, the build goes red. That is the whole design. ## What the corpus proves | program | claim | |---|---| | `add` | 5 + 7 lands in a register with no flags raised | | `borrow` | 2 − 5 wraps to `0xFD` and sets carry and negative | | `overflow` | 127 + 1 sets overflow — what makes signed branches correct | | `countdown` | a counted loop runs exactly five times | | `signed` | −1 is less than 1, though 255 is greater | | `stack` | PUSH/POP return values in reverse order | | `callret` | CALL and RET come back to the right place | | `ram` | STORE then LOAD round-trips through scratch RAM | | `shift` | SHL moves the top bit into carry | | `ports` | two bytes written to a port arrive in order | | `signed-cmp` | −2 is less than −1, so a signed branch works on negatives | ## Run it ``` node tools/gen-corpus.mjs # assemble corpus.json -> c/corpus.h gcc -O2 -o weft8-corpus c/weft8.c c/main.c ./weft8-corpus # eleven JSON lines node tools/parity.mjs ./weft8-corpus # the three-way check node test-node.js # 96 assertions about the corpus, the C and the page ``` On a microcontroller the same `weft8.c` is the machine, and the peripherals become real pins: a port write can drive an LED or read a button. That step is not shipped here yet — an ESP32 sketch that has never been compiled would be a claim, not a proof, and this repository is about proofs. **Honest note.** This repository's own sandbox had no C compiler, so the C is compiled and checked by CI on every push, not locally. `test-node.js` covers everything that can be checked without a compiler: that the corpus is well-formed and unique, that the JavaScript machine reproduces every hand-computed result, that the C source implements all 27 opcodes and carries the same guards, and that `c/corpus.h` carries the exact bytes of every program. ## The Weft-8 family One machine, seven faces. Every one of these runs `weft8.js` from the Loom, byte for byte — learn it once and you have learned all seven. | | what it is | |---|---| | [the Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/) | the machine and its editor — where it all starts | | [Weft Puzzles](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-weft-puzzles/) | five puzzles solved in assembly, a robot on a grid | | [Clip Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-clip-loom/) | clipboard programs you can read: strip, squeeze, wrap | | **Weft-8 on hardware** (you are here) | the same machine in C, three-way parity with the JS one | | [weft8-kit](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-kit/) | rules small enough to sign off | | [Weft-8 Classroom](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-classroom/) | eight exercises that teach how a computer works | | [Weft-8 beside x86 and ARM](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-compare/) | the same four jobs in three machines | ## Licence **PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0** · © 2026 Dr Sohil Momin. # weft8-kit ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **A rule engine small enough to sign off.** [![Live bench](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-the%20rule%20bench-5c7a55?style=flat-square&labelColor=22261d)](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-kit/) [![Test](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/weft8-kit/test.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=tests&labelColor=22261d)](https://github.com/drsamonline/weft8-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![Build + deploy](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/weft8-kit/build-apps.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=build&labelColor=22261d)](https://github.com/drsamonline/weft8-kit/actions/workflows/build-apps.yml) [![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-8c3b2e?style=flat-square&labelColor=22261d)](LICENSE) [![Built on the Loom](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20on-the%20Loom%20(app--jacquard)-8c3b2e?style=flat-square&labelColor=22261d)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) [![Dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime%20deps-0-5c7a55?style=flat-square&labelColor=22261d)](package.json) [**Open the rule bench →**](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-kit/)
![The rule bench](docs/shot.png) A rule is a **Weft-8 program with a contract**: the caller puts inputs in the ports, the rule writes one byte to the verdict port, and everything else is the machine's business. ``` IN0 0xD0 IN1 0xD1 IN2 0xD2 IN3 0xD3 the inputs, 0-255 VERDICT 0xD7 0 pass · 1 flag · 2 stop ``` That is the whole interface. The same in the browser, in a test, and in any app that adopts the kit. ## Why a rule engine at all Three properties a rules engine in a general-purpose language struggles to promise: - **Readable** — a rule is twenty lines you can read aloud. No callbacks, no hidden state, no library deciding what "and" means. - **Bounded** — 27 opcodes, none of which touch a file, a network or a page, and a step limit. A runaway rule stops and says so. - **Provable** — every rule ships its cases and the test suite runs them on the real machine, including a case where the comparison is deliberately flipped to prove the test bites. ## The five example rules | Rule | Question | What it shows | |---|---|---| | `record-complete` | are both fields filled in? | two inputs, one comparison each — the smallest possible rule | | `follow-up-due` | has it been longer than the agreed interval? | a threshold that is an **input**, not a number baked into code | | `two-red-flags` | two or more flags, and severity ≥ 7? | what an "and" costs when the machine has no `and` branch | | `ceiling` | is the value above the ceiling you set? | the pattern a dose or budget check uses | | `two-of-three` | are two of the three fields present? | counting is not an instruction — you add one per input and compare | > These are **examples of the pattern, not clinical guidance.** The numbers in them are illustrations. ## Built on the Loom `docs/play/weft8.js` is the **Weft-8** from [Jacquard (the Loom)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) — byte for byte the same engine, the same one its 102 assertions cover. This kit adds one file on top: `rules.js`, the port contract and the rule set. ## Adopt it Copy two files into your app: ```html ``` `Rules.evaluate(rule, values)` returns `{ verdict, word, steps, halted, error, bytes }` and never throws on a bad rule — a rule that does not assemble comes back with `errors`. ## Test it ``` npm install node test-node.js # 99 assertions — the machine, every rule case, and the guarantees node tests/page-smoke.js # 9 assertions — the bench, driven in jsdom ``` The suite asserts every rule's own cases, that a runaway rule writes **no** verdict and stops at the step limit, that **no opcode reaches the network, the filesystem or the DOM** (the opcode list *is* the permission list), and that flipping a comparison or deleting a check makes the matching case fail. ## The limits, stated - The machine compares **signed** bytes, so an input above 127 reads as negative. The `ceiling` rule says so in its own words, and a test pins that behaviour rather than hiding it. - Four rules is a demonstration, not a library of clinical logic. Adopting the kit means writing and checking your own. ## The Weft-8 family One machine, seven faces. Every one of these runs `weft8.js` from the Loom, byte for byte — learn it once and you have learned all seven. | | what it is | |---|---| | [the Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/) | the machine and its editor — where it all starts | | [Weft Puzzles](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-weft-puzzles/) | five puzzles solved in assembly, a robot on a grid | | [Clip Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-clip-loom/) | clipboard programs you can read: strip, squeeze, wrap | | [Weft-8 on hardware](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-hardware/) | the same machine in C, three-way parity with the JS one | | **weft8-kit** (you are here) | rules small enough to sign off | | [Weft-8 Classroom](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-classroom/) | eight exercises that teach how a computer works | | [Weft-8 beside x86 and ARM](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-compare/) | the same four jobs in three machines | ## Licence **PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0** · © 2026 Dr Sohil Momin. # ziptastic

[![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-MIT-3f7a52

The native engine of **CHCE** (Chimera Hybrid Compression Engine): one
self-contained binary that composes preprocessors, a dual-resolution match
finder, a joint optimal parser and per-block entropy backends into a single
stream format. No external processes, no network, no model files.

**Status: Phase 5b done.** A source review (`docs/SOURCES_REVIEW.md`) turned up
the x86 BCJ filter already vendored and already linked; applying it as a Layer 0
transform takes the corpus to 54,243,754 bytes (+11.17% vs `xz -9`, from
+11.94%), and `ooffice` to −4.06% against `xz -9` — the first file to beat the
baseline.

**Phase 5, for the record:** Three entropy models are offered per block and the
smallest wins: static rANS, chunked adaptive rANS, and a range-coded model that
adapts after every bit. The corpus drops from 57,930,807 to 54,619,596 bytes
(-5.72%), and the gap to `xz -9` from +18.72% to +11.94%. The chunked rANS
model alone gained only 0.087% — the range coder is where the phase's win
actually came from, because it is FIFO and rANS is not.

**Phase 4, for the record:** The parse is now coded with context-modelled
rANS: Silesia lands at 57.9 MB against `xz -9`'s 48.8 MB (+18.7%), down from
+84% when the parse had no coder at all. Decode speed is 26–70 MB/s, short of
the 150 MB/s target — that needs interleaved streams (Phase 12).

**Phase 3, for the record:** The optimal parser works and
round-trips all 12 Silesia files bit-exactly, but the phase's ratio gate is
**not met**: the parse path stores literals as raw bytes (no entropy coder
until Phase 4), so it lands 84% larger than `xz -9` rather than within 5%.
The stream you actually get on disk is still never worse than `xz -9`, because
the Tier-1 LZMA2 fallback wins whenever the parse path is larger. See
`docs/BENCHMARKS.md` for the measurements and the reasoning. Every input is also encoded as raw LZMA2 and the smaller
stream wins, so output is never worse than `xz -9` (measured: −0.73% over the
whole Silesia corpus, every file individually smaller). The CHCE-native
backends that are meant to win by more start at Phase 4.

## What it is meant to do

1. Beat `xz -9` by **≥3%** on Deflate-heavy archives (ZIP, PDF, PNG, nightly
   builds).
2. **Never be worse than `xz -9`** by more than 0.5% on any input, guaranteed
   by a per-block LZMA2 fallback.
3. With `--max-ratio`, approach the `paq8px` ratio class on general data.

The differentiator is not a new compressor. It is the composition: one parser
pricing fine matches, coarse (long-range) matches and semantic tokens with one
cost model, a per-block mode selector that re-optimises the parse for the mode
it picked, and a hard LZMA2 fallback under all of it.

## Build

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build -j
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```

Requirements: CMake ≥ 3.20 and a C++20 compiler. Nothing else — liblzma is
built from the vendored xz sources by the same CMake run, and the test suite
brings its own harness, so there is no gtest to fetch and nothing to install.

## Use

```bash
ziptastic -9 corpus/archive.zip > archive.chce   # compress
ziptastic -d archive.chce archive.zip            # decompress
cat file | ziptastic | ziptastic -d              # pipe
ziptastic bench corpus/                          # ratio + speed table
ziptastic --help
```

| option | meaning |
|---|---|
| `-9` | maximum effort preset (no CM backend) |
| `--no-lzma2` | disable the LZMA2 fallback (removes the Tier-1 guarantee) |
| `--no-parse` | disable the optimal parse (RAW blocks only) |
| `--max-ratio` | allow the CM backend — slowest, smallest (Phase 10) |
| `-b N` | block size in KiB (default 256) |
| `-o FILE` | output file |
| `-f` | overwrite an existing output |
| `-v` | per-run statistics on stderr |

## Phase plan

Phases run in order and each one's exit tests must pass before the next
begins. See `prompt` (the build instructions) and `docs/BENCHMARKS.md` for
measured results.

| Phase | Deliverable | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | CMake skeleton, CLI, RAW blocks, header validation | **done** |
| 1 | LZMA2 fallback — the "never worse than xz" guarantee | **done** |
| 2 | Fine (binary-tree) match finder | **done** |
| 3 | Joint optimal parser | **done, ratio gate not met** |
| 4 | Context-modelled rANS backend | **done** (ratio pass, speed gate not met) |
| 5 | Adaptive frequency tables | **done** (via range coder) — corpus -5.72% |
| 5b | x86 BCJ transform | **done** — ooffice now beats `xz -9` |
| 6 | Coarse (SREP-style) long-range index | next |
| 7 | Static + adaptive Huffman | |
| 8 | Semantic precompression (Preflate) | |
| 9 | BWT, Brotli, Zstd, LZ4 backends | |
| 10 | CM backend (`--max-ratio`) | |
| 11 | PPMd backend | |
| 12 | Speed/ratio optimisation | |

## Layout

```
include/chimera/   public headers (format, block, …)
src/engine/        compressor, decompressor, block writer, (later) match
                   finder, parser, mode selector
src/codecs/        thin wrappers around vendored codecs (liblzma so far)
src/entropy/       rANS and Huffman backends
src/precompressors/ DEFLATE / text / numeric pre-filters
src/dedup/         coarse block-hash index
tests/             unit, integration, benchmark, fixtures
docs/              FORMAT.md (bitstream spec), BENCHMARKS.md (results log)
vendor/hcs/        vendored upstream sources — read-only
```

`vendor/hcs/` is a mirror and is never modified. Anything that needs a change
gets a wrapper under `src/`.

## License

MIT — see `LICENSE`. Only permissively licensed sources are ever linked in;
GPL/LGPL tools (paq8px, upx, advancecomp, packJPG, lzo) are excluded from this
repository entirely.
